prerequisites: renunciation of intention (6.2); self-control; moderation (6.16–17)
signs_of_progress: the mind steady like a lamp in a windless place (6.19); contentment in the self and happiness beyond the senses (6.20–21); the happiness of contact with Brahman (6.28); seeing the self in all and all in the self (6.29)

warnings.text: Yoga is not for one who eats too much or not at all, sleeps too much or too little.
The mind is restless; it is restrained by practice and dispassion.

name: Initiation (dīkṣā) in the Kaula way
method_summary: After mutual testing, the guru initiates by touch, sight or piercing; Śākta initiation is held the highest (Kulārṇava 12.12; 14.53-66).
prerequisites: testing of the disciple for a year, six months or three

warnings.text: Guru and disciple who give and receive without mutual testing both become piśācas.
For the capable the observances remain binding; knowingly breaking them is a great fault.

alt_method_summary: Before a Soma sacrifice the sacrificer is consecrated in a hut with vows of fasting and restraint; the priests make him an embryo again (AB 1.3); he is born anew at the final bath.

The guru, after preliminary purifications and worship of the deity on a maṇḍala and in the fire, performs on the disciple a rite that acts on the soul (not caste or body): in the Śaiva form it binds the disciple to the observances (samaya-dīkṣā) and, in the liberating initiation (nirvāṇa-dīkṣā), purifies the six paths and destroys the bonds through mantra-power; consecrations of sādhaka and ācārya may follow. Pāñcarātra initiation admits to Bhagavān's mantras and worship.

The guru, having become Śiva by ritual identification, removes or burns the disciple's bonds by mantra-power (Sanskrit manuals), or initiates by look, touch, word, thought, scripture, yoga or fire (Tamil).

name: Initiation (dīkṣā) into Hari's worship
method_summary: The ācārya initiates a qualified devotee who has undergone the saṃskāras: the disciple sips the Lord's foot-water, receives mantra and vows, and thereafter worships; the Kṛṣṇāmṛtamahārṇava calls those without Hari's initiation 'beasts among men'.
prerequisites: devotion
saṃskāras
a qualified ācārya
notes: Ritual particulars (maṇḍala, fasting days) deliberately summarized, not listed.

name: Consecration of the sacrificer (dīkṣā)
method_summary: The consecration before the soma rite: the sacrificer is shaved, bathed, clothed anew, restricted in food and speech and kept apart, and so 'reborn' fit for the gods; 'here I go from untruth to truth' (VS 1.5) is the vow-taker's formula.

warnings.text: The dietary restrictions of the consecration are ritual observances within the rite; they are not recorded here in detail.

name: Initiation (dīkṣā) in the Trika
method_summary: Initiation in its many forms - samaya, putraka, abbreviated, by the balance, of the absent and the dead - purifying the paths (adhvan) and removing the bonds; the teacher observes signs of immersion in the disciple (ānanda, udbhava, kampa, nidrā, ghūrṇi; MVT 11.35). For one who knows the Heart, initiation needs no oblation (Parātrīśikā 25).

name: Daily routine (dinacaryā)
method_summary: Rise at the brāhma muhūrta (before dawn) to protect life; attend to the body and cleanliness; clean the teeth with a twig suited to season and doṣa; apply collyrium to the eyes; nasal oil, gargling and (for some) medicated smoke; daily oil-massage, especially of head, ears and feet; exercise to half one's strength; bathing; clean clothes, fragrance; eat in measure when the previous meal is digested; follow good conduct through the day; at night, after a watch has passed, sleep remembering the gods, sages and teachers.

warnings.text: Tooth-twig, massage and bathing each have conditions in which they are to be avoided (indigestion, fever, eye and ear disease, kapha affliction, just after purification).

signs_of_progress: life, health, power and fame (AHS Sū 2.49)

name: Pilgrimage to the divine sites and maṅgaḷāśāsana
method_summary: Lineage contribution (Āḻvārs): the Āḻvārs travelled to the Lord's temples and sang each one — Tirumaṅkai some eighty — longing to be born even as a fish or a step at Tiruvēṅkaṭam, seeing the Lord at Śrīraṅgam from feet to face, calling the reclining Lord at Kuṭantai to rise and speak; the sites they sang became the 108 divya-deśas.
alt_method_summary: Visiting the temples sung by the Āḻvārs and praying for the Lord's welfare there, as the Āḻvārs and teachers did.

name: Recitation of the Divya Prabandham
method_summary: Recitation of the Āḻvārs' hymns in temples and homes — daily selections (nityānusandhānam), the annual festival of recitation (adhyayana-utsava) and the sung and enacted araiyar service — as the Tamil Veda.

name: Seeing the faults (doṣa-darśana)
method_summary: Reflecting on the faults in acquiring, guarding and losing objects, in attachment, and in the harm enjoyment does to beings, so that passion subsides; passion is not quieted by enjoyment but by seeing the faults of both.

warnings.text: Abstaining from objects for these faults is only a contentment, not liberation, without knowledge of the principles.

name: Discrimination of seer and seen (dṛg-dṛśya-viveka)
method_summary: Tracing the chain of seer and seen — object seen by eye, eye by mind, mind by witness — to the seer that is never seen.

name: Shunning bad company (duḥsaṅga-tyāga)
method_summary: Avoiding in every way the company that breeds desire, anger, delusion, loss of memory and of understanding and utter ruin — small ripples that become an ocean through association (NBS 43–45); likewise not listening to talk of lust, wealth, unbelievers and enemies (NBS 63).

name: The bull-sound (ḍuṇḍuṅkāra / huḍukkāra)
method_summary: A holy sound like a bull's bellow produced by touching the tongue-tip to the palate, made as part of the offering.

name: The autumn worship of Durgā (Bengal)
method_summary: The great autumn worship of Durgā with her children, including the worship of a kumārī and the 'junction' worship (sandhi-pūjā), framed by the āgamanī and vijayā songs of Umā's homecoming and departure.
notes: Detailed rites (and offerings in some households) not recorded; the Kālikā Purāṇa's autumn-worship chapters not checked in Phase B.

name: Constant recollection of the dvaya
method_summary: Reciting the dvaya with its meaning — refuge at the feet of Nārāyaṇa with Śrī, and prayer for service — throughout life, as the Lord bade Rāmānuja in the Śaraṇāgati Gadya.

name: Living alone (ekacaryā)
method_summary: The sage wanders alone, homeless and unobtrusive, because many people cause quarrel and even two cause talk.

name: Ekādaśī fast
method_summary: Fasting on the eleventh lunar day of both fortnights as the 'vow of Nārāyaṇa's day', with rules for days overlapped by the tenth (fast on the twelfth instead) and for the time of breaking the fast. A one-day fast, not a prolonged one.
duration: one lunar day, broken on the following day
notes: The texts' own exemptions (for the sick, aged, etc.) were not checked; no warnings recorded.
alt_method_summary: Fasting on the eleventh lunar day, named among the causes of devotion to Rāma.
Fasting from grains (or fully) on the eleventh lunar day, with extra hearing and chanting; obligatory for Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇavas (Haribhaktivilāsa).
Fasting and worship of Viṣṇu on the eleventh lunar day of each fortnight, with vigil and breaking of the fast on the twelfth.
Vārkarīs fast on every ekādaśī, and the Āṣāḍhī and Kārtikī ekādaśīs are the goal of the vārī.
Abstaining from grain (or food) on the eleventh lunar day as an observance pleasing to the Lord. Summary only.
alt_notes: U06 contributes only this source; details belong to the Purāṇa units.

name: One-pointed worship of Nārāyaṇa (ekānta-bhakti)
method_summary: Exclusive devotion to Nārāyaṇa, worship according to rule without desire for fruit, non-violence, self-restraint and knowledge of the self, by which the devotee goes directly to Vāsudeva (MBh 12.336).

name: Practice on a single principle (ekatattva-abhyāsa)
method_summary: Holding the mind to one principle to counter the obstacles and their accompaniments (1.32, YBh 1.32).

name: One garment or none
method_summary: He wears a single garment, or goes naked.

name: Concentrations (dhāraṇā) in the Mokṣadharma's yoga
method_summary: The Mokṣadharma's yoga teaches fixing the mind in concentrations (dhāraṇā) — on the elements and within the body — with the steadiness of an arrow-maker intent on his arrow, by which the yogin gains yoga-power (MBh 12.289; 12.298–306).

warnings.text: The path of yoga is described as hard and dangerous (the images and verses to be confirmed).

notes: Low confidence on the specific objects and similes; to be extracted in Phase D.

name: The five element-concentrations (pañca-dhāraṇā) in the haṭha texts
method_summary: The breath is held with the mind for a set period (not reproduced) in the place of each element, contemplated with its colour, shape, seed-syllable and deity: earth (yellow, square, la, Brahmā), water (white, crescent, va, Viṣṇu), fire (red, triangle, ra, Rudra), air (smoky/black, ya, Īśvara) and space (clear, ha, Sadāśiva) (GS 3.68-81; GŚ 68-75). The texts place them differently: in the heart, throat, palate, between the brows and in the brahmarandhra (GŚ 69-73); at the anus-region, navel, above the navel, between navel and brows and above the brows (DYŚ 100-110; ŚS 3.63-65); from feet to knees, knees to anus, anus to heart, heart to brows and brows to crown (Yogatattva). The Gorakṣaśataka names them the stabilising, liquefying, burning, whirling and drying concentrations (GŚ 74). The Gheraṇḍa counts them as five of its twenty-five mudrās.
signs_of_progress: conquest of each element: not harmed by earth, water, fire or wind; moving in the sky; the door of liberation opened (GS 3.70-81; DYŚ 102-110)
no death even at Brahmā's dissolution (DYŚ 110; ŚS 3.65)
mastery of the element: not harmed by earth, water, fire, air; moving in space (Yogatattva 83–102)

warnings.text: The dhāraṇās are to be kept secret; revealing them brings loss of success.
They are not to be given to the deceitful or those without devotion.

alt_method_summary: Holding breath and mind in five regions of the body, each with its element, shape, colour, seed-syllable and deity (Brahmā, Viṣṇu/Nārāyaṇa, Rudra, Īśvara, Sadāśiva; in the Triśikhi the four vyūhas and Vāsudeva); each conquers its element. Durations omitted.

name: The five most potent limbs of devotion
method_summary: Serving the deity with faith, relishing the Bhāgavata with the like-minded, association with advanced devotees, congregational chanting of the name, and residence in Mathurā/Vraja; even slight contact with them awakens love.

name: Five kinds of withdrawal (pratyāhāra)
method_summary: Forcibly withdrawing the senses; seeing all that is seen as the Self; offering the fruits of acts; turning from all objects; and moving/holding the breath through the eighteen vital points (Darśana 7; Śāṇḍilya 1.69); the Yogatattva's withdrawal is regarding all perceived as the Self.
alt_method_summary: The Yoga Yājñavalkya teaches withdrawal in five forms, among them the forcible withdrawal of the senses, seeing all as the self, and the movement of the breath through the eighteen vital points — the form the Yoga Upaniṣads (Śāṇḍilya, Darśana) repeat.
notes: Contributes the Yoga Yājñavalkya's version to U04's entry; the full list of five is recalled only in outline for the Yoga Yājñavalkya.

name: The fivefold Śiva-sacrifice
method_summary: Austerity as drying the body for Śiva, action as Śiva's worship, japa as the five syllables or praṇava, meditation, and knowledge as the meaning of the Śiva Āgamas — each replacing its Vedic counterpart.

name: Cultivating the four attitudes (maitrī, karuṇā, muditā, upekṣā)
method_summary: Cultivating friendliness toward the happy, compassion toward the suffering, gladness toward the virtuous and equanimity toward the non-virtuous, so that white dharma arises and the mind becomes clear and steady (1.33, YBh 1.33); saṃyama on the first three gives strengths (3.23).
signs_of_progress: clarity of mind (citta-prasādana); strengths of friendliness etc. (3.23)

warnings.text: Equanimity toward the wicked is not a cultivation; no samādhi and no strength come from it.

equivalents.note: Same four attitudes and 'vihāra' vocabulary (YBh 4.10) as the Buddhist brahmavihāras; objects and aim differ (YS 1.33 assigns each to a class of object)

name: Cultivating the four gatekeepers
method_summary: Cultivating peace, inquiry, contentment and the company of the holy — all four, or at least one with full effort, since the others follow.

name: Bhīṣma's fourfold meditation (dhyāna-yoga)
method_summary: The sage, seated, withdraws the senses and repeatedly steadies the wandering mind; in the first meditation reflection, reasoning and discrimination arise; persevering without despair he reaches the happiness of nirvāṇa (MBh 12.188).

name: Gajakaraṇī ('the elephant's act')
method_summary: Raising the apāna breath to the throat, one vomits what is in the stomach; by gradual practice the wheel of channels comes under control (HYP 2.38). The Haṭharatnāvalī counts it among its eight acts.

warnings.text: One with excess fat or phlegm should first practise the six acts; others should not do them, their doṣas being in balance.

name: Worship of Mahāgaṇapati before the great vidyā
method_summary: Worship of Mahāgaṇapati with his five enclosures to remove obstacles before the worship of the great vidyā. Taught in section 2 of the Paraśurāma Kalpasūtra. (Summary; no mantras.)
prerequisites: initiation (dīkṣā) from a qualified guru into the relevant vidyā

name: Gargling and holding liquid in the mouth (gaṇḍūṣa, kavala)
method_summary: Holding oil or decoctions in the mouth as part of the daily routine (AHS Sū 2.6; Ca Sū 5).

name: Procreation rites (BAU 6.4)
method_summary: Lineage contribution (Upaniṣadic): BAU 6.4 treats marital union as a sacrificial act with rites for conception and offspring. Recorded as a summary only (sexual rite).
notes: Summary only under the restricted-content rule; no procedures, formulas or details reproduced.
alt_method_summary: The rite performed by the husband at the proper time for conception, first of the bodily sacraments (MDh 2.26–27; YS 1.11).

name: Garuḍa mudrā
method_summary: The hands facing each other, the little fingers and the index fingers joined, the thumbs joined, the middle and ring fingers bent like wings — said to destroy all poison; shown in Vaiṣṇava worship (Śāradātilaka ch. 4 commentary).

name: Garuḍāsana (the Garuḍa seat)
method_summary: Pressing the ground with shins and thighs, the body steadied by the knees, the hands on the knees (GS 2.37).
notes: The Gheraṇḍa's garuḍāsana is not the modern standing posture of the same name.

name: Rubbing the sweat of practice into the body (gātra-mardana)
method_summary: When sweat arises in the first grade of breath-control it is to be rubbed into the limbs (HYP 2.13; ŚS 3.40; DYŚ 69; GŚ 50).
signs_of_progress: firmness and lightness of the body (HYP 2.13)

warnings.text: If the sweat is not rubbed in, the element of the body is lost.

name: Gauḍīya initiation (dīkṣā)
method_summary: After mutual examination, the guru gives the disciple the Kṛṣṇa mantras (the eighteen-syllable gopāla-mantra and the kāma-gāyatrī, among others), tilaka and neck-beads; initiation makes one fit for deity worship. The mantras are given privately and are not recorded here.

name: Śrāddha at Gayā
method_summary: Offering piṇḍas at Gayā's sacred spots in sequence for the release of the ancestors.

name: Repetition of the Gāyatrī (Sāvitrī)
method_summary: Repeating the Sāvitrī verse to Savitṛ ('we meditate on that excellent radiance … may he impel our thoughts'), preceded by Oṃ and bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ, at the twilights; it is imparted by the teacher at initiation.
prerequisites: initiation (upanayana) in the tradition's own rules
notes: The rules of who may recite it and how often belong to the gṛhya and dharma literature (U02).
alt_method_summary: Recitation of the Sāvitrī verse preceded by Oṃ and the three utterances, especially at the twilights (MDh 2.76–78; YS 1.22–25).

name: Meditation on the Gāyatrī
method_summary: Venerate the Gāyatrī as all this — speech, earth, body, heart — whose four feet are the worlds, the Vedas, the breaths and the sun; and the space within the heart as identical with the space outside (ChU 3.12; BAU 5.14).

name: Dense recitation (ghanapāṭha)
method_summary: The most elaborate commonly practised recitation (ab ba abc cba abc, bc cb bcd dcb bcd …), whose master is called ghanapāṭhin.

name: The sevenfold yoga of the pot (ghaṭastha-yoga)
method_summary: The Gheraṇḍa Saṃhitā's whole course: cleansing acts, postures, mudrās, withdrawal, breath-control, meditation and samādhi, each producing one quality of the 'pot' (purity, firmness, steadiness, calm, lightness, perception of the self, non-attachment).

name: Gross, luminous and subtle meditation (Gheraṇḍa)
method_summary: Gross: visualize a jewel island in an ocean of nectar in the heart with the chosen deity (or the guru in the lotus of the crown); luminous: meditate on kuṇḍalinī as a flame at the root, the navel sun, or the praṇava-light between the brows; subtle: by śāmbhavī, on awakened kuṇḍalinī (GS 6.1–22).

warnings.text: Subtle meditation is secret, hard even for the gods to obtain (a warning of secrecy).

name: The Dol festival at Ghoshpara
method_summary: At Dol Pūrṇimā (Holi) devotees gather at Ghoshpara at Satī Mā's shrine, bathe in the Himsāgar tank, tie threads at the pomegranate tree for healing and boons, and sing; many are possessed by bhāva.

name: The meditation seat and posture of the Gītā
method_summary: A firm seat of one's own in a clean place, neither too high nor too low, spread with kuśa grass, a deerskin and cloth; sitting there, hold body, head and neck erect, motionless and steady.
notes: The order of the layers (cloth, skin, grass) is read differently by commentators.

name: Study and hearing of the Gītā
method_summary: Studying the dialogue is worship of the Lord by the sacrifice of knowledge; hearing it with faith and without cavil brings the worlds of the righteous; teaching it to devotees is the dearest service (18.68–71).

warnings.text: It is not to be told to one without austerity or devotion, who does not wish to hear, or who speaks ill of the Lord.

name: Song as offering (gīta)
method_summary: Singing of the Lord's qualities and deeds, following the rules of music.

name: The gift of the Vaitaraṇī cow
method_summary: Giving a (dark) cow to a brahmin at or before death so that the dead may cross the Vaitaraṇī by boat.

name: Gomukhāsana (the cow-face seat)
method_summary: The right ankle set beside the left buttock and the left beside the right, so that the legs resemble a cow's face (HYP 1.20); in the Gheraṇḍa the feet are on the ground with the heels by the sides of the back and the body steady (GS 2.16).
notes: Yoga Yājñavalkya ch. 3 is recalled (low confidence) to describe eight postures: svastika, gomukha, padma, vīra, siṃha, bhadra, mukta, mayūra. The Śivasaṃhitā (5.5) counts 'sitting in gomukha' among the obstacles that take the form of knowledge.

name: Recitation of the Gopāla mantra
method_summary: Worship and recitation of Kṛṣṇa's five-part mantra with meditation on his form (Gopālapūrvatāpanī).

name: Gorakṣāsana (Gorakṣa's seat)
method_summary: The feet turned up between the knees and thighs, the heels covered with the upturned hands, the throat contracted and the gaze on the nose-tip (GS 2.24-25). In HYP 1.54 'gorakṣāsana' is the siddhas' name for bhadrāsana.
signs_of_progress: a cause of success for yogins (GS 2.25)

name: Recitation of the tradition's scripture (pārāyaṇa)
method_summary: Reading or chanting a whole scripture in a set period: the Jñāneśvarī or Gāthā (Vārkarī), the Rāmcaritmānas in nine days (navāhna) or a month (māsa-pārāyaṇa) (Rāmānandī and wider Hindi-speaking devotion), the Kīrtana-ghoṣā and Bhāgavata in the nāmghar (Ekaśaraṇa).

name: Breath-control through moon and sun (Gorakṣaśataka)
method_summary: In the bound lotus, filling through the left (moon) and releasing through the right (sun) while meditating on the moon-disc, then the reverse while meditating on the sun-disc at the navel; this purifies the channels and manifests the inner sound.

warnings.text: Draw in and release the breath slowly; do not hold it beyond measure nor release it hastily.
Avoid pungent, sour and salty food; take milk.

signs_of_progress: sweat, then trembling, then rising up (GŚ 49); purified channels, kindled fire, inner sound, health (GŚ-Briggs 101)
notes: Measures of retention given in the text are not reproduced.

name: The five seals and locks of the Gorakṣaśataka
method_summary: Mahāmudrā, nabhomudrā (khecarī), uḍḍiyāna, jālandhara and mūlabandha: one who knows them is fit for success; uḍḍiyāna conquers death, jālandhara stops the nectar falling into the fire, mūlabandha draws apāna upward.

warnings.text: The reversed practice is to be obtained from the guru's mouth.

name: The five element-concentrations (Gorakṣaśataka)
method_summary: Holding the mind with the breath on earth (heart, yellow, square, la), water (throat, white crescent, va), fire (palate, red triangle, ra), air (between the brows, smoky circle, ya) and space (brahmarandhra, clear, ha, with Sadāśiva); they stabilise, dissolve, burn, whirl and dry, and the space-concentration opens the door of liberation.
notes: The fixed durations in the text are not reproduced.

name: Meditation with and without qualities (Gorakṣaśataka)
method_summary: With the gaze at the nose-tip, meditating on the centres in their colours (with qualities) and on the attributeless Śiva in the sky and the all-pervading self (without qualities); adjuncts are removed by practice.

name: Keeping the vow hidden (gūḍhavrata)
method_summary: He keeps his knowledge, austerity, vow and mantras concealed.

name: Worship of Hari with qualities according to fitness
method_summary: Meditative worship (upāsanā) of Hari under the qualities fit for the worshipper: Brahmā with all qualities, humans as bliss (ānanda), knower (jña) and the ever-existing Self (sadātmā); the gods are liberated when Hari becomes directly perceived through such worship.

warnings.text: A person who desires what he is unfit for surely falls; serve Viṣṇu according to your fitness.

name: Seeing that the guṇas act: non-doership
method_summary: Knowing that the guṇas act upon the guṇas (3.28) and that the senses move among their objects, the knower of truth thinks 'I do nothing at all' (5.8–9); he sits as one indifferent, knowing 'the guṇas are acting' (14.23), and sees prakṛti as the doer and the self as non-doer (13.29).

name: Guptāsana (the hidden seat)
method_summary: The feet hidden between the knees and thighs and the anus placed on the feet (GS 2.20); HYP 1.37 gives guptāsana as another name of siddhāsana.

name: Devotion to the teacher (guru-bhakti)
method_summary: Hold the highest devotion to God and to one's teacher as to God (ŚU 6.23); honour the teacher as a god (TU 1.11.2); the pupils worship Pippalāda as the father who takes them across (PrU 6.8).
alt_method_summary: Treating the guru as father, mother and Maheśvara, never slandering or disobeying him; the disciple first tests the guru, then serves him.

Honouring the true guru as the giver of the Name, above or equal to God: surrender, service and remembrance of the guru; among Bāuls and Kartābhajās worship of the living guru as the human form of the Lord.

Lineage contribution (Āḻvārs; Bhakti Sūtras): Madhurakavi's devotion to Nammāḻvār — his teacher's name sweeter than Kṛṣṇa, 'I know no other god', the teacher as mother and father; the Nārada Sūtra: devotion comes chiefly by the grace of great souls, who are not different from the Lord.

warnings.text: Disciples who break the guru's command and slander him become 'dead while living'.
Kāl sends false teachers in the true guru's name.

name: Meditation on the guru's form
method_summary: Meditating on the guru's form, the root of meditation, often visualized in the lotus of the head at dawn (Devī Gītā 7.40.1).

name: Recitation of the Guru Gītā
method_summary: Reciting or chanting the Guru Gītā, prescribed in the text for success, protection and liberation at death; in recent times chanted daily in Muktananda's ashrams.

warnings.text: Not to be taught to the faithless, the deceiver or the hypocrite.

name: Worship of the guru's feet (pādukā) and the circle of gurus
method_summary: Daily contemplation of the guru's feet in the crown with nectar flowing from them (PKS 2.2), recitation of the pādukā given at initiation, and worship of the lineage of gurus in their divine, perfected and human streams.

name: Worship of the guru's sandals (pādukā)
method_summary: Worship of the guru's sandals and recitation of the lineage's pādukā-mantra — 'no mantra beyond the pādukā, no god beyond the guru' (Kulārṇava 12.12).

name: Service of the teacher
method_summary: Serving and worshipping the teacher as the Lord in body, speech and mind; in the Guru Gītā the guru's satisfaction fulfils all practices.
alt_method_summary: Voluntary service to the Master and community (Sant Mat: physical, financial and mental sevā at the Dera); among Bāuls feeding and serving sādhus (sādhu-sevā).

name: Approaching a teacher with fuel in hand
method_summary: Having become disgusted with the worlds won by action, go 'fuel in hand' to a teacher learned in the Veda and established in brahman (MuU 1.2.12); live with the teacher a set time in austerity, celibacy and faith before asking (PrU 1.2); serve the teacher (ChU 4.4-9, 8.7-12, 8.15).

name: Approaching the teacher (gurūpasatti)
method_summary: Approaching, 'fuel in hand', a teacher learned in scripture and established in Brahman, with humility, service and questioning, and receiving the teaching repeatedly until it is grasped.

name: Surrender to the guru (gurūpasatti)
method_summary: The fifth means of the Nimbārka school: complete dependence on the guru, who then performs the means on the disciple's behalf.

name: Worship of Hanumān
method_summary: Recitation of the Hanumān Cālīsā (often on Tuesdays and Saturdays) and worship at Hanumān/Māruti shrines as Rāma's servant and remover of obstacles; the Samartha sampradāya joins it to the cultivation of bodily strength.

name: The Hare Kṛṣṇa mahāmantra
method_summary: The sixteen names 'hare kṛṣṇa hare kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa hare hare / hare rāma hare rāma rāma rāma hare hare' (the Kalisantaraṇa gives the Hare Rāma half first), chanted in japa or sung in kīrtana; the Upaniṣad states there are no rules of time, place or purity for it.

name: Recitation of the sixteen names
method_summary: Repeating 'hare rāma hare rāma rāma rāma hare hare, hare kṛṣṇa hare kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa hare hare'; the Kalisantaraṇa says no rule binds it, and that three and a half crore repetitions free from the gravest sins.
notes: Gauḍīya practice recites it with the 'hare kṛṣṇa' half first; the Upaniṣad gives the 'hare rāma' half first.

name: Remembering Hari as the doer; action as worship
method_summary: Doing the prescribed duties and avoiding the forbidden, without desire for results, while remembering that Hari within moves one's limbs and that all acts of mind, speech and body are his worship — the Yogadīpikā's definition of yoga.

name: Week of the name (harināma saptāh)
method_summary: A village holds seven days of continuous singing of the name and reading of the Jñāneśvarī or the Gāthā, with nightly kīrtan, ending with a common meal.

name: Loud laughter as offering (hasita, aṭṭahāsa)
method_summary: Loud laughter ('a-ha-ha'), opening throat and lips, offered to the Lord while absorbed in meditation on Śiva.

name: Hasti-niṣadana (sitting like an elephant)
method_summary: Named among the examples of posture in Vyāsa's bhāṣya on YS 2.46 ('posture is steady and comfortable'). The bhāṣya gives only the name; its form is explained by the commentators (Vācaspati Miśra, Vijñānabhikṣu and others), whose descriptions are not reproduced here.
notes: Name certain; form per commentators not recalled with confidence.

name: The restraints and observances of the haṭha texts
method_summary: The ten yamas (non-harming, truth, non-stealing, continence, forbearance, fortitude, compassion, straightforwardness, moderate diet, purity) and ten niyamas of the interpolated HYP verses and the Yoga Yājñavalkya; the SS's list of things to avoid (3.33) and to follow (3.35); in the HYP the ethical frame is chiefly celibacy, moderate diet and renunciation (1.57).

name: The postures of the Haṭhābhyāsapaddhati (group entry)
method_summary: A prose haṭha manual that describes more than a hundred postures (about 112 are counted), set in a sequence after the yamas, niyamas and cleansing acts and before breath-control and mudrā; many are dynamic or repeated movements and some use a rope. Its postures reappear, illustrated, in the Mysore Śrītattvanidhi. The individual names are not recalled with enough confidence to be entered here (see REPORT).
notes: Group entry standing in for the individual postures the unit could not responsibly name.

name: The eighty-four postures of the Haṭharatnāvalī (group entry)
method_summary: The Haṭharatnāvalī (ch. 3) names eighty-four postures and describes a selection, repeating the Haṭhapradīpikā's descriptions for several (siddha, padma, siṃha, bhadra and others) and adding many variants; the full list is not entered here because the unit could not recall it reliably (see REPORT for candidate names to check).

name: Havelī kīrtan
method_summary: Temple singing of the aṣṭachāp poets' songs in classical rāgas matched to each period of the day and season, as part of the Lord's service.

name: Meditation in the heart lotus
method_summary: Seated in solitude, body straight, meditating on the Lord (with Umā; or as the thumb-sized Oṃ; or as the flame) in the heart lotus (Kaivalya 5–7; Dhyānabindu 19; Vāsudeva).

name: Pilgrimage to Hiṅglāj
method_summary: Pilgrimage to the Goddess at Hiṅglāj (Balochistan), made by Kīnārām according to tradition and honoured by Aghora and Nāth ascetics.

name: Meditation in the heart-lotus (Uddhava's instruction)
method_summary: Seated evenly, gaze at the nose-tip, purify the breath-channels, raise Oṃ in the heart like a bell; visualise the upturned eight-petalled heart-lotus with sun, moon and fire in its pericarp and the Lord's form in the fire; meditate on all its limbs, then on the smile, then fix the mind in space, then think of nothing; the self is seen in the Lord, light in light (BhP 11.14.32-46).

warnings.text: Keep far from the company of the attached; meditate in a secluded, safe place.

name: Closing the doors of the senses with the intellect
method_summary: With the intellect he shuts all the doors (senses), so that outwardly their working seems deranged.

name: Restraint and withdrawal of the senses
method_summary: Withdraw the senses from their objects as a tortoise draws in its limbs (2.58); restrain them first and so slay desire (3.41); move among objects with senses free of attraction and aversion (2.64); Alarka learns the senses are conquered not by force but by yoga (Anugītā 14.30).

warnings.text: The turbulent senses carry off the mind even of a wise man who strives.
Abstaining from objects removes them but not the taste, which ceases only on seeing the supreme.

name: Restraint and withdrawal of the senses (indriya-saṃyama)
method_summary: Withdraw the senses from their objects on all sides as a tortoise draws in its limbs (2.58); restraining them all, sit yoked, intent on Kṛṣṇa (2.61); keep the senses withheld from their objects on all sides (2.68); move among objects with senses free of attraction and aversion and under the self's control (2.64); control the senses by the mind while acting (3.7); restrain the senses first in order to slay desire (3.41).
signs_of_progress: wisdom firmly established (2.58, 2.61, 2.68)
serenity (prasāda), the end of all sorrows and steady understanding (2.64–65)
even the inner taste for objects turns away on seeing the highest (2.59)

warnings.text: For one who abstains, the objects turn away but the taste (rasa) remains; it turns away only on seeing the highest.
The turbulent senses forcibly carry off the mind even of a discerning person who strives.
The mind that follows the roving senses carries off wisdom as the wind a ship on the water.
Restraining the organs of action while dwelling on objects in the mind is hypocrisy (mithyācāra).
Beings follow their nature; 'what will restraint accomplish?'
Attraction and aversion lie in the object of each sense; do not come under their sway, for they are waylayers.

equivalents.note: The Gītā's withdrawal of the senses from their objects (tortoise image); the word pratyāhāra is not used in ch. 1–3.

notes: Merger: probably the same as the skeleton's prc:indriya-nigraha ('Restraint and withdrawal of the senses', BhG 2.58, 3.41); both extractors used this id, so it is kept; flagged for the de-duplication pass.

name: The inner sacrifice of the senses (Anugītā)
method_summary: Contemplating the senses, mind and intellect as the seven tongues of the fire Vaiśvānara within, their objects as fuel-sticks, and the knower-functions as priests, one offers the objects into the fires within (Anugītā 14.20–24).
notes: Related to the prāṇāgnihotra of the Āraṇyakas (U02).

name: Inner worship: japa, meditation, pūjā, homa as acts of consciousness
method_summary: Outer ritual is for the gross; japa is the repeated contemplation of the supreme state, meditation the formless steady understanding, worship the firm mind in the great void, oblation the offering of elements, senses and objects with the mind into the fire of consciousness, bathing the entry into one's own nature (VBT 144-153; Paramārthasāra 74-80).

equivalents.note: inner worship (antaryāga) of other Śākta and Śaiva systems

name: Gazing on the iṣṭaliṅga (liṅga-yoga)
method_summary: Holding the liṅga on the palm at eye level and gazing on it steadily, then turning the gaze inward to the liṅga within; taught in modern Śivayoga training and associated in legend with the 'unblinking' (animiṣa) yogi.

equivalents.note: fixed gazing on an object; here the object is the worn liṅga and the practice is devotional

notes: Recorded from general knowledge of the Śivayoga revival (Hānagal Kumāra Svāmi); textual source to be found.

name: Worship of the iṣṭaliṅga on the palm
method_summary: Daily worship of one's own liṅga held on the left palm (karapīṭha) with water, ash, flowers and the like, without invocation or dismissal because Śiva already abides in it; the palm-worship is ranked above worship on an outer pedestal.

warnings.text: Never abandon liṅga-worship, even at the loss of possessions or life.

name: Devotion to Īśvara (īśvara-praṇidhāna)
method_summary: A special devotion (bhakti) to Īśvara, offering all actions to the supreme teacher or renouncing their fruit (YBh 1.23, 2.1; RM 1.23); Īśvara, won over, favours the yogin by mere intention and samādhi is near (1.23); a niyama and part of kriyā-yoga (2.1, 2.32).
signs_of_progress: realization of the inward consciousness and absence of obstacles (1.29); perfection of samādhi (2.45)

equivalents.note: Vyāsa defines praṇidhāna as a special bhakti; in Yoga its fruit is samādhi, not union with the Lord

name: Worship of the Lord (Nyāya)
method_summary: Worship (upāsti) of the Lord, declared by the wise to be the path to heaven and liberation; for the Naiyāyika it includes the reasoned contemplation of Him.

name: Resigning all actions to the Lord (mayi sarvāṇi karmāṇi saṃnyasya)
method_summary: Renouncing all actions in Kṛṣṇa, with a mind directed to the self, free of expectation and of 'mine', and with the fever gone, act (fight) (3.30); those who follow this teaching constantly, with faith and without carping, are freed from actions (3.31).

warnings.text: Those who cavil at this teaching and do not follow it are deluded in all knowledge and lost.

prerequisites: Faith (śraddhā) and freedom from carping (3.31).
signs_of_progress: release from actions (3.31)
alt_method_summary: Whatever one does, eats, offers, gives or practises as austerity, do it as an offering to the Lord, mentally renouncing all actions in him; one is thereby freed from the bonds of action with good and evil fruits.

name: Performing dharma as an offering to the Lord (īśvarārpaṇa)
method_summary: Doing the enjoined acts with the thought of offering them to Śrī Govinda (Āpadeva) or Īśvara (Laugākṣi Bhāskara), which makes dharma a cause of the highest good; the Gītā's 'whatever you do, do it as an offering to me' is cited as authority.

name: Jālandharabandha (the throat lock)
method_summary: Contracting the throat and setting the chin firmly on the chest (HYP 3.70; GS 3.12; ŚS 4.38; DYŚ 126; GŚ 36). It binds the network of channels and the 'water of the sky', so that the nectar falling from the moon (or the thousand-petalled lotus) is not consumed by the fire at the navel; it stops the two side channels and binds the sixteen supports (HYP 3.71-73; GS 3.12; DYŚ 127-128). In breath-control it is applied at the end of inhalation (HYP 2.45).
signs_of_progress: destroys old age and death and the host of throat ailments (HYP 3.70-71)
the nectar is not burnt by the fire and the breath is not disturbed (HYP 3.72; GŚ 36)
practised six months one becomes an adept (GS 3.13)

name: Wrangling and cavilling to protect truth
method_summary: Using contentious debate — including quibbles and futile rejoinders, or pure refutation without a counter-thesis — only to protect an ascertained truth from opponents, as a fence of thorny branches protects seedlings.

warnings.text: Quibbles, futile rejoinders and points of defeat are defined so that they can be avoided in one's own speech and exposed in the opponent's (NBh 1.1.1); vitaṇḍā without any purpose collapses into prattle.

name: Service and worship of the jaṅgama
method_summary: Honouring, feeding and serving the wandering Śivayogins (jaṅgamas), whose sight, touch and worship sanctify, and giving them the fruits of one's work.

name: Recitation (japa)
method_summary: Repetition of sacred words: 'among sacrifices I am the sacrifice of japa' (BhG 10.25); utterance of Oṃ at death (8.13) and of 'oṃ tat sat' at the start of rites (17.23–24); the Jāpaka's recitation of the Veda/Sāvitrī in meditation without desire (MBh 12.189–193); recitation of the thousand names (13.135).

warnings.text: Recitation done with desire, pride or wrongly leads to lesser worlds, not to Brahman (as taught in the Jāpaka story).

notes: U05's contribution to a shared practice (moderate confidence on the Jāpaka details).
alt_method_summary: Mental remembrance of the mantra in every condition (Kālīvilāsa 4.5-6); in Bengali devotion, repeating Kālī's name as the 'fence' that protects the field of life (Rāmprasād).

name: Three kinds of japa
method_summary: Loud, whispered (upāṃśu) and mental recitation, each far superior to the previous (Darśana 2; Śāṇḍilya 1.2).

name: Japa — audible, whispered, mental
method_summary: Repetition of a mantra, which surpasses ritual sacrifice tenfold when audible, a hundredfold when whispered and a thousandfold when mental; by japa alone a brāhmaṇa can reach perfection (MDh 2.85–87).

name: Braid recitation (jaṭāpāṭha)
method_summary: Reciting each pair forward, backward and forward again (ab ba ab, bc cb bc …).

name: Jātakarma (birth rite)
method_summary: At birth, before the cord is cut, the father gives the child honey and ghee, whispers 'speech' in its ear and wishes it long life and intelligence.

name: Kṛṣṇa-Jayantī fast
method_summary: Fasting on Kṛṣṇa's birthday — the dark eighth day conjoined with Rohiṇī at midnight — to be kept by all, especially the twice-born and Hari's devotees.

name: Jihvā-śodhana (cleansing — and lengthening — the tongue)
method_summary: The root of the tongue is cleaned with three fingers inserted into the throat to remove phlegm (GS 1.30). RESTRICTED in part: the text goes on to describe rubbing the tongue with butter, 'milking' it and drawing it out with an iron instrument daily at sunrise so that it lengthens (GS 1.31-32) — a preparation for khecarī; that procedure is not reproduced.
signs_of_progress: the text says a long tongue destroys old age, death and disease (GS 1.29)

warnings.text: Khecarī and its preparation are to be learnt only from a qualified guru and done gradually.

name: Renovation and re-consecration (jīrṇoddhāra)
method_summary: Rites for repairing a temple or replacing a damaged image, moving the deity's presence temporarily into a pot or substitute (bālālaya) and re-installing it.

name: Entering living samādhi (cīva camāti)
method_summary: Summary only: the tradition's account that a Siddhar, at the end, enters samādhi and is enclosed alive in a shrine, remaining present there. Recorded as the tradition's account; no instructions.
notes: Restricted (ends in death); belief recorded, no procedure.

name: Śrāddha for oneself while living
method_summary: A śrāddha performed for oneself during life (by those without heirs or seeking release), taught in LiP 2.45 and the Pretakalpa (ch. 8, 'self-śrāddha').
notes: Chapter titles checked (LiP 2.45 'jīvacchrāddhavidhi'; GP 2.8 'śrāddhakartr-ātmaśrāddha'); contents not read; no teaching extracted yet.

name: Combining knowledge with works
method_summary: Continuing the Vedic and social duties of one's station throughout life together with meditation on Brahman, rather than renouncing works after knowledge.

name: Jñāna mudrā / cin-mudrā (the gesture of knowledge)
method_summary: The tips of thumb and index finger joined and the other fingers extended, turned to the side — the gesture of knowledge held by teaching deities such as Sarasvatī and Dakṣiṇāmūrti; the commentary distinguishes a related 'exposition gesture' (vyākhyāna-mudrā) (Śāradātilaka, commentary on ch. 6 and ch. 7).

name: Breath-control as knowledge
method_summary: Exhalation as negating the world or renouncing objects, inhalation as 'I am Brahman' or scriptural knowledge, retention as steadiness in realization (Tejobindu 1.31–33; Varāha 5.58).

name: Repeated study of the science of the self
method_summary: Study and retention of the science of the self, practised constantly as study, listening and reflection.

name: The eighty-four postures of the Jogapradīpikā (group entry)
method_summary: The Brajbhāṣā Jogapradīpikā (18th c.) teaches eighty-four postures, alongside mudrās and other practices; the individual names are not recalled with enough confidence to be entered here.

name: Jyotiṣṭoma (the model soma sacrifice)
method_summary: The archetypal soma rite ('one desiring heaven should sacrifice with the Jyotiṣṭoma'), whose basic form is the Agniṣṭoma; Śabara names it as the paradigm of what leads to the highest good.

name: Initiation into the Kabīr Panth
method_summary: Initiation by a mahant or ācārya with the giving of the Name and the kaṇṭhī necklace; in the Dharamdāsī line also the pān-parvānā; vows of vegetarianism and abstinence from intoxicants.

sources.ref: on the true Name and the pān-parvānā

name: Service (kainkarya) to the Lord
method_summary: Service of the Lord in temple and home — making garlands, cleaning, cooking offerings, singing — done for his pleasure alone, the natural expression of the soul's being his servant.

name: Kākī mudrā ('the crow')
method_summary: The mouth is shaped like a crow's beak and air is drunk in slowly (GS 3.86-87). The same 'crow's-beak' drinking of cool air is taught in the Śivasaṃhitā at the two twilights and day and night (ŚS 3.70, 3.74-75), and kākī is the means of filling the belly with air in vātasāra and bahiṣkṛta dhauti (GS 1.15, 1.22) and of drawing in prāṇa in yoni mudrā (GS 3.38).
signs_of_progress: destroys all diseases; one becomes free of disease like a crow (GS 3.86-87)
destroys consumption (ŚS 3.74)

warnings.text: Kākī is secret in all the tantras.

name: Traditional study with the teacher (kālakṣepa)
method_summary: Study of the Śrībhāṣya, the Gītābhāṣya, the Tiruvāymoḻi commentaries and the rahasya works at the feet of a teacher of the lineage, orally, in the traditional order.

name: Skull-eating and corpse-ash practices (reported)
method_summary: Summary only: opponents report that the Kālāmukhas eat from a skull, bathe in the ash of corpses and eat it, and carry a club, as means to seen and unseen ends.

warnings.text: Yāmuna declares these acts forbidden by every scripture.

name: Pot-consecration and bathing (kalaśābhiṣeka)
method_summary: Water is consecrated in arrays of pots in which deities are invoked and then poured over the image, to renew its power or to purify after pollution (e.g. sahasrakalaśa in Kerala).

name: Cheating death (kālavañcana)
method_summary: The texts' means of postponing or conquering death: breath held in the body (HYP 2.39–40), preserving bindu and nectar, the element-concentrations that remove fear of each element (DYŚ 100–110), and (HTK) knowledge of the signs of approaching death to anticipate it.

name: Kālī-pūjā
method_summary: The worship of Dakṣiṇakālī on the new-moon night of Kārttika (Dīpānvitā) in Bengal, in homes and public pandals and at temples such as Dakshineswar and Kalighat, with the Tantrasāra's meditation and mantras; also weekly and monthly worship.
notes: The spread of public Kālī-pūjā is traditionally credited to Rājā Kṛṣṇacandra of Nadia (18th c.) — tradition's account, not checked.

name: Meditation on the kāmakalā
method_summary: Meditation on the Goddess's kāmakalā form — the point as face, the two points below and the triangle — taught in the Saundaryalaharī for the power to attract and in the Kāmakalāvilāsa as knowledge of the Śiva-Śakti union that liberates. Summary only.
prerequisites: initiation (dīkṣā) from a qualified guru into the relevant vidyā

warnings.text: The sixty-four tantras aimed at particular powers beguile the world; the Goddess's own tantra aims at all the ends of life.

name: Eating and drinking from the skull bowl
method_summary: The Aghora ascetic uses a skull (khappar) as his bowl, as a discipline of non-discrimination; the Kaulajñānanirṇaya calls the skull the best of vessels.

warnings.text: Aghora practice is given only by the guru and kept secret; the recent teacher Aghoreśvar Bhagavān Rām is reported to have taught that it is naturalness and service, not spectacle (the lineage's oral rule as reported; no text located — to be sourced).

name: Kapālabhāti / bhālabhāti (the skull-shining)
method_summary: In the Haṭhapradīpikā, rapid exhalation and inhalation like a blacksmith's bellows (HYP 2.35). In the Gheraṇḍa bhālabhāti is threefold: vāmakrama (breathing through alternate nostrils, not forcefully), vyutkrama (water drawn in through the nose and expelled through the mouth) and śītkrama (water sucked in through the mouth and expelled through the nose) (GS 1.55-60).
signs_of_progress: dries up the disorders of phlegm (HYP 2.35; GS 1.55)

warnings.text: One with excess fat or phlegm should first practise the six acts; others should not do them, their doṣas being in balance.
Some teachers hold that all impurities are dried up by breath-control alone and do not approve of the other acts.
The six acts, which purify the body, are to be kept secret.

name: Kapālarandhra-dhauti (rubbing the forehead hollow)
method_summary: The hollow at the forehead (bhālarandhra) is rubbed with the right thumb, on waking, after meals and at the end of the day (GS 1.34-35).
signs_of_progress: removes phlegm; the channels become clean and divine sight arises (GS 1.34-35)

name: Kapila's eight-limbed yoga with meditation on the Lord's form
method_summary: Duty, contentment, service of self-knowers, moderate pure food, solitude, the yamas and niyamas, posture, gradual mastery of breath, withdrawal, holding breath in one of its seats with the mind, meditation on the Lord's form limb by limb, and samādhi.
signs_of_progress: melting heart, hair standing on end, the mind attaining nirvāṇa like a flame (3.28.34-35)

name: Karaṇa: bodily seals in the āṇava means
method_summary: Āṇava immersion through karaṇa - bodily postures and seals (mudrā) - one of the five āṇava supports listed in MVT 2.21 and TĀ 1.170; treated in TĀ 5 and 32.
notes: Summary only; details of the karaṇas not recorded.

name: Karma-yoga: performing one's duty without attachment to the fruit
method_summary: Perform the prescribed action (one's own dharma) as duty, with evenness in success and failure, abandoning attachment and the desire for the fruit; action so done 'for the sake of sacrifice' does not bind and purifies the self.
stage: all; for the one wishing to ascend to yoga action is the means (6.3)
prerequisites: knowledge of one's own dharma (3.35)
signs_of_progress: evenness (samatva) in success and failure; freedom from the sense of doership (5.8–9)

warnings.text: Attachment to inaction is also forbidden.
One who restrains the organs of action but dwells on objects in mind is a hypocrite.
Action other than for the sake of sacrifice binds the world (3.9).
Do not let your attachment be to inaction.
Actionlessness is not attained by not undertaking actions, nor perfection by renunciation alone.
Restraining the organs of action while the mind dwells on sense-objects is hypocrisy (mithyācāra).
The wise should not unsettle the understanding of the ignorant who are attached to action.

alt_method_summary: Undertake action with the organs of action, the senses controlled by the mind, without attachment (3.7); do the allotted action (niyataṃ karma), since action is better than inaction (3.8); act for the sake of sacrifice, free from attachment (3.9); keep one's entitlement to the action and not to its fruit, the fruit not being the motive (2.47); act established in yoga, the same in success and failure (2.48); act, as the knower does, for holding the world together (3.20, 3.25).

name: Relinquishing the fruit of all actions
method_summary: Giving up the fruit of all actions, self-controlled and taking refuge in the Lord's yoga — the step for one unable even to work for the Lord (12.11), praised above meditation because peace follows immediately (12.12), and what the wise call tyāga (18.2, 18.11).

name: Ear-splitting (kān-phaṛāī)
method_summary: At the second initiation the cartilage of both ears is split by a specialist guru and, after healing, the large earrings (darśan/mudrā) are inserted — the defining mark of the Kānphaṭa yogī. Summary only.

warnings.text: A bodily rite performed only by the guru within the order; not a practice to be undertaken by oneself (tradition's rule as reported).

prerequisites: first initiation and probation
notes: Body-cutting rite: summary only per project rules.

name: Karṇa-dhauti (cleansing the ears)
method_summary: The openings of the ears are cleaned with the tips of the index and ring fingers (GS 1.33).
signs_of_progress: by daily practice the inner sound becomes manifest (GS 1.33)

name: Karṇavedha (ear-piercing)
method_summary: Piercing the child's ears, a later addition to the lists.

name: Herbal kaṟpam (kaṟpa mūlikai)
method_summary: Summary only: the use of particular herbs regarded as rejuvenating (the tradition names, among others, kaṭukkāy (chebulic myrobalan), nellikkāy (emblic), karicālai (false daisy) and vallārai), taken as a long regimen under a physician's direction. No doses or preparations recorded.

warnings.text: Kaṟpam is taken only after purging and under the prescribed regimen; the physician decides.

notes: Herb names recalled at moderate confidence; the full list of kaṟpa herbs is not reconstructed.

name: Kartābhajā initiation
method_summary: Initiation by a Mahāśay with the sect's secret mantra, after which the disciple (barātī) worships the Kartā, pays dues and keeps the teaching hidden behind outward custom.
notes: The mantra is secret and not recorded.

name: The Kātyāyanī vow of the gopīs
method_summary: A month-long observance in Mārgaśīrṣa by unmarried girls: early bathing in the river, worship of the goddess Kātyāyanī in an image of sand, and prayer to obtain the desired husband (for the gopīs, Kṛṣṇa).

name: Kāya kaṟpam (rejuvenation of the body)
method_summary: Summary only: regimens held to make the body firm, remove the humours at their times, reverse grey hair and wrinkles (TM 727) and prolong life for yoga — herbal kaṟpam, breath and yogic kaṟpam, and mineral-metal kaṟpam. No preparations, doses or durations are recorded; the mineral and mercurial forms are restricted.

equivalents.note: Āyurvedic rejuvenation; the Siddha form includes yogic and breath means

signs_of_progress: grey hair and wrinkles perish; the body becomes lustrous 'like collyrium' (TM 727) — the text's claim

warnings.text: Mineral and metal medicines are poison unless purified and prepared exactly as taught by a guru, and must be taken under strict regimen (pattiyam).
For the true knower who has seen the true thing, kaṟpam and yoga are needless (the means are not the goal).
All the powers — even transmuting metals and entering another's body — are easier than stilling the mind; the powers are not the goal.

name: Kāyaka — work as worship
method_summary: Each devotee earns a living by honest work in his or her own occupation, done as worship, not interrupted even for worship, and not gathering beyond the day's need.

name: The daily round of a Kerala temple
method_summary: From the opening of the sanctum at dawn, a fixed series of pūjās through the day (dawn, morning, mid-morning, noon and night pūjās) and processional offerings (śīveli) around the shrine, performed by the śānti; the tantri intervenes for installations, festivals and purifications.
notes: Names often given: uṣaḥpūjā, etiruttu pūjā, pantīraṭi pūjā, ucca pūjā, attāḻa pūjā (from memory; unverified).

name: Keśānta / Godāna (first shave)
method_summary: The first shaving of the beard at about sixteen, with a gift of a cow.

name: Kevala-kumbhaka (retention alone)
method_summary: RESTRICTED — summary only: the easy holding of the breath free of inhalation and exhalation, the fruit of sahita practice (HYP 2.72-73); it is said to arise spontaneously with mastery of siddhāsana (HYP 1.41). The Gheraṇḍa's kevalī is a retention measured against the count of the ajapā, with daily increments at set times (GS 5.92-99; counts not reproduced). When it is mastered nothing in the three worlds is unattainable; kuṇḍalinī awakens and the suṣumnā is freed (HYP 2.74-75; DYŚ 67-68).
signs_of_progress: nothing in the three worlds is hard to attain; the state of rājayoga (HYP 2.74-75)
awakening of kuṇḍalinī, unobstructed suṣumnā (HYP 2.75)
sweat, trembling, frog-like hopping, rising from the ground (DYŚ 69-76; ŚS 3.40-46)

warnings.text: As a lion, an elephant or a tiger is tamed only slowly, so the breath must be brought under control gradually; otherwise it kills the practitioner.
Proper breath-control destroys all disease; improper practice produces all disease — hiccup, asthma, cough and pains in the head, ears and eyes arise from the disturbed breath.
Draw the breath in slowly and release it slowly; do not hold it excessively nor release it quickly.
Powers that arise at this stage are obstacles; they are not to be displayed; the yogin should behave like a fool or a deaf man to hide them.
Breath must be tamed gradually, like a lion, elephant or tiger; otherwise it kills the practitioner; improper practice causes hiccup, asthma, cough and pains of head, ears and eyes.
Powers that arise must not be displayed.

equivalents.note: Both are a suspension of breath beyond the phases of inhalation and exhalation; the Yoga Sūtra's 'fourth' is defined by going beyond the outer and inner spheres, the haṭha kevala by the absence of inhalation and exhalation. The texts do not themselves identify them.

alt_method_summary: The spontaneous suspension of breath that arises after long practice; the Yoga Upaniṣads associate it with awakening of kuṇḍalinī and with powers. Summary only.

name: Khecarī mudrā ('moving in space')
method_summary: RESTRICTED — summary only: the tongue, turned back, enters the cavity above the palate (the 'skull-cavity' or 'well of nectar') while the gaze rests between the brows (HYP 3.32; GS 3.27; ŚS 4.31; DYŚ 125; GŚ 34). The texts describe a gradual, months-long preparation of the tongue that involves cutting — not reproduced here. They also give an inner khecarī, the breath held in the void between iḍā and piṅgalā (HYP 4.43-45), and an esoteric reading of 'eating cow's flesh and drinking the liquor of the immortals' as the tongue entering the palate and drinking the moon's nectar (HYP 3.47-49). The Khecarīvidyā makes a secret mantra received from the guru essential to it.
signs_of_progress: freedom from disease, death, sloth, sleep, hunger, thirst and swoon; not stained by karma nor bound by time (HYP 3.38-40)
bindu does not fall (HYP 3.42)
the tongue tastes a succession of flavours ending in nectar (GS 3.30-32; HYP 3.50)
samādhi of the bliss of taste (GS 7.9)

warnings.text: Khecarī, like all the ten mudrās, is to be guarded like a jewel-box and told to no one.
The preparation is gradual, over months; never all at once, or the body perishes.
Learn it only from a guru who knows it from text, meaning and practice, with the mantra from the guru's mouth; keep it secret.
The practice succeeds only through the guru and the mantra together and is not to be attempted otherwise.
It is not to be given to anyone; it is to be concealed with effort.
Called 'most secret'; to be guarded.
Learned from the guru's mouth.
Learn only from a guru who knows it from text, meaning and practice; keep it secret.
Proceed gradually, never all at once, or the body perishes.

equivalents.note: The Vivekamārtaṇḍa names the seal nabhomudrā where the Haṭhapradīpikā has khecarī; the Gheraṇḍa describes nabhomudrā as a separate, simpler practice (tongue turned up, breath held, anywhere).

alt_method_summary: U21 contribution: in the Nāth texts the tongue turned back into the cavity above the palate with the gaze between the brows, associated with drinking the nectar and conquering death. Summary only.

The 'moving in space' seal of the tongue, taught as a secret vidyā with a mantra (melana) received from the guru's mouth; the bodily procedures described by the texts are not reproduced. Also given inner meanings (the gaze; the renouncer's 'mudrā').
Summary only: the Tirumantiram's third tantra has a section on kēcari yōkam, revered by the Siddhars; recorded as a restricted summary without method.
notes: U22 contribution to the shared entry; section title checked in the local TM e-text.

name: Singing the Lord's names (kīrtana, nāma-saṅkīrtana)
method_summary: Singing or reciting the names and deeds of the Lord, alone or together; declared the fearless way for all (BhP 2.1.11) and the means of the Kali age that gives what meditation, sacrifice and worship gave in earlier ages (BhP 12.3.51-52; VP 6.2.17).
signs_of_progress: love born, heart melted, laughing, weeping and dancing 'like one mad' (BhP 11.2.40)
the Lord manifests and makes the devotee experience him (NBS 80)

warnings.text: The ten offences against the name (as cited from the Padma) obstruct its fruit.

alt_method_summary: Great souls ever sing the Lord's praise, strive, and bow to him with devotion (9.14); with minds on him they enlighten one another and always speak of him, content and rejoicing (10.9).

Lineage contribution (Āḻvārs; Bhakti Sūtras): singing the Lord's names with the mouth while thinking of him with the mind and offering pure flowers (TP 5); the devotees roam the earth singing and dancing (TVM 5.2.1); the name 'Nārāyaṇa' sung as refuge (PTM 1.1); every decad's last verse promises its fruit to those who recite it. The Nārada Sūtra: hearing and singing the Lord's qualities are means even in worldly life (NBS 37); being sung of, he quickly manifests (NBS 80).

Vārkarī: kīrtan and bhajan on abhaṅgas with the name; Ekaśaraṇa: kīrtana from the Kīrtana-ghoṣā, with hearing the foremost of devotions; Rāmānandī: singing Rāma's qualities, which in Kali carries one across.
Gauḍīya congregational singing of the name and of Rādhā–Kṛṣṇa's play (with khol and karatāla; later padāvalī-kīrtana styles); Puṣṭimārga havelī kīrtan of the aṣṭachāp songs.
Singing the Sants' and Bāuls' songs in gatherings — as worship, as teaching and (for Bāuls) as practice and coded instruction; Ravidāsīs sing the Amritbāṇī; Kartābhajās the Bhāber Gīt.
notes: U05's contribution to a shared practice.

name: Meditation on the centres (Kaula)
method_summary: Fixing the mind on a centre — the root, the brahma-knot, the heart, the throat, the palate, the forehead, the brahmarandhra — or on a lamp-flame in the sixty-four-petalled lotus, each with its own signs and powers.

warnings.text: To be given only to a devoted disciple tested (even for a year); kept secret from the deceitful, cruel and undevoted.

signs_of_progress: trembling, shaking, speech in tongues, spontaneous seals, frog-hopping, levitation, knowledge of past and future (KJN 14.16–19)

name: Placing the syllables for liberation (Kaula nyāsa)
method_summary: Placing seed-syllables on the anus, genitals, navel, mouth, nostrils, ears, eyes and forehead; for one in whom it is established, liberation is certain and at death the skull splits.

name: Non-killing (kollāmai)
method_summary: Refraining from taking any life and protecting all creatures, even at the cost of one's own life.
alt_method_summary: Not killing, tormenting or eating living beings, regarding them as one's own life (Pattirakiriyār 14); do not throw stones at birds or kill a frightened life (Kaṭuveḷi 25, 29).

name: Step recitation (kramapāṭha)
method_summary: Reciting overlapping pairs of words (ab, bc, cd …) so that both the words and their junctions are fixed; taught in the Prātiśākhyas.

warnings.text: A mantra wrong in accent or letter does not convey its meaning; as a verbal thunderbolt it harms the sacrificer, as 'Indra-śatru' did through a fault of accent.

name: Krama contemplation of the twelve Kālīs
method_summary: Contemplating every act of cognition as the sequence of the twelve Kālīs - emission, persistence, withdrawal and the nameless across object, means of knowledge and subject - until the sequence dissolves into the sequenceless (TĀ 4.148-172; Abhinavagupta's Kramastotra).

name: Feigned sleep and snoring (krāthana)
method_summary: While awake he acts as if asleep, making a snoring sound in the throat with the out-breath, so that people despise him.

warnings.text: Undertaken only after knowledge has been gained, impurity reduced and the teacher's permission obtained; the feigned acts must not conflict with the restraints (non-harming, celibacy etc.).

name: Krauñca-niṣadana (sitting like a curlew)
method_summary: Named among the examples of posture in Vyāsa's bhāṣya on YS 2.46 ('posture is steady and comfortable'). The bhāṣya gives only the name; its form is explained by the commentators (Vācaspati Miśra, Vijñānabhikṣu and others), whose descriptions are not reproduced here.
notes: Name certain; form per commentators not recalled with confidence.

name: Kṛcchra penances
method_summary: Summary only: graded expiatory penances regulating food and water over a set period (Prājāpatya, Sāṃtapana, Atikṛcchra, Taptakṛcchra, Parāka) (MDh 11.211–215).

warnings.text: Penances are to be undertaken according to one's capacity and under the direction of learned authorities; the digests allow substitutes for those unable to perform them.

notes: Restricted (prolonged fasting): no quantities or durations recorded. The warning is paraphrased at chapter level (moderate).

name: Bathing in the Krīm Kuṇḍ
method_summary: Bathing in the tank at Kīnārām Sthal, Varanasi, held to cure illness and grant blessings, especially on set days.

name: Kriyā-yoga (austerity, self-study, devotion to Īśvara)
method_summary: For the unconcentrated mind: austerity, self-study and devotion to Īśvara together (2.1), to cultivate samādhi and thin the afflictions (2.2); the yogin should first be intent on it (RM 2.1).
signs_of_progress: afflictions thinned, like seeds burnt (YBh 2.2)

warnings.text: Austerity is to be practised so as not to disturb the clarity of the mind.

name: The 'razor' concentration (kṣurikā)
method_summary: A concentration that 'cuts' through the vital points and channels with mind and breath; summary only.

name: Kukkuṭāsana (the cockerel)
method_summary: From padmāsana the hands are inserted between the knees and thighs, planted on the ground, and the body raised into the air (HYP 1.23; GS 2.31).
prerequisites: padmāsana

name: Kula worship (the 'primal sacrifice') as interpreted by Abhinavagupta
method_summary: The secret Kaula ritual of Tantrāloka 29, in which worship with a consort and the Kaula substances is presented as the outward form of the union of Śiva and Śakti in consciousness. Summary only; no procedure is given here.

warnings.text: Presented as the secret rite (rahasya) for qualified initiates only.

notes: Restricted (sexual rite).

name: Worship of young girls as the Goddess (kumārī-pūjā)
method_summary: Young girls are honoured and fed as living forms of the Goddess, especially during Navarātri.
alt_method_summary: A young girl is worshipped as the living Goddess (in the eastern tantras, at Kāmākhyā and in the Bengal Durgā-pūjā).
notes: Detailed rules (age-names of the kumārī etc.) not recorded here; not checked.

name: The retentions of the Kumbhakapaddhati (group entry)
method_summary: RESTRICTED — existence and scope only: Raghuvīra's Kumbhakapaddhati is a manual devoted to breath-retention that describes many more kinds of kumbhaka than the Haṭhapradīpikā's eight. Their names and methods are not recorded here.

warnings.text: As a lion, an elephant or a tiger is tamed only slowly, so the breath must be brought under control gradually; otherwise it kills the practitioner.
Proper breath-control destroys all disease; improper practice produces all disease — hiccup, asthma, cough and pains in the head, ears and eyes arise from the disturbed breath.
Draw the breath in slowly and release it slowly; do not hold it excessively nor release it quickly.

notes: Group entry; the individual retentions are a Phase-D target (names only, methods restricted).

name: Raising Kuṇḍalinī through the six centres (Śākta)
method_summary: The Goddess coiled at the root is awakened and led with the jīva up through the six centres to unite with Śiva in the thousand-petalled lotus, then led back (Ṣaṭcakranirūpaṇa 51-53). Summary only; taught as depending on the guru.

warnings.text: The practitioner is to be 'devoted to the guru's lotus feet' (the text's own qualification).

name: Kūrmāsana (the tortoise seat)
method_summary: The anus closed firmly with the ankles placed in reverse order (HYP 1.22); in the Gheraṇḍa the ankles crossed under the scrotum with body, head and neck straight (GS 2.32).

name: Hut-entering rejuvenation (kuṭīprāveśika)
method_summary: The principal mode of rasāyana: after preliminary rites, with shaved head, steadied resolve and a mind freed of its doṣas and turned to friendliness toward beings, the person enters a specially built secluded hut, is purified by cleansing therapies and then takes the rejuvenative under a physician's care. Summary only: construction, diet, preparations and durations are not recorded.

warnings.text: The better mode but very hard to carry out; only for the capable and self-controlled.
Diseases arising from lapses in the regimen are to be treated apart from the rasāyana.

prerequisites: capacity, health, wisdom, self-control, leisure and means (Ci 1.4.27)
notes: Marked restricted because the full regimen involves prolonged seclusion, purgation and special diet, and some formulations include metals and gems (e.g. Ci 1.4.22).

name: Contemplation of the three targets (lakṣya-traya)
method_summary: Attending to the inner target (kuṇḍalinī, inner sound, blue light), the outer target (colours and lights in space) and the intermediate target (voids).
signs_of_progress: lights, stars, a diamond mirror, the full moon, the midday sun, a flame (Maṇḍalabrāhmaṇa 2.1)
alt_method_summary: The Vivekamārtaṇḍa asks how yogins can succeed who do not know in their own body the six centres, the sixteen supports, the three targets (lakṣya) and the five voids; the Haṭhapradīpikā's śāmbhavī is defined by the 'inner target' held while the gaze is outward (HYP 4.36-37). The fuller teaching of the inner, outer and intermediate targets is in the Advayatāraka and Maṇḍalabrāhmaṇa Upaniṣads and the Siddhasiddhāntapaddhati.
notes: Contributes haṭha/Nāth sources to U04's entry; see U28's cpt:three-laksyas.

name: Contemplation of the Goddess as kuṇḍalinī
method_summary: Contemplation of the Goddess rising from the base through the cakras, piercing the three knots, uniting with her consort in the crown, showering nectar over the body and returning to sleep coiled at the base, as described in the Sahasranāma and the Saundaryalaharī; in the Kalpasūtra's morning routine the nectar flows from the guru's feet in the crown. Summary only.
prerequisites: initiation (dīkṣā) from a qualified guru into the relevant vidyā

warnings.text: Those without the succession of teachers, proud of mere knowledge, are harmed by the mantra's rays through their breach of the samaya.
The mind's steady flow toward the meaning comes only by the guru's grace, not by scripture alone.

signs_of_progress: nectar felt flowing from the crown (SL 10; LSN 39)
the Goddess seen as a streak of lightning above the six lotuses by the pure-minded (SL 21)

name: Recitation of the Lalitā Sahasranāma
method_summary: Daily recitation of the thousand names, often with the introductory and concluding parts; Bhāskararāya treats it as a daily duty that can also serve desired ends; the Rudrayāmala (as he quotes it) places name-recitation at the summit of a ladder of births leading to liberation while living.

warnings.text: The concluding section restricts the hymn to devotees of Lalitā (as summarized; low confidence).

name: Practice with a consort (latā-sādhana)
method_summary: The Kaula rite with a female partner (latā). Restricted: named only; the Mahānirvāṇa limits it to one's own wife in the Kali age.

warnings.text: In the Kali age only one's own wife.
Taking a woman by force leads to the Raurava hell.
Women are goddesses; never to be struck, reviled or deceived.

name: The four dissolutions (Aṣṭāvakra Gītā)
method_summary: Recognizing 'I am like space, the world a pot', 'I am the ocean, the world its waves', 'I am the shell, the world the imagined silver', 'I am in all beings and they in me' — after which nothing is to be renounced, accepted or dissolved.

name: The 'signals' of laya-yoga (saṅketa)
method_summary: Laya-yoga is the dissolution of the mind brought about by any of the 'signals' Ādinātha taught — eight crore of them: meditating on the void while walking, standing, sleeping and eating; gazing at the nose-tip; meditating on the back of the head (said to conquer death); gazing between the brows; attending to the forehead; to the big toes; lying like a corpse, relaxed, in a solitary place (DYŚ 14-24). The Haṭhapradīpikā similarly speaks of a crore and a quarter ways of laya, nāda being chief (HYP 4.66).
signs_of_progress: dissolution of the mind (cittalaya) (DYŚ 14, 24)
alt_method_summary: Dissolving the mind by fixing attention on an 'indication': meditating on the void at all times, gazing at the nose-tip or between the brows, meditating on the back of the head or on the big toes, lying relaxed like a corpse in solitude — Ādinātha taught eight crore such (DYŚ 14–24).

name: Learning from all beings (the avadhūta's method)
method_summary: Observing the ways of the elements, animals and people and drawing from each a lesson for detachment and knowledge, as the avadhūta took twenty-four teachers and his own body as a twenty-fifth.

name: Remembering the incarnations' deeds
method_summary: Reading, reciting and meditating on the episodes of the Līḷācaritra and the lives of the five Kṛṣṇas as the devotee's constant remembrance.

name: Offering all enjoyment to the liṅga (arpaṇa)
method_summary: Whatever is set aside for one's own enjoyment — food, sights, sounds — is first offered to the liṅga and then received as its grace.

name: Wearing the liṅga (liṅgadhāraṇa)
method_summary: The iṣṭaliṅga, kept in a small casket (karaḍige) on a cord, is worn on the body at all times — at the head, throat, chest, armpit, belly or in the hand, never below the navel; inwardly the liṅga of light is held in the mind at the base, heart or brows.

warnings.text: Never separate the liṅga from the body at any time or place.
Wearing it below the navel is a cause of sin; not on the tip of matted hair, lower back or an unclean place.
The text treats the liṅga's accidental fall with the utmost gravity (recorded as restricted).

name: Liṅga-initiation (liṅgadīkṣā)
method_summary: The guru, with assistants, bathes the disciple with water from pots consecrated by the five brahma-mantras, whispers the five-syllable mantra secretly into the right ear, installs a purified liṅga in the disciple's life-breath and places it in his hand to be worn for life. In Liṅgāyata practice it is given to all, women and children included.
prerequisites: a qualified guru (SSM 6.1–6); the disciple's discernment and dispassion

warnings.text: The mantra is given secretly (nigūḍham).

name: Worship of the liṅga
method_summary: Worship of Śiva in the formless liṅga (including liṅgas made of earth for the occasion), with bathing, bilva leaves, lamps and offerings; the Śiva Purāṇa teaches that Śiva alone may be worshipped in the liṅga because he alone is niṣkala.

name: Burial of the dead as liṅgaikya
method_summary: The dead devotee, having become one with the liṅga, is buried seated with the liṅga in hand rather than cremated; no death-pollution or ancestral rites are observed.
notes: Community practice from general knowledge; verify the details (posture, rites) in Phase C.

name: Metal transmutation (lohavedha / dhātuvāda)
method_summary: The transformation of base metals by processed mercury, treated in the 'vāda' sections of the rasa texts and regarded as a test to be passed before mercury is applied to the body. RESTRICTED: summary only.

warnings.text: Rasa-śāstra is not to be taken as merely for metallurgy; its purpose is liberation through the body.
Mercury with its impurities, though nectar itself, is poison; a physician skilled in practice but ignorant of the science is death in human form.

name: The honey-doctrine (madhu-vidyā)
method_summary: ChU 3.1-11: meditate on the sun as the honey of the gods, the Vedas as flowers and the rays as honeycomb cells; for one who knows it the sun neither rises nor sets. BAU 2.5 (also called the madhu-brāhmaṇa): meditate on earth, waters, fire and all things as 'honey' for all beings and all beings as honey for them, culminating in 'this self is brahman'.

warnings.text: To be taught only to one's eldest son or a worthy pupil (ChU 3.11.5-6).

notes: Upaniṣadic 'vidyā' (meditation-knowledge); the Brahma Sūtra (3.3) discusses which vidyās are to be combined.

name: Bee-like alms (mādhukarī)
method_summary: The renunciant takes a little food from many houses without burdening any and stores nothing for later.
alt_method_summary: Taking a little food from several houses after the household cooking fires are out, never from a single house; eating moderately (half food, a quarter water, a quarter air).

name: Unfolding of the centre (madhyavikāsa)
method_summary: The bliss of consciousness is gained by the unfolding of the centre - the central consciousness, the suṣumnā of the breath, the gap between states - through the means listed in PH 18.

name: Mahābandha (the great lock)
method_summary: With the left heel at the perineum and the right foot on the left thigh, the breath is filled, the chin set firmly on the chest, the perineum contracted and the mind fixed in the middle; the breath is held as far as able and released slowly, on both sides (HYP 3.19-21; ŚS 4.21-22; DYŚ 123). In the Gheraṇḍa the left ankle blocks the anus and the right foot presses that ankle, with jālandhara (GS 3.18-20). Some teachers replace the throat lock here with the tongue pressed at the root of the front teeth (HYP 3.22).
signs_of_progress: stops the upward movement in all channels; releases death's noose; brings about the confluence of the three rivers and leads the mind to Kedāra (HYP 3.23-24)
the breath enters the middle of the suṣumnā; the body is nourished (ŚS 4.22)

warnings.text: Mahāmudrā and mahābandha are fruitless without mahāvedha.

name: Mahābandha and mahāvedha
method_summary: Combined locks and the 'great piercing' named in the Yogatattva; summary only.

name: Repetition of the Mahāmṛtyuñjaya (Tryambaka) verse
method_summary: Repeating and offering with the verse 'we worship Tryambaka … may I be freed from death, not from immortality' for release from death and for health; in the Yajurveda it accompanies the Tryambaka offerings to Rudra.

name: Mahāmudrā (the great seal)
method_summary: Pressing the perineum with the left heel, the right leg stretched out and its foot held with the hands, the chin on the chest (throat lock), the breath filled and held upward, then released slowly; practised on the left side and then equally on the right (HYP 3.10-15; GS 3.6-8; ŚS 4.16-20; DYŚ 121-122; GŚ 33). The texts say kuṇḍalinī then straightens like a snake struck with a stick and a death-like state arises as the breath leaves the two channels (HYP 3.11-12). It is the first of the trio (with mahābandha and mahāvedha) taught already in the Amṛtasiddhi.
signs_of_progress: destroys the great afflictions and death; all tastes become tasteless and even poison is digested like nectar; consumption, skin disease, constipation, gulma and indigestion vanish (HYP 3.14-17)
removes wrinkles, grey hair, old age and death, consumption, cough, fever (GS 3.8)

warnings.text: It is to be guarded with effort and not given to just anyone.
It is secret in all the tantras; to be practised as the guru teaches.
The ten mudrās are to be guarded like a jewel-box and told to no one.

notes: Homonym only of the Buddhist mahāmudrā (Kagyu); no equivalence is asserted. U04's combined entry prc:mahabandha-mahavedha overlaps the next two entries.
alt_method_summary: The 'great seal' named among the haṭha practices of the Yogatattva and Dhyānabindu; recorded by name and purpose only.

name: Mahāmudrā as a hand-gesture (paramīkaraṇa)
method_summary: The thumbs interlocked and the fingers extended, shown to 'make supreme' (paramīkaraṇa) in the worship of the deity (ŚT 23.113-114); distinct from the haṭha mahāmudrā.

name: The Mahānubhāva renunciant discipline
method_summary: Monks and nuns keep moving (aṭana), live by begging, keep no possessions, harm no creature, avoid worldly company and remain in remembrance of Parameśvara and his incarnations.

name: The great departure (mahāprasthāna)
method_summary: Summary only: at the end of life the Pāṇḍavas renounce the kingdom and walk toward the north until the body falls (MBh 17.1–2). No instructions are given here.

warnings.text: The epic presents the departure as the close of a completed life after renunciation of kingship; each of the fallen is said to fall by his own fault, and only Yudhiṣṭhira reaches heaven in the body.
Later Dharmaśāstra authorities list the great departure among practices forbidden in the Kali age (kalivarjya).
