method_summary: A rite in the third month of pregnancy, before the embryo 'moves', for a male child.

name: Hearing the Purāṇa (kathā-śravaṇa)
method_summary: Listening with faith to the recitation and exposition of the Purāṇa by a qualified reciter, the first step of the Bhāgavata's path (hearing leads to taste, purification, steady devotion and knowledge of the Lord), with rules for giving and honouring the text.

name: Preparatory repetition (puraścaraṇa)
method_summary: The Kālīvilāsa holds that in the Kali age (true) puraścaraṇa is not possible because people are afflicted by hunger and sleep; instead the mantra is to be remembered mentally at all times, pure or impure, walking, standing or sleeping.
alt_method_summary: Before a mantra is used for rites, the practitioner masters it by a prescribed course of repetition with fire offering and other supplements, under dietary and conduct rules. Summary only.
notes: U31 owns mantra practice; no counts recorded here.

name: Pure food taken with restraint
method_summary: Eating food that is pure — of desirable colour, taste, smell and touch, sprinkled and consecrated, given by the untainted and taken with the proper recitation — together with self-restraint, since without restraint pure food yields no prosperity; taint lies in injury.

name: The meditation on the person as sacrifice (puruṣa-vidyā)
method_summary: Regard one's life as a soma sacrifice: the first twenty-four years as the morning pressing, the next forty-four as the midday, the next forty-eight as the evening; hunger and thirst as consecration; austerity, giving, uprightness, non-injury and truthfulness as the priestly gifts; death as the final bath.
signs_of_progress: Mahidāsa Aitareya lived 116 years (ChU 3.16.7)
notes: Upaniṣadic 'vidyā' (meditation-knowledge); the Brahma Sūtra (3.3) discusses which vidyās are to be combined.

name: Service of the Lord's form (puṣṭi sevā)
method_summary: Loving, householder service of Kṛṣṇa's image (svarūpa) as a living child and lord — waking, feeding, dressing, playing, resting him — with body, wealth and above all the mind; the fruit of service is more service.

name: Spontaneous devotional practice (rāgānugā sādhana)
method_summary: Driven by eager longing for a Vraja resident's love, the practitioner continues external practice in the body while inwardly remembering Kṛṣṇa and the chosen associate and serving in the inner perfected body, living (physically or mentally) in Vraja and following those who love him.
prerequisites: eager longing (lobha)
guidance of a guru in the chosen mood

warnings.text: Semblances of emotion (ratyābhāsa) in those whose hearts are impure are not bhāva; outward signs alone do not prove love.

name: The secret sacrifice (rahoyāga) — summary only
method_summary: A secret rite by whose sequence the Goddess is worshipped, with secret libations (LSN 83); its content differs by lineage and is not recorded here.

warnings.text: The Kaula worship is to be done in secret; making it public leads to hell.

name: Rājasūya (royal consecration)
method_summary: The Śrauta consecration of a king, during which the story of Śunaḥśepa is recited (AB 7.13–18).

checks.note: VS 9.35ff. and 10 (consecration waters 'apo devā madhumatīr agṛbhṇan … rājasvaś citānāḥ') located — 'VS 9–10' confirmed.

alt_method_summary: The soma rite consecrating a king, with the royal anointing and symbolic acts of sovereignty.

name: Bloodletting (raktamokṣaṇa)
method_summary: Removal of vitiated blood, counted among the purificatory measures by the surgical school (with leeches, venesection and the like). RESTRICTED: summary only; no method recorded.

warnings.text: Venesection belongs to the surgeon's domain (Dhānvantarīyas); Caraka refers such procedures to them.

notes: Suśruta chapter refs recalled (Sū 13 leeches, Śā 8 venesection), not checked.

name: Repetition of Rāma's name and mantra
method_summary: Repeating the Rāma mantra received at initiation (Rāmānandī: the six-syllable mantra) or the name 'Rāma' aloud, softly or mentally, often on tulsī beads; the Samartha sampradāya uses the thirteen-syllable 'śrī rām jay rām jay jay rām'; tradition credits Samartha Rāmdās with thirteen crore repetitions at Ṭākaḷī.

equivalents.note: the same practice with Rāma's name/mantra

name: Recitation of the Rāma tāraka mantra
method_summary: Recitation of Rāma's mantra, the tāraka given at Avimukta (Rāmatāpanī; Rāmarahasya).
alt_method_summary: Rāmānandī reading: Śiva liberates those dying at Kāśī by the power of Rāma's name.

name: Rāmlīlā (enactment of the Rāma story)
method_summary: The Rāmcaritmānas is recited while its episodes are enacted over many nights, above all at Navarātri–Daśaharā; the boy-actors playing Rāma, Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa are honoured as the deities during the performance. Tradition links its beginning at Vārāṇasī to Tulsīdās and his circle.

name: Initiation into rasa-knowledge
method_summary: Rasa-knowledge is given only by a qualified guru, pleased by the disciple's devotion, after initiation and worship, and kept secret. RESTRICTED: rites and mantras not recorded.

warnings.text: Without the guru's grace and permission the work is fruitless; the unfit gain nothing and lose their wealth.

prerequisites: devotion to the guru, good conduct, initiation (RRS 6.5-6)

name: The processing of mercury (rasa-saṃskāra)
method_summary: The rasa texts require mercury to be purified of its natural and adventitious impurities and brought through a series of eighteen processings before any use, under a qualified guru, in a proper hall. RESTRICTED: the processes, ingredients, apparatus and quantities are deliberately not recorded.

warnings.text: Mercury with its impurities, though nectar itself, is poison; a physician skilled in practice but ignorant of the science is death in human form.
Impure minerals and metals destroy life (impure pyrite causes death without doubt; impure copper and iron destroy life, strength and lustre).
Mercury is not to be used where a vital point is injured or in burns from caustic or fire.
Without the guru's grace and permission the work is fruitless; the unfit gain nothing and lose their wealth.

name: Worship of the mercurial liṅga
method_summary: Seeing, touching, remembering, worshipping and giving mercury, and worship of a liṅga made of processed mercury, are praised as surpassing all other liṅga worship. RESTRICTED: the making of the liṅga and its rites are not recorded.

warnings.text: Mercury with its impurities, though nectar itself, is poison; a physician skilled in practice but ignorant of the science is death in human form.

name: Rejuvenation therapy (rasāyana) — herbal
method_summary: Taken in youth or middle age after purification, by the self-controlled, either in a hut (kuṭīprāveśika) or amid ordinary life (vātātapika), with herbal preparations; its fruits are long life, memory, intelligence, health, youth, lustre and strength. No formulations recorded.

warnings.text: Rasāyana applied to an unpurified body is fruitless, like dye on a dirty cloth.
One who has not removed his bodily and mental doṣas never attains its benefits.
If disease arises from a lapse in the regimen, treat it with its own remedies, setting rasāyana aside.

prerequisites: purification of body; purity and restraint of mind (Ci 1.4.36-37)
signs_of_progress: long life, memory, intelligence, health, youth, lustre, voice, strength, success of speech (Ca Ci 1.1.7-8)

equivalents.note: Siddha rejuvenation regimens

name: Expiatory and yogic recitation of the Raudrī Gāyatrī
method_summary: After seeing urine or faeces or speaking with women or śūdras, he touches water, performs breath-control and mutters the Raudrī Gāyatrī or the Bahurūpī; in the third stage recitation of the chosen Gāyatrī is the ground from which yoga proceeds.

name: Reflecting on the evil of birth, death, old age, disease and pain
method_summary: Constantly seeing the faults of birth, death, old age, disease and sorrow, one of the marks called knowledge (13.8).

name: Care of the dying (Purāṇic)
method_summary: Turning the dying person's mind to the Lord (remembrance, the name), gifts made by or for the dying (above all the Vaitaraṇī cow), and the recitation of sacred texts.
notes: Further customary acts (placing on the ground, sesame, Gaṅgā water, tulasī) are described in the Pretakalpa's later chapters; not checked verse by verse.

name: Ritual hand-gestures (hasta-mudrā) in worship
method_summary: Gestures of the hands made at fixed points of worship, mantra-repetition and meditation, which 'give joy' (mudaṃ rāti) to the deities and make them present; the fingers are held to be the five elements (little finger earth … thumb space) whose joinings produce the gestures. The Śāradātilaka gives the invocation series (āvāhanī and the rest), avaguṇṭhana, dhenu and mahāmudrā (ŚT 23.106-114) and its commentary many more (aṅkuśa, kumbha, śaṅkha, garuḍa, jñāna, weapon-gestures of the deities).

warnings.text: The mudrās are not to be shown in a crowd or to the uninitiated; for seekers of liberation they may be made mentally.

alt_method_summary: Hand gestures shown to the deity at invocation, installation and offering, and in purificatory acts, named and described in the ritual manuals.

name: Seasonal purification
method_summary: Removal of the doṣas accumulated in a season at its proper time (e.g. kapha of winter in spring), by the purificatory therapies, followed by rejuvenatives; purified doṣas do not recur. Summary only.

warnings.text: Doṣas that have accumulated too much, when provoked, can cut off life; doṣas merely subdued by fasting and digestives may flare again.

name: Seasonal routine (ṛtucaryā)
method_summary: Adjust diet and conduct to the six seasons: in the 'taking' half (late winter to summer) strength declines and the dry tastes grow; in the 'releasing' half (rains to early winter) the moon restores strength; in winter the strong fire needs heavy, unctuous, sweet-sour-salt food; accumulated doṣas are cleared in the following season.

warnings.text: In winter the strong fire, finding no fuel, consumes the tissues; hence heavy food then (not a general licence).

name: Constant remembrance of Rudra
method_summary: He always remembers Rudra and, cutting with the intellect the root of the net of causes of faults, fixes the whole mind on Rudra.

name: Recitation of the Śatarudrīya with the Camaka (Rudra-japa)
method_summary: Chanting the Namaka (homage to Rudra in all forms) with the Camaka (petitions 'for me'), singly or in multiples — traditionally eleven recitations (ekādaśa-rudra), 121 (laghu-rudra), 1,331 (mahā-rudra), 14,641 (ati-rudra); in the agnicayana the Śatarudrīya pacifies Rudra.
notes: The multiples are recalled from living practice literature (moderate confidence).

queries: Ekadasa Rudra Laghu Rudra 121 Maha Rudra 1331 Ati Rudra 14641
checks.note: Multiples confirmed: Ekādaśa-rudra (11 Namaka with the 11 Camaka anuvākas), Laghu-rudra 121, Mahā-rudra 1,331, Ati-rudra 14,641.

name: Rudrābhiṣeka (bathing the liṅga with the Rudram)
method_summary: Bathing an image or liṅga of Śiva with water, milk and other substances while the Śatarudrīya is chanted — a later temple and domestic worship that employs the Saṃhitā litany.
notes: Post-Saṃhitā usage (Āgamic/Purāṇic setting); only the Vedic mantra element is U01's.

name: Wearing rudrākṣa
method_summary: Wearing rudrākṣa beads of specified faces and numbers on the crown, head, throat, arms and wrists; one of the eight shields; at death rudrākṣa-water is drunk while thinking of Rudra.
alt_method_summary: Wearing beads of chosen size, colour and number of faces, consecrated with mantras, observing food and conduct rules (Rudrākṣajābāla).

name: Meditation on the deity's form
method_summary: Holding the mind on the form of the Lord in the heart or before the mind's eye, limb by limb from the feet to the smiling face, until it does not waver; then simplifying the form (without weapons, without ornaments, one limb) or dwelling on the face (BhP 2.2.8-14; 3.28.12-33; VP 6.7.75-90).
stage: intermediate; after ethical preparation, posture and breath
prerequisites: yama and niyama
mastery of posture and breath
withdrawal of the senses
signs_of_progress: the form stays in mind whether walking, standing or acting (VP 6.7.87)
alt_method_summary: Vārkarī: meditation on Viṭṭhala's form standing on the brick, hands on hips, tuḷsī garland at the neck.

name: The teaching of being (sad-vidyā)
method_summary: Uddālaka's method: by one lump of clay all clay is known; in the beginning was being alone; it made heat, water and food threefold; illustrated by sleep, dying, honey, rivers, the tree, the banyan seed, salt, the blindfolded man and the axe ordeal, each ending 'that you are'.
notes: Upaniṣadic 'vidyā' (meditation-knowledge); the Brahma Sūtra (3.3) discusses which vidyās are to be combined.

name: The daily routine of right conduct (sadācāra)
method_summary: Rising while remembering Hari, purification, cleaning the teeth, sipping water, bathing according to rule, the twilight rites, worship and study, all acts dedicated to Acyuta.

name: The six-limbed yoga of the Maitrī
method_summary: Breath-control, withdrawal of the senses, meditation, concentration, contemplative reasoning (tarka) and absorption; the text adds placing the mind in the no-mind and the breath in the fourth (6.19), a concentration by restraining speech, mind and breath with a gesture of the tongue at the palate, seeing brahman by tarka (6.20), and rising through the suṣumṇā joined with breath, Om and mind (6.21).
signs_of_progress: seeing the golden-coloured maker; faults do not approach the knower, as animals avoid a burning mountain (6.18); becoming selfless (nirātman), the mark of liberation (6.20)

equivalents.note: shares prāṇāyāma, pratyāhāra, dhyāna, dhāraṇā and samādhi with Patañjali's limbs but has tarka and a different order

notes: Recorded as the text states it; later haṭha elaborations of the palate practice (khecarī) are restricted and belong to other units. Distinct from the Kālacakra six-branch yoga.

name: The seven aids as disciplines
method_summary: Purity of food, freedom from desire, repeated practice, performance of the five great sacrifices and other duties, the virtues (truthfulness, uprightness, compassion, generosity, non-injury, non-covetousness), freedom from dejection and from elation.

name: Melās and sādhu-sevā
method_summary: Gathering at festivals — Joydeb-Kenduli at Pauṣ Saṃkrānti, Lalon's festival at Cheuṛiyā, the Kartābhajā Dol melā at Ghoshpara — for singing, teaching and feeding sādhus.

name: Good conduct (sadvṛtta)
method_summary: Follow, with constant mindfulness, the conduct of the good: honour gods, teachers and elders; keep clean; speak truly, gently and first; do not take or covet what is another's; restrain greed, envy, anger and pride; avoid the wicked and serve the elders; abandon the ten sinful acts; see all beings, even insects, as oneself; follow the middle way; reflect each night on how one's days are passing; be devoted to continence, knowledge, giving, friendliness, compassion, joy, equanimity and calm.
signs_of_progress: health and mastery of the senses at once (Ca Sū 8.18); a hundred years free of disease (8.31)

name: Sadyaḥsamutkrānti: initiation bringing immediate departure
method_summary: A rite described in Tantrāloka 19 by which the teacher releases a qualified disciple from the body at once into Śiva. Summary only; no procedure is given here.

warnings.text: Treated in the tantra as reserved to the qualified teacher and disciple (details not recorded here).

notes: Restricted (a rite ending bodily life). Content from the chapter title and table of contents only.

name: Meditation with and without qualities
method_summary: Meditation on a form (the Lord in the heart, Maheśvara as oneself) or on the Self's nature without form, leading to samādhi (Yogatattva 104; Śāṇḍilya 1.71; Darśana 9).
alt_method_summary: Holding the breath, meditating on the chosen deity (with qualities: gives the powers) and then on the qualityless like space (gives liberation), leading to samādhi (DYŚ 111–114; GŚ 76–85).

name: Meditation on the qualified Brahman (saguṇa-upāsanā)
method_summary: Sustained meditation on Brahman with attributes or through a symbol (Oṃ, the sun, the mind), seated, one-pointed, in any suitable place, continued until death; leads to the Brahma-world and gradual liberation, and prepares the mind for knowledge.

name: The natural discipline (sahaj): every act as worship
method_summary: Living in constant awareness of the Lord without forced austerities: eyes open, going about as circumambulation, work as service, lying down as prostration; no closing of eyes, stopping of ears or mortification.
signs_of_progress: the Lord's form seen everywhere with open eyes (Kabīr)

warnings.text: Everyone speaks of sahaj but no one knows it: it is not ease or laxity.

name: Name and mantra of the beginner (pravarta)
method_summary: At the beginner's stage the Sahajiyā relies on the Name and the mantra received from the guru, as in ordinary Vaiṣṇava practice, before any esoteric discipline.

name: The practice of the couple (Sahajiyā, Bāul) — summary only
method_summary: RESTRICTED. The ritual union of a man and a woman partner (sādhana-saṅginī), after long preparation through the stages of name, mantra and bhāva, in which the partners contemplate each other as Kṛṣṇa and Rādhā and aim to transform kāma into prema without the downward fall; recorded only as its aim and the texts' warnings.

sources.ref: on the difficulty of the path

warnings.text: The path is as hard as holding an elephant with a spider's thread; one must be near the fire and not burn.
Only the siddha, free of lust, is qualified; for others it is a fall into kāma.

name: Worship with the thousand names (nāma-arcana, kuṅkumārcana)
method_summary: Offering one flower (or vermilion) into the bindu with each name in the dative with 'namaḥ', after reciting the introductory part and the placements, contemplating the identity of oneself and the Goddess as the principal thing (Bhāskararāya on the phalaśruti).

name: Sahita-kumbhaka (retention joined with inhalation and exhalation)
method_summary: Retention accompanied by inhalation and exhalation, to be practised until kevala is attained (HYP 2.71-72); in the Dattātreyayogaśāstra the alternate-nostril practice is itself called sahita (DYŚ 58-60). The Gheraṇḍa counts sahita as the first of its eight retentions, in two forms: sagarbha, with the seed-syllables a, u, m and meditation on Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Rudra (rajas, sattva, tamas), and nirgarbha, without seed (GS 5.47-55). Restricted only as to the counts and ratios, which are not reproduced.

warnings.text: As a lion, an elephant or a tiger is tamed only slowly, so the breath must be brought under control gradually; otherwise it kills the practitioner.
Proper breath-control destroys all disease; improper practice produces all disease — hiccup, asthma, cough and pains in the head, ears and eyes arise from the disturbed breath.
Draw the breath in slowly and release it slowly; do not hold it excessively nor release it quickly.
Breath must be tamed gradually, like a lion, elephant or tiger; otherwise it kills the practitioner; improper practice causes hiccup, asthma, cough and pains of head, ears and eyes.

alt_method_summary: Retention joined with inhalation and exhalation, in four named varieties (Yogakuṇḍalī 1.19ff.). Summary only; no counts.

name: Funeral rites for Śaiva initiates (antyeṣṭi)
method_summary: Special funeral rites for initiates in which the guru ritually completes the soul's release; described in the Siddhānta paddhatis.

name: Caryā (Śaiva temple service)
method_summary: Service of Śiva in the temple with the body: sweeping and smearing the floor, gathering flowers and making garlands, lighting lamps, singing the hymns, serving devotees — in the attitude of a servant (dāsa-mārga), as Appar did.
signs_of_progress: the fruit is sālokya, dwelling in Śiva's world

name: Śaiva meditation with and without object
method_summary: Meditation on Śiva's form (Śrīkaṇṭha) first, with an object and a seed, and at the end without object or seed, as awareness of the formless self; knowing the meditator, the act, the object and the purpose.

name: Jñāna (knowledge of Śiva)
method_summary: Knowledge given by grace through the guru, cultivated in four steps: hearing (kēṭṭal), reflecting (cintittal), clarity (teḷital) and abiding (niṭṭai); seeing the tattvas and the soul as not-Śiva and the world as a mirage, meditating the five letters, abiding at Śiva's feet — the true path (san-mārga).
signs_of_progress: fruit: sāyujya, union

name: Kriyā (Śaiva ritual worship)
method_summary: Worship of Śiva in the liṅga or image with the prescribed mantras, offerings and fire — the son's attitude (satputra-mārga), as Campantar's.
prerequisites: initiation (dīkṣā)
signs_of_progress: fruit: sāmīpya, nearness to Śiva

name: Pilgrimage to the Tēvāram shrines
method_summary: Visiting and singing at the shrines praised in the Tēvāram (the 274 'sung places', pāṭal peṟṟa talam) and at Chidambaram, following the saints' journeys.

name: Hymn-devotion to Śiva as one's own self
method_summary: Praising Śiva with hymns in which the devotee relishes an identity already recognized; for one rich in devotion Śiva manifests without meditation, mantra or procedure (Śivastotrāvalī 1.1; Abhinavagupta's Bhairavastava).

name: Yoga (Śivayoga)
method_summary: Inner worship and meditation on Śiva: the Āgamas' six-limbed yoga (breath control, withdrawal, holding, meditation, reasoning [tarka], absorption) or the Tirumantiram's eight limbs, fixing the mind on Śiva in the heart or at the centres — the friend's attitude (sakhā-mārga), as Cuntarar's.
signs_of_progress: fruit: sārūpya, Śiva's form

warnings.text: The powers that arise from yoga are not the goal; only knowledge by grace gives final release.

name: Friendship with the Lord (sakhya)
method_summary: Relating to the Lord as a trusted friend. Eighth of the Bhāgavata's nine forms; friendship is one of love's eleven forms in the Nārada Sūtra.
notes: One of the Bhāgavata's nine forms of devotion (prc:navadha-bhakti, U07). Exemplar: Arjuna, whom Kṛṣṇa calls 'my devotee and friend' (BhG 4.3). The Gauḍīya sakhya-rasa (trm:sakhya-rasa, U16) systematises it.

name: Abiding as the witness (sākṣi-bhāva)
method_summary: Recognizing oneself as the unchanging witness of the mind's modes, the senses and the states, like the lamp in a theatre that lights all and remains when all have gone.

name: Resting as the witness (Aṣṭāvakra Gītā)
method_summary: Knowing oneself as the witness of the elements, body and mind, separating from the body and resting in consciousness, one is free now.

warnings.text: The practice of samādhi itself is called bondage from the absolute standpoint (1.15).

name: Contraction of power (śaktisaṅkoca)
method_summary: Withdrawing the flow of the senses from their objects and turning back toward the source, like a tortoise drawing in its limbs (Kṣemarāja's auto-commentary on Pratyabhijñāhṛdaya 18; summary).

name: Expansion of power (śaktivikāsa); the bhairavī seal
method_summary: Keeping awareness within while the eyes and senses remain open to objects without blinking - 'attention inward, gaze outward' - so that the senses open simultaneously into consciousness (Kṣemarāja's auto-commentary on Pratyabhijñāhṛdaya 18, which quotes the bhairavī mudrā; summary).

name: Śakticālana (moving the power)
method_summary: RESTRICTED — summary only: rousing kuṇḍalinī, who sleeps coiled above the kanda covering the door of Brahman with her mouth, so that she leaves the mouth of the suṣumnā and the breath enters it (HYP 3.104-123; GS 3.49-60; ŚS 4.53-57). The texts describe it with a particular seat, pressure at the kanda, bhastrikā and contraction, or (in the Gheraṇḍa) with the navel bound in cloth and aśvinī mudrā; they call it the only means to cleanse the channels and say the yoni mudrā does not succeed without it (GS 3.57). No procedure, measure or time is reproduced.

warnings.text: Success comes to the celibate who always eats wholesome, moderate food.
It is to be practised by the guru's instruction.
It is to be kept secret and practised in a hidden room.
The ten mudrās are to be guarded like a jewel-box and told to no one.

alt_method_summary: Rousing the kuṇḍalinī from her place and leading her upward through the suṣumnā, with sarasvatī-cālana; the texts say it removes abdominal disease. Summary only.

name: Śalabhāsana (the locust)
method_summary: Lying face down with the hands (palms) on the ground by the chest, the feet raised a span into the air (GS 2.39).

name: Sāman chanting (sāmagāna)
method_summary: Singing the verses of the Sāmaveda to their melodies as given in the song-books — village and forest songs and their ritual applications — with stretched vowels, repetitions and stobhas, the notes shown on the fingers; at the soma rite the udgātṛ, prastotṛ and pratihartṛ divide the parts.
prerequisites: initiation in a Sāmaveda śākhā

warnings.text: A mantra wrong in accent or letter does not convey its meaning; as a verbal thunderbolt it harms the sacrificer, as 'Indra-śatru' did through a fault of accent.
The forest (āraṇyageya) melodies are regarded as potent and are learned apart, outside the village (as reported).

name: Samādhi as the eighth limb
method_summary: Meditation shining only as its object, as if empty of its own form (3.3, YBh 3.3).
alt_method_summary: Lineage contribution (Upaniṣadic): the sixth limb of the Maitrī's yoga (6.18); 'the happiness of a mind whose stains are washed away by samādhi cannot be described' (MaiU 6.34); being 'collected' (samāhita) in BAU 4.4.23 and KU 1.2.24.

name: Collective temple singing (samāj-gāyan)
method_summary: Temple musicians and devotees sing the founders' padas in fixed rāgas and style before the deity at set times.

name: Offering before use (samarpaṇa)
method_summary: Nothing unoffered is used: food, clothes and all things are first offered to the Lord and then accepted as his grace.

name: Samasaṃsthāna (the even configuration)
method_summary: Named among the examples of posture in Vyāsa's bhāṣya on YS 2.46 ('posture is steady and comfortable'). The bhāṣya gives only the name; its form is explained by the commentators (Vācaspati Miśra, Vijñānabhikṣu and others), whose descriptions are not reproduced here.
notes: Name certain; form per commentators not recalled with confidence.

name: Cultivating sameness (samatva)
method_summary: Make pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat the same, and then act (2.38); be the same in success and failure — this sameness is called yoga (2.48); the steadfast person whom these do not disturb, the same in pain and pleasure, is fit for immortality (2.15).
signs_of_progress: not disturbed by pleasure and pain (2.15)
neither rejoicing nor hating on meeting the pleasant or the unpleasant (2.57)

name: Samāvartana (return home, final bath)
method_summary: The ceremonial bath (snāna) ending studentship, after which the graduate (snātaka) may marry; he keeps the snātaka rules (MDh 4).

name: Samaya worship in the heart-space (dahara)
method_summary: The Samayin imagines the Śrīcakra in the small space of the heart (or identifies it with the moon-disc in the crown lotus) and worships the Goddess there without any external support; he also worships the Śiva-Śakti pair in each cakra, Samayā with Samaya in the base and the thousand-petalled lotus (SL 36-41 with Lakṣmīdhara).
prerequisites: initiation (dīkṣā) from a qualified guru into the relevant vidyā

equivalents.note: the Samaya form of inner worship

name: Initiation into the observances (samaya-dīkṣā)
method_summary: First Śaiva initiation making the disciple a samayin, bound by post-initiatory rules and entitled to worship and study; for the incapable, the observances may be purified away (seedless initiation).
alt_method_summary: The first initiation, conferring the status of samayin with rules of conduct and the right to worship and study.

name: Worship of the Goddess led through the cakras (Samaya procedure described by Bhāskararāya)
method_summary: When the initiate's contemplation of unity is firm and the guru's rite of 'great piercing' (mahāvedha) has been done, the Goddess, risen from the base, is said to become manifest in the maṇipūra; there she is worshipped with offerings, then led to the heart, the throat and the brow with further offerings, and united with Sadāśiva in the thousand-petalled lotus. Summary only — no method of raising the power is recorded.
prerequisites: initiation (dīkṣā) from a qualified guru into the relevant vidyā
firm contemplation of the unities; the guru's mahāvedha rite

warnings.text: Those without the succession of teachers, proud of mere knowledge, are harmed by the mantra's rays through their breach of the samaya.
The mind's steady flow toward the meaning comes only by the guru's grace, not by scripture alone.

name: Śāmbhava immersion
method_summary: Immersion (samāveśa) that arises for one who thinks of nothing, awakened by the teacher: consciousness rests in itself without thought-constructs, the universe seen as a reflection in the mirror of consciousness (MVT 2.23; TĀ 1.168, 3).

name: Śāmbhavī mudrā (Śambhu's seal)
method_summary: The inner target held while the gaze is outward and unblinking — looking yet not seeing, with mind and breath dissolved in the inner target (HYP 4.36-37); in the Gheraṇḍa, looking at the point between the eyes and beholding the self (GS 3.64). It is the means to dhyāna-samādhi (GS 7.5-8) and to subtle meditation (GS 6.21); trāṭaka leads to it (GS 1.54); śāmbhavī is held while listening to the inner sound (HYP 4.67).
signs_of_progress: the reality, Śambhu's state beyond void and non-void, shines forth (HYP 4.37)
one who knows it is Ādinātha, Nārāyaṇa, Brahmā — is Brahman (GS 3.66-67)
the place where such a yogin lives is purified (Advayatāraka)

warnings.text: It is obtained by the guru's grace.
The Vedas, śāstras and purāṇas are like common courtesans; śāmbhavī is guarded like a woman of good family.

equivalents.note: Śāṇḍilya Up. 1.31 defines vaiṣṇavī mudrā in the very terms by which HYP 4.36 defines śāmbhavī (inner target, outward unblinking gaze).

alt_method_summary: Gazing with open, unblinking eyes while attention rests on the inner target; three forms by the eyes' opening (amā, pratipat, pūrṇimā), the open 'full-moon' gaze being recommended.
Attention held on an inner aim while the eyes gaze outward without blinking; the half-open, steady gaze in which breath and mind dissolve.

name: Meditation on combinations (saṃhitā)
method_summary: Meditate on the five great combinations — of worlds, lights, knowledge, progeny and the body — each as prior form, latter form, junction and link (TU 1.3).

name: The means-accomplishments: study, hearing, reasoning, friends, giving
method_summary: Five of the eight accomplishments of SK 51 serve as means to knowledge of the principles: studying the texts, hearing instruction, examining by reasoning ('what is true, what is highest, what is the final good'), gaining a friend or fellow student who knows, and serving the venerable with gifts (Gauḍapāda) — Vācaspati (recalled) reads dāna as the purification of discriminative knowledge. Approaching a teacher to end the three sufferings is itself an accomplishment.
prerequisites: desire to know born of suffering (SK 1)
signs_of_progress: knowledge of the twenty-five principles arises

warnings.text: Error, incapacity and contentment are the curb that holds the world in ignorance like a goaded elephant; they must be abandoned.
Hearing without reflection does not bring fulfilment, as with Virocana.

equivalents.note: hearing/study (śabda, adhyayana) ~ Advaita's śravaṇa (interpretive)
reasoning (ūha) ~ Advaita's manana (interpretive)

name: Rites for concord (sāṃmanasya)
method_summary: Rites with the concord hymns to make family and assembly of one heart and mind.

name: Renunciation (saṃnyāsa) in the Dharmaśāstra
method_summary: After the Prājāpatya sacrifice with all possessions given away, the renouncer deposits the fires in himself and goes forth giving safety to all beings; he lives alone, without fire or house, begging once a day, purifying step, water, speech and act, delighting in the self, practising breath-control and meditation, neither welcoming death nor life (MDh 6.33–85); he must not renounce the Veda (VDh 10.4).
stage: after the debts are paid (or, in other views, from any stage)

warnings.text: Seeking liberation without paying the three debts leads downward (MDh 6.35–37).

name: The father-to-son transfer at death (sampratti)
method_summary: A dying father transfers his roles and faculties to his son: 'you are brahman, the sacrifice, the world' (BAU 1.5.17); or lying on the son and placing speech, breath, sight and the other faculties in him one by one, the son receiving each (KauU 2.15).

name: Vaikhānasa image worship (samūrtārcana)
method_summary: Daily worship of Viṣṇu with Vedic mantras: eight services to the fixed image by flowers only, thirty-two services to the movable (kautuka) image, invoking the five forms, with fire offering.

name: Discussion with the learned (saṃvāda)
method_summary: Discussion with pupils, teachers, fellow-students and distinguished seekers of the good who are free of envy — even without advancing one's own counter-thesis — for the ripening of wisdom: cutting doubt, understanding the unknown, confirming what has been ascertained.
signs_of_progress: doubt cut
the unknown understood
what is ascertained confirmed (NBh 4.2.47)

name: The meditation on the gatherer (saṃvarga-vidyā)
method_summary: Venerate wind as the gatherer into which fire, sun, moon and waters go (with respect to the gods) and breath as the gatherer into which speech, sight, hearing and mind go in sleep (with respect to the self).
notes: Upaniṣadic 'vidyā' (meditation-knowledge); the Brahma Sūtra (3.3) discusses which vidyās are to be combined.

name: Saṃyama
method_summary: Concentration, meditation and samādhi together on one object (3.4), applied stage by stage (3.6) to objects such as the three transformations, the sun, moon, pole star, navel wheel, throat-well, heart, the moment and its sequence (3.16–52).
signs_of_progress: the light of insight (3.5); the powers (3.16–49)

warnings.text: The powers are obstacles in samādhi; they are powers only in the emergent state.
Invited by the celestials, form neither attachment nor pride, for the undesired would recur.
Without mastering the lower stage one does not gain saṃyama on higher stages by skipping.

name: Saṃyamas for powers (Śāṇḍilya)
method_summary: Concentration on parts of the body, on merit and demerit, on the throat, the kūrma-nāḍī, the light in the head and so on, each yielding a power.

name: Sandhyā (twilight worship)
method_summary: At dawn and dusk: sipping and bathing, sprinkling with the water-verses, breath-control with the Gāyatrī, offering water to the sun (which scatters the Mandeha demons, TA 2.2), and reciting the Sāvitrī standing till sunrise or sitting till the stars appear (YS 1.22–25); the sun is meditated on as Brahman.
alt_method_summary: The daily worship at the junctions of the day by the initiated: purification with water, the sin-effacing verses (RV 10.190), offerings of water to the sun, and repetition of the Gāyatrī.
notes: U01 contribution: its Saṃhitā mantras. The rite's structure is set out in gṛhya/dharma texts (U02).

name: Śāṇḍilya's meditation (Śāṇḍilya-vidyā)
method_summary: In tranquillity, venerate all this as brahman — that from which it arises, into which it dissolves and by which it breathes; form one's resolve, since one becomes on departing what one resolves here; meditate on the self in the heart, made of mind, with breath as body and light as form, smaller than a grain and greater than the worlds, as brahman to be attained on departing, without doubt.
notes: Upaniṣadic 'vidyā' (meditation-knowledge); the Brahma Sūtra (3.3) discusses which vidyās are to be combined.

name: Śāṇḍilya-vidyā (meditation on the self made of mind)
method_summary: Resolving that one becomes at death what one's resolve is, one meditates on the self as made of mind, with breath for body, of the form of light, small as a grain within and greater than all worlds, and resolves to attain it on departing (ŚB 10.6.3; ChU 3.14).

name: Saṅkaṭāsana (the constricted seat)
method_summary: The left leg set on the ground and the right leg wound around the left, with the hands on the knees (GS 2.28).
notes: The e-text wording is terse; details of the leg placement are uncertain.

name: Śaṅkha mudrā (the conch gesture)
method_summary: The left thumb grasped in the right fist, the right thumb extended and the remaining left fingers joined and stretched to touch it — the conch, shown over the arghya vessel (Śāradātilaka ch. 4 commentary; 'śaṅkhamudrāṃ pradarśya' in the arghya rite).

name: Ṣaṇmukhī mudrā (closing the six openings)
method_summary: Closing the ears, eyes, nostrils and mouth with the fingers — in the Śivasaṃhitā the thumbs close the ears, the index fingers the eyes, the middle fingers the nostrils and the ring fingers the mouth — while the breath is restrained, so that the self is seen as light and then the inner sound arises (ŚS 5.22-26; HYP 4.68, where the practice is not named; GS 3.37 within yoni mudrā; Yogacūḍāmaṇi 114-115).
signs_of_progress: the self is seen as light; the sinner is freed; the body is forgotten (ŚS 5.22-24)
a clear, pure sound is heard in the purified suṣumnā (HYP 4.68)
sounds like bells (Yogacūḍāmaṇi 114-115)

warnings.text: It is to be practised secretly (guptācāreṇa).

notes: The name ṣaṇmukhī for HYP 4.68 comes from Brahmānanda's commentary (recalled). U04 filed the same practice as prc:shanmukhi-mudra (non-IAST slug); the two ids should be merged into this one.

name: Renunciation (saṃnyāsa)
method_summary: Rising above the desires for sons, wealth and worlds, living as a mendicant on alms, wandering forth for the sake of the self (BAU 3.5.1, 4.4.22); ascetics purified by the yoga of renunciation (MuU 3.2.6); forest-dwelling with austerity and faith on alms (MuU 1.2.11); after the father-son transfer the recovered father may wander as a mendicant (KauU 2.15).
notes: The rules of the renunciant orders are in the Saṃnyāsa Upaniṣads (U04) and later texts (U57).

name: The renunciation rite (saṃnyāsa-dīkṣā)
method_summary: Penances, śrāddhas (including for oneself), the virajā homa, placing the fires in oneself, the declaration of renunciation said three times, the gift of fearlessness, abandoning topknot and thread (or not, in the Vaiṣṇava rite), receiving staff and cloth, and the teaching of praṇava and great saying.
prerequisites: dispassion; the fourfold means; eligibility; consent of kin (varies by text)

name: Honest household livelihood
method_summary: Living as a householder by one's own craft (Kabīr the weaver, Ravidās the leatherworker, Dādū the cotton-carder), asking only for enough for the family and the visiting sādhu, rather than renouncing or begging.

name: The Sant Mat vows
method_summary: Lacto-vegetarian diet (no meat, fish or eggs), abstention from alcohol and drugs, a moral life, and daily meditation — required of initiates.

warnings.text: Breaking the vows creates karma that holds the soul back.

name: Pacificatory rites (śānti)
method_summary: Rites appeasing portents, planets and harmful powers with the peace hymns.

name: Peace chants (śānti-pāṭha)
method_summary: Reciting peace invocations at the beginning and end of study and rites: 'may we hear with our ears what is auspicious' (RV 1.89.8), 'may Mitra be propitious to us' (1.90.9), 'peace be heaven, peace the atmosphere …' (VS 36.17), 'peaceful be heaven, peaceful the earth' (AVŚ 19.9).

name: Contentment (saṃtoṣa)
method_summary: Not wanting more than the means at hand (YBh 2.32).
signs_of_progress: unsurpassed happiness (2.42)

name: Sapiṇḍīkaraṇa
method_summary: The rite that unites the preta's piṇḍa with those of father, grandfather and great-grandfather, ending the preta state; preferably on the twelfth day, or after three fortnights, six months or a year.
alt_method_summary: The rite that merges the piṇḍa of the newly dead with those of his three forefathers, making the preta a pitṛ (on the twelfth day or at the end of the first year, by different authorities).

name: The seven subtle dhāraṇās (MkP 40)
method_summary: Holding the mind at the head on earth, water, fire, air, space, mind and intellect in turn, experiencing and then abandoning the subtlety of each, without attachment to any.

warnings.text: Attachment to any element's subtlety destroys the yogin and he returns (to rebirth).

name: Recitation of the Devī Māhātmya (Saptaśatī, Caṇḍī-pāṭha)
method_summary: Recitation of the seven hundred verses of the Devī Māhātmya, preceded by its limbs — the Kavaca, Argalā and Kīlaka — with japa of the nine-syllable mantra, and followed by the three 'secrets' (rahasya); especially on the eighth, ninth and fourteenth lunar days and in Navarātri.

name: Taking refuge (śaraṇ)
method_summary: Initiation by a sattrādhikār: the disciple takes refuge in the four real things — the name, Kṛṣṇa, the guru and the devotees — and vows exclusive devotion; open to all castes and peoples.

name: Taking refuge in the Lord alone (śaraṇāgati)
method_summary: Abandoning all dharmas, take refuge in the Lord alone, who frees from all sins (18.66); take refuge in him with one's whole being (18.62); coming once for refuge, saying 'I am yours', one is granted freedom from fear (Rāmāyaṇa 6.18.33).
notes: Interpreted variously by the schools (see dsp:gita-primary-teaching); U05's contribution to a practice systematized by U14.
alt_method_summary: Lineage contribution (Upaniṣadic): 'I, desiring liberation, go for refuge to that God who illumines the understanding of the self' (ŚU 6.18).

The seeker takes refuge in the Lord (or in Śrī) as the sole means, with the resolve to do what pleases him, avoidance of what displeases, faith that he will protect, choosing him as protector, laying down oneself and helplessness; thereafter free of grief and fear, without 'mine' or ego.

Lineage contribution (Āḻvārs): the devotee with no other refuge settles beneath the Lord's feet, naming Śrī who never leaves him (TVM 6.10.10); clings to him though he cause grief (PT 5.1); pleads the unbreakable relation (TP 28); entrusts the hour of death to him in advance (PAT 4.10.1).
Rāmānandī: turning one's face to Rāma, who never abandons one who comes for refuge (Vibhīṣaṇa); Haridāsī: living as Hari keeps one; Ekaśaraṇa: single refuge in Kṛṣṇa.

equivalents.note: Śrīvaiṣṇava prapatti rests on these texts

name: Sarasvatīcālana (moving Sarasvatī)
method_summary: RESTRICTED — summary only: the 'stirring of Sarasvatī', taught with śakticālana as a means of rousing kuṇḍalinī in the (original) Gorakṣaśataka and the Yogakuṇḍalī Upaniṣad, which say it removes abdominal disease. The procedure is not reproduced.
notes: The unit could not verify the procedure's details and deliberately gives none; the Mallinson 'original' Gorakṣaśataka is not available locally.
alt_method_summary: In the 'original' Gorakṣaśataka a practice for arousing the goddess (kuṇḍalinī) in the central channel; summary only, recalled.

name: Renunciation of everything (sarva-tyāga)
method_summary: True renunciation is the giving up of the mind itself, the root of all; outer renunciation of kingdom or belongings does not suffice while the notion 'I renounce' remains.
alt_method_summary: Giving up house, wealth, kin and body-pride at a stroke, as Paṭṭiṉattār did on reading 'even an eyeless needle will not come'; the renouncer-in-mind is highest (Tiruvēkampamālai 1); seeing kin as false (Pattirakiriyār 13).

name: Forgetting everything (Aṣṭāvakra Gītā)
method_summary: Abiding in oneself comes not from studying many scriptures but from forgetting everything.

name: Cultivation of the six virtues (ṣaṭ-sampatti)
method_summary: Practising calm, self-control, withdrawal, forbearance, faith and concentration as auxiliaries of knowledge (BS 3.4.27; BĀU 4.4.23).

name: Receiving the Lord's feet (caṭāri / śaṭhāri)
method_summary: In Śrīvaiṣṇava temples, the priest places on the worshipper's head a crown-like vessel bearing the Lord's feet, called after Śaṭhakopa (Nammāḻvār), who is held to be the Lord's feet — refuge at the feet received through the Āḻvār.
notes: Exact explanation of the name varies; moderate confidence.

name: Recitation of the Śatarudrīya
method_summary: Recitation of the Rudra hymn of the Yajurveda; 'these are the names of immortality' (Jābāla 3); by it one becomes atyāśramin and reaches kaivalya (Kaivalya 2).

name: Piercing the six centres (ṣaṭcakra-bheda) — summary only
method_summary: RESTRICTED. The Ṣaṭcakranirūpaṇa describes rousing kuṇḍalinī by a method learned from the guru and leading her up through the six centres, dissolving each element into the next, to union with Paramaśiva in the thousand-petalled lotus, and back. No steps are recorded.
prerequisites: initiation and instruction by a guru (ṢCN 50, 55)

warnings.text: Only by the method learned from the guru (the text's condition).

name: The six magical acts (ṣaṭkarma)
method_summary: Rites of pacifying, subjugating, paralysing, dissension, driving away and killing, which the Mahāvidyās (especially Bagalāmukhī and Dhūmāvatī) are said to accomplish. Restricted: named only.

warnings.text: Worship without the proper rule is reckoned sorcery (abhicāra) and meets obstacles at every step.

name: The cleansing acts of the Ṣaṭkarmasaṅgraha (group entry)
method_summary: A manual devoted to the cleansing acts and their many variants, with the diseases each is said to cure; its individual acts are not recalled with enough confidence to be entered here.
notes: Group entry; a Phase-D target.

name: Holy company (satsaṅga)
method_summary: Seeking out and serving the holy, hearing the talks that arise in their company; the Yoga Vāsiṣṭha's fourth gatekeeper, the Bhāgavata's means that wins the Lord, the first of the Adhyātma Rāmāyaṇa's nine means.

warnings.text: Bad company (kusaṅg) undoes practice; know the sādhu by conduct, not dress.

signs_of_progress: faith, attraction and devotion arise in order (Kapila Gītā 3.25.25)
alt_method_summary: Lineage contribution (Bhakti Sūtras; Āḻvārs): the company of the great is hard to gain, unfathomable and unfailing, won by the Lord's grace; strive for it alone (NBS 39–42); the Tiruppāvai's girls first wake their companions before going to the Lord (TP 6–15).
Seeking and serving the company of saints: without it no discernment (Tulsī); asked above liberation (Tukārām); Mīrā sat with sādhus against her family; Tyāgarāja salutes all great souls.
Gathering with sants and devotees to sing their songs (bhajan), hear their words and the master's discourse; among Bāuls and Kartābhajās the ākhṛā and melā gatherings with sādhu-sevā.

name: Sattarka: purification of thought by pure reasoning (śākta means)
method_summary: Thought-constructs are purified (vikalpa-saṃskāra) by pure reasoning (sattarka), the teacher's instruction and scripture, repeatedly affirming the pure thought 'I am Śiva, all this is my glory' until it becomes thought-free (TĀ 4; MVT 2.22).

name: Conquest of the mind (sattvāvajaya)
method_summary: Restraining the mind from unwholesome objects; for mental disorder, examining with understanding what is wholesome in dharma, artha and kāma, serving those who know, and cultivating knowledge of self, place, family, time and strength; knowledge, understanding, steadiness, memory and concentration are the medicines of the mind.

name: Sāttvic food
method_summary: Prefer foods that increase life, vitality, strength, health, happiness and cheerfulness, that are savoury, oily, substantial and agreeable; avoid the bitter, sour, salty, very hot, pungent, dry and burning (rājasic) and the stale, tasteless, putrid, leftover and impure (tāmasic) (17.7–10).

name: Relinquishment before action (sāttvika-tyāga)
method_summary: Before any act, relinquishing the sense of agency, of ownership and desire for its fruit: 'the Lord himself, for his own sake, has this done through me'.

name: Truthfulness (satya)
method_summary: Speech and mind according to fact, spoken for the good of all beings after examination (YBh 2.30).
signs_of_progress: actions and their fruits rest on one's word (2.36)

warnings.text: Truth spoken to harm beings is not truth but sin, a semblance of merit leading to painful darkness.

alt_method_summary: Lineage contribution (Upaniṣadic): 'speak the truth' (TU 1.11.1); truth alone conquers (MuU 3.1.6); truthful speech among the priestly gifts (ChU 3.17.4); the truthful is not burned (ChU 6.16).

name: Purity (śauca)
method_summary: Outer purity with earth, water and pure food, and inner washing away of the mind's stains (YBh 2.32).
signs_of_progress: disgust for one's own body, non-contact with others; purity of sattva, cheerfulness, one-pointedness, mastery of the senses, fitness to see the self (2.40–41)

name: Recitation of the Saundaryalaharī
method_summary: Recitation of the hundred verses as praise and worship; popular manuals attach to each verse a yantra, a method of recitation and a fruit.
notes: The verse-by-verse prayoga tradition is recorded from memory; source manuals not identified.

name: Sautrāmaṇī
method_summary: A rite to Indra the good protector (sutrāman) with offerings including surā, performed for healing and restoration.

checks.note: VS 19.1 'svādvīṃ tvā svādunā … indrāya sutrāmṇe pacyasva' opens the sautrāmaṇī — 'VS 19–21' confirmed.

name: Practice seated on a corpse (śava-sādhana)
method_summary: A vīra rite of winning the Goddess's vision seated on a corpse in the cremation ground, as in the account of Sarvānanda. Restricted: named only.

warnings.text: The wilful, the uninitiated, one who drinks the unconsecrated substance, takes a woman by force or kills for his own pleasure, and the addict without Kaula instruction go to hell; the intoxicated Kaula knows neither meditation nor God nor guru and falls.

Aghora practice is given only by the guru and kept secret; the recent teacher Aghoreśvar Bhagavān Rām is reported to have taught that it is naturalness and service, not spectacle (the lineage's oral rule as reported; no text located — to be sourced).

alt_method_summary: A rite seated upon a corpse in the cremation ground, attributed to Aghora and Śākta adepts; recorded only as named.

name: Śavāsana (the corpse; mṛtāsana)
method_summary: Lying supine on the ground like a corpse (HYP 1.32; GS 2.19); the Dattātreyayogaśāstra counts lying like a corpse, relaxed in solitude, among the 'signals' of laya-yoga (DYŚ 22-23).
signs_of_progress: removes fatigue and brings rest to the mind (HYP 1.32; GS 2.19)
notes: Later 'yoga-nidrā' teachings built on this posture belong to recent lineages (U52).

name: Savikalpa samādhi (Vedānta)
method_summary: Absorption with the mental mode resting in Brahman while the distinction of knower and known remains; with inner and outer forms, attended by objects or by words (Dṛg-Dṛśya Viveka).

warnings.text: Relishing its bliss (rasāsvāda) obstructs nirvikalpa samādhi.

name: Seeing the Lord in all beings and bowing to all
method_summary: Regarding every being as the Lord, with equal vision toward brāhmaṇa and outcaste, prostrating even to dog, outcaste, cow and donkey, ignoring others' laughter, until the vision of the Lord in all arises; images are worshipped only until the Lord is known in one's own heart and in all beings.

name: The self-introspection diary
method_summary: Daily written record of failures in non-violence, truthfulness, chastity, love for all and selfless service, and of time given to meditation, introduced by Kirpal Singh.

name: Serving one's parents as dharma
method_summary: The meat-seller serves his aged parents as gods and sends Kauśika home to serve his own (MBh 3.204–206).

name: Closing the senses (ṣaṇmukhī)
method_summary: Closing ears, eyes and other openings with the fingers so that the inner sounds are heard.
signs_of_progress: sounds like bells (Yogacūḍāmaṇi 114–115)

name: Siddhar alchemy (iracavātam: mercury, pāṣāṇam, muppu)
method_summary: Summary only: the Siddhar art of 'binding' mercury, purifying and calcining poisonous minerals and using the secret salt (muppu), both to transmute metals and to make the body deathless; Bogar's Palani image of nine pāṣāṇams is its emblem. No substances, quantities or processes are recorded.

warnings.text: The knowledge is veiled in code language and given only to a proven disciple; unpurified mercury and pāṣāṇam are deadly poison.
All the powers — even transmuting metals and entering another's body — are easier than stilling the mind; the powers are not the goal.
For the true knower who has seen the true thing, kaṟpam and yoga are needless (the means are not the goal).

notes: Restricted (metals/mercury).

name: Siddha daily regimen (nōy aṇukā viti)
method_summary: Rules by which disease does not approach: eat only after the previous meal is digested and in measure (Kuṟaḷ 942, 946); regular oil-baths, moderate sleep, restraint and seasonal adjustment as taught in the verses ascribed to Tēraiyar.
notes: Tēraiyar's specific rules recalled only in outline (low).

name: Seeking and worshipping the guru
method_summary: Seeking the master (āriyaṉ) and bowing at his feet (Pattirakiriyār 26); gazing daily on the guru as the flame of grace and seeing the Lord as the guru (Tirumūla ñāṉam 5–6).

name: Siddhar rites against enemies
method_summary: Summary only: some Siddhar worship-manuals (Rāmatēvar's Pūjāviti 5–7) include rites for striking down an enemy. No procedure recorded.

warnings.text: Is one to curse? Do no cruel deeds.

notes: Restricted (harmful rite).

name: Siddhāsana (the adept's seat)
method_summary: Seated with the heel of one foot pressing the perineum (yonisthāna) and the other foot placed above the genitals, body straight, chin on the chest (a form of jālandhara), senses restrained and the gaze fixed between the brows (HYP 1.35; GS 2.7; ŚS 3.85; GŚ 8). A second arrangement with the left ankle above the genitals is given 'by another view' (HYP 1.36). The texts call it the chief of postures, the one to sit in always.

names.name: vajrāsana / muktāsana / guptāsana (other names reported in HYP 1.37)

signs_of_progress: purifies the 72,000 channels (HYP 1.39)
with it kevala kumbhaka, unmanī and the three locks arise spontaneously (HYP 1.41-42)
practised with moderate diet and meditation on the self for twelve years it brings completion (HYP 1.40)
breaks open the door of liberation (HYP 1.35; GS 2.7)
duration: the HYP (1.40) speaks of twelve years of practice for completion

equivalents.note: HYP 1.37 reports that some call siddhāsana vajrāsana; GS 2.12 describes vajrāsana as a distinct posture.
HYP 1.37 reports the name muktāsana for it; GS 2.11 describes muktāsana separately.
HYP 1.37 reports the name guptāsana for it; GS 2.20 describes guptāsana separately.

notes: Brahmānanda (Jyotsnā on HYP 1.36) calls the first form Matsyendra's and the second that of another school. GŚ numbering per the GRETIL e-text (Kuvalayananda–Shukla).
alt_method_summary: One heel pressed at the perineum, the other foot above the genitals, body straight, senses restrained, gaze fixed between the brows; with the lotus one of the two pre-eminent postures, 'opening the door of liberation'.

name: Concentrations yielding the siddhis (Uddhava Gītā)
method_summary: Kṛṣṇa describes, for each of the eighteen powers, a concentration of the mind on a particular aspect of the Lord; summarized here without the individual procedures.

warnings.text: The siddhis are obstacles and a waste of time for one practising the highest yoga; the goal of yoga is not reached by them.

name: Sīmantonnayana (parting of the hair)
method_summary: A rite in the later months of pregnancy in which the husband parts the wife's hair for her and the child's protection.

name: Siṃhāsana (the lion seat)
method_summary: The ankles placed under the scrotum at the sides of the perineum, crossed (left to the right side, right to the left), the hands on the knees with fingers spread, the mouth open, gazing at the nose-tip (HYP 1.50-52); in the Gheraṇḍa the knees rest on the ground and jālandhara is applied (GS 2.14-15).
signs_of_progress: brings about the three locks (HYP 1.52)
destroys all diseases (GS 2.15)
notes: Yoga Yājñavalkya ch. 3 is recalled (low confidence) to describe eight postures: svastika, gomukha, padma, vīra, siṃha, bhadra, mukta, mayūra.

name: Simran (Sant Mat)
method_summary: Mental repetition of the five (or other) names given at initiation, with attention at the eye centre, to still the mind and gather the attention.
notes: The names are confidential and not recorded.

name: The head-vow (śirovrata)
method_summary: A vow whose performance, 'according to rule', qualifies one to be taught the knowledge of brahman (MuU 3.2.10-11); the text does not describe it.
notes: Commentators differ on its nature; not reconstructed here.

name: Śītalī ('the cooling')
method_summary: The breath is drawn in with the tongue (protruded), held, and released slowly through the nostrils (HYP 2.57-58; GS 5.74-75).
signs_of_progress: destroys gulma, spleen disorders, fever, bile, hunger, thirst and poisons (HYP 2.58)
no indigestion, phlegm or bile (GS 5.75)

warnings.text: As a lion, an elephant or a tiger is tamed only slowly, so the breath must be brought under control gradually; otherwise it kills the practitioner.
Proper breath-control destroys all disease; improper practice produces all disease — hiccup, asthma, cough and pains in the head, ears and eyes arise from the disturbed breath.
Draw the breath in slowly and release it slowly; do not hold it excessively nor release it quickly.

name: Sītkārī ('the hissing')
method_summary: The breath is drawn in through the mouth with the sound 'sīt' and released only through the nose (HYP 2.54-56).
signs_of_progress: one becomes a second god of love, honoured by the circle of yoginīs; no hunger, thirst, sleep or sloth; strength of body (HYP 2.54-56)

warnings.text: As a lion, an elephant or a tiger is tamed only slowly, so the breath must be brought under control gradually; otherwise it kills the practitioner.
Proper breath-control destroys all disease; improper practice produces all disease — hiccup, asthma, cough and pains in the head, ears and eyes arise from the disturbed breath.
Draw the breath in slowly and release it slowly; do not hold it excessively nor release it quickly.

name: Śītkrama bhālabhāti (water through the mouth)
method_summary: Water is sucked in through the mouth with a hissing sound and expelled through the nose (GS 1.59-60).
signs_of_progress: one becomes like the god of love; no old age or fever; the body free; phlegm disorders removed (GS 1.59-60)

name: Recitation of Śiva mantras
method_summary: Recitation of Śiva's five- or six-syllable mantra and of Dakṣiṇāmūrti's mantras (Pañcabrahma; Bhasmajābāla; Dakṣiṇāmūrti).

name: Recitation of the thousand names of Śiva (Mahābhārata)
method_summary: Reciting the thousand names of Śiva that Upamanyu taught Kṛṣṇa (MBh 13.14–17).

name: Śivānubhava — shared discourse on experience
method_summary: Devotees gather to speak from and test their experience of Śiva in dialogue, as the śaraṇas did in the Anubhava Maṇṭapa; continued in modern maṭhas as 'śivānubhava' gatherings.

name: The Śivarātri vow
method_summary: Fast and night-long vigil with worship of the liṅga on Śiva's night; the hunter who kept it unknowingly was saved.

name: Śivayoga-samādhi
method_summary: Through inner worship, meditation on Śiva as one's self: the supreme self is contemplated in the haṃsa form with the feeling 'I am He' until attention is undivided; the six centres are contemplated from the base to the brows and Śambhu in the aperture called Kailāsa within the thousand-petalled lotus.

warnings.text: The breath element (meeting of prāṇa and apāna) is done on the teacher's instruction (commentary on 12.6); no method is recorded here.

name: The sixty-four limbs of devotional practice
method_summary: Rūpa's list of practices: the first ten (taking shelter of a guru, initiation and instruction, serving the guru with trust, following the saints, inquiring into true dharma, renouncing enjoyment for Kṛṣṇa, residence at holy places, accepting only what is needed, honouring Ekādaśī, honouring the sacred trees, cows and brāhmaṇas) and ten avoidances (of non-devotees' company, many disciples, great undertakings, many books for argument, miserliness, grief, disrespect of other gods, harming beings, offences in worship and to the name, tolerating blasphemy) are the gateway; then hearing, chanting, remembering, worship, bowing, prayer, service, friendship, self-offering, wearing Vaiṣṇava marks, honouring prasāda, tulasī, festivals and more, ending with the five most potent limbs.
notes: The full list of sixty-four is recalled only in part; verse-by-verse list to be extracted in Phase D.

name: Constant remembrance of the Lord (smaraṇa)
method_summary: Remember the Lord at all times, with mind and intellect fixed on him, even while acting (8.7); the yogin who remembers him constantly with undivided mind finds him easily attained (8.14).
alt_method_summary: Lineage contribution (Bhakti Sūtras; Āḻvārs; Gīta Govinda): worshipping the Lord at all times with one's whole being (NBS 79); forgetting him is supreme anguish (NBS 19); remembrance is one of love's eleven forms (NBS 82). Because at death remembrance may fail, the Āḻvārs place the mind at the Lord's feet now and entrust the hour of death to him (Mukundamālā; PAT 4.10.1). The Gīta Govinda is offered to minds that delight in remembering Hari (GG 1.3).

name: Cremation-ground practice (śmaśāna-sādhana)
method_summary: Night worship of Kālī/Tārā by the vīra in the cremation ground, praised in the Karpūrādistotra and practised at Tārāpīṭh. Restricted: summary only.

warnings.text: Kaula texts reserve such rites for the initiated vīra and condemn the wilful (Kulārṇava 5.96-105).

equivalents.note: the Pāśupata dwelling in the cremation ground (U17)

name: Dwelling in the cremation ground
method_summary: In the fourth stage he lives in the cremation ground, in the open or at the foot of a tree, not leaving it until the body falls, living on what comes unasked, practising remembrance.
signs_of_progress: union with Rudra (the stated gain)

name: Satyakāma's meditation on the four quarters of brahman
method_summary: Venerate brahman as having four quarters of four parts each — the quarters of space ('shining'), earth, mid-space, sky and ocean ('endless'), fire, sun, moon and lightning ('luminous'), breath, sight, hearing and mind ('having an abode') — as taught to Satyakāma by a bull, fire, a goose and a diver-bird.
notes: Names of the quarters from memory (moderate). Upaniṣadic 'vidyā' (meditation-knowledge); the Brahma Sūtra (3.3) discusses which vidyās are to be combined.

name: Sopāśraya (sitting with a support)
method_summary: Named among the examples of posture in Vyāsa's bhāṣya on YS 2.46 ('posture is steady and comfortable'). The bhāṣya gives only the name; its form is explained by the commentators (Vācaspati Miśra, Vijñānabhikṣu and others), whose descriptions are not reproduced here.
notes: Name certain; form per commentators not recalled with confidence.

name: Spanda awareness
method_summary: Being constantly intent on discerning the spanda principle, one attains one's own nature even while awake; spanda is to be grasped in intense states (great anger, joy, perplexity, running) and in the opening (unmeṣa) from which a new thought arises in one absorbed in a single thought (SK 1.21-22, 3.9).

warnings.text: Light, sound, form and taste that arise from the unmeṣa agitate the embodied (read as a caution against distraction by them).
A void, sleep-like absorption is artificial and not the principle (SK 1.12-13).

name: Feigned trembling (spandana)
method_summary: He deliberately shakes his limbs as if struck by a wind-disorder.

warnings.text: Undertaken only after knowledge has been gained, impurity reduced and the teacher's permission obtained; the feigned acts must not conflict with the restraints (non-harming, celibacy etc.).

name: Śrāddha
method_summary: Rites of faith for the dead and the ancestors - ekoddiṣṭa for the preta, the sixteen śrāddhas, monthly and annual rites, pārvaṇa for the three ancestors - with feeding of brahmins; they feed the dead on Yama's road and satisfy the ancestors.

name: Śrāddha (offering to the ancestors)
method_summary: Qualified brāhmaṇas are invited and fed as the ancestors' representatives, rice-balls (piṇḍa) are offered to the father, grandfather and great-grandfather, and water and sesame given; performed monthly at the new moon and on death-anniversaries and other occasions (MDh 3.122–286).

name: The śrauta sacrifice (in general)
method_summary: Solemn rites performed in three fires (gārhapatya, āhavanīya, dakṣiṇāgni) by priests of the Vedas — hotṛ (Ṛgveda), adhvaryu (Yajurveda), udgātṛ (Sāmaveda) and brahmán (overseer), up to sixteen in the great soma rites — for a patron (yajamāna) and his wife, with oblations, recitations, chants and gifts (dakṣiṇā).
prerequisites: initiated householder, married, who has established the fires

name: Hearing the scriptures (śravaṇa)
method_summary: Study of scripture and its right interpretation under a teacher. In Dvaita: hearing the true scriptures (Vedas, Mahābhārata, Pañcarātra, Purāṇas) with Madhva's commentaries so as to know Viṣṇu's supremacy, the five differences and gradation; the first principal means to knowledge, never to be curtailed.
stage: all (the lowest adhikārin qualifies by study and devotion)
prerequisites: devotion to Viṣṇu
a qualified teacher
eligibility by class and qualities (adhikāra)
sādhana-catuṣṭaya
a teacher (śrotriya, brahmaniṣṭha)
alt_method_summary: Systematic study of the Upaniṣads (with the Gītā and Brahma Sūtras) under a qualified teacher, determining by the six marks of purport that their meaning is the non-dual Brahman; for the Vivaraṇa the principal means, for one of sharp understanding sufficient by itself.
Lineage contribution (Upaniṣadic): 'the self should be seen, heard, reflected upon and meditated upon'; hearing is the second of the four verbs (BAU 2.4.5, 4.5.6).
signs_of_progress: doubt about what scripture teaches is removed (pramāṇa-saṃśaya)

name: Hearing the Lord's names, qualities and deeds (śravaṇa)
method_summary: Listening to the names, qualities, deeds and stories of the Lord — from the Bhāgavata and the epics, from devotees and in kathā — with love. First of the Bhāgavata's nine forms (BhP 7.5.23); with singing, a means to devotion even for those living in the world (NBS 37); Garga defines devotion as attachment to hearing his stories (NBS 17); the love of Rāma's stories is the second of the nine in the Rāmāyaṇa tradition.
stage: all; the first of the nine
signs_of_progress: the inauspicious in the heart is shaken off and steady devotion arises (BhP 1.2.16–21)

warnings.text: Stories of lust, wealth, unbelievers and enemies are not to be listened to.

equivalents.note: hearing the Purāṇa recited is the chief form of bhakti-hearing
Vedāntic śravaṇa is study of the Upaniṣads for knowledge of Brahman; bhakti śravaṇa is hearing of the Lord's deeds and names out of love — same word, different object and purpose

notes: One of the Bhāgavata's nine forms of devotion (prc:navadha-bhakti, U07). Exemplar in the tradition's list: Parīkṣit (cpt:nine-exemplars-of-devotion).

name: Offering to the deity's attendants (śrībhūtabali)
method_summary: Offering of cooked rice on the stones of the deity's attendant beings and guardians placed around the shrine, with the festival image carried in procession.

name: Contemplation of the body as the Śrīcakra
method_summary: The body's openings, channels, winds and faculties contemplated as the enclosures and deities of the Śrīcakra; worship as contemplation of non-difference (Bhāvanā; Tripurā).

name: Worship of the nine enclosures of the Śrīcakra (navāvaraṇa-pūjā)
method_summary: After the preliminaries (Gaṇapati worship, purification, placements on the body, preparation of the special water), the Goddess is invoked into the central point and the deities of the nine enclosures are worshipped from the outer square inward — each enclosure with its presiding goddess, class of yoginīs, attendant deities and mudrā — followed by the sixty-four services, libations into the bindu, japa and the offering of all to the Goddess. The Yoginīhṛdaya calls this cakra-worship 'aparā', performed even by Śiva; the Samaya school performs it only inwardly. (Summary; no mantras recorded.)
prerequisites: initiation (dīkṣā) from a qualified guru into the relevant vidyā

warnings.text: Those without the succession of teachers, proud of mere knowledge, are harmed by the mantra's rays through their breach of the samaya.
The Kaula worship is to be done in secret; making it public leads to hell.
Outer worship on a physical support is rejected by the Samayins, who worship only in the heart-space.

equivalents.note: outer and inner forms of the same worship

name: Śrīvidyā initiation (śāktī, śāmbhavī, māntrī)
method_summary: The guru, after his own worship, purifies the blindfolded disciple with the special water, contemplates the red and white feet on his head and a wave of light burning away his bonds, bathes him from a consecrated vessel, places the letters on his body, whispers the Bālā mantra and then the chosen mantra, gives his own pādukā and a name ending in '-ānandanātha', teaches the rules of conduct and makes the disciple his own self (PKS 1.34-43). Summary only.

name: Fire offering in Śrīvidyā
method_summary: The fire rite: preparation of the fire and offerings to the Goddess and her retinue. Taught in section 9 of the Paraśurāma Kalpasūtra. (Summary; no mantras.)
prerequisites: initiation (dīkṣā) from a qualified guru into the relevant vidyā

name: Japa of the Śrīvidyā mantra
method_summary: Repetition of the fifteen- or sixteen-syllable mantra received at initiation, with attention to its subtle final phases and its meanings; the Varivasyārahasya insists that japa without knowledge of meaning bears no fruit. (No syllables recorded.)
prerequisites: initiation (dīkṣā) from a qualified guru into the relevant vidyā

warnings.text: Recitation without knowing the meaning bears no fruit and may do harm.
Those without the succession of teachers, proud of mere knowledge, are harmed by the mantra's rays through their breach of the samaya.

name: The ten mudrās of Śrīvidyā worship
method_summary: Ten hand-seals shown in the worship of the Śrīcakra, one for each enclosure (sarvasaṃkṣobhiṇī to sarvayoni) and the tenth, trikhaṇḍā. (Names only; forms not described.)

name: The daily routine of the Śrīvidyā initiate
method_summary: Rising before dawn, contemplating the guru's feet in the crown with nectar flooding the body, meditating on Gaṇapati in the heart, the morning ablutions and offerings, libations, and the day's worship (PKS 2.2); constant holding of the vidyā and immersion in Śiva-hood (PKS 1.17-18).

name: Placements on the body (nyāsa) in Śrīvidyā
method_summary: Placing of mantras and deities on the body before worship: the purification of the hands, the eight goddesses of speech on head, forehead, brows, throat, heart, navel, genitals and base, the mātṛkā, the great sixfold placement and others, by which the worshipper becomes the deity's body. (Summary; no mantras.)
prerequisites: initiation (dīkṣā) from a qualified guru into the relevant vidyā

name: Keeping the initiate's conduct (samaya)
method_summary: Observing the rules of the Kalpasūtra: no censure of other schools or persons, secrecy, constant remembrance of the vidyā, avoidance of the six passions, unsanctioned violence and theft, one guru, non-possessiveness, action without regard to fruit, fearlessness; outwardly Śaiva and among people Vaiṣṇava (Kaula Upaniṣad).

warnings.text: Those without the succession of teachers, proud of mere knowledge, are harmed by the mantra's rays through their breach of the samaya.

name: Feigned amorous gestures (śṛṅgāraṇa)
method_summary: Standing at a distance from a group of women, he looks at one young woman and makes signs of desire such as arranging his hair, so as to be called unchaste; the act is a pretence.

warnings.text: Undertaken only after knowledge has been gained, impurity reduced and the teacher's permission obtained; the feigned acts must not conflict with the restraints (non-harming, celibacy etc.).

name: Sthānakalpanā: positing places (breath, body, outer)
method_summary: The lowest āṇava support: positing the divine in 'places' - in the breath and its time-cycles (TĀ 6), in the body, and in outer supports such as the liṅga or maṇḍala.

name: Veneration of sanctified places
method_summary: Visiting and worshipping at places the incarnations visited and venerating objects associated with them.

name: Sthirasukha (the steady-and-comfortable)
method_summary: Named among the examples of posture in Vyāsa's bhāṣya on YS 2.46 ('posture is steady and comfortable'). The bhāṣya gives only the name; its form is explained by the commentators (Vācaspati Miśra, Vijñānabhikṣu and others), whose descriptions are not reproduced here.
notes: Name certain; form per commentators not recalled with confidence.

name: Recitation of the tradition's hymns
method_summary: Daily recitation of Madhva's Dvādaśastotra and Narasiṃhanakhastuti and Trivikrama's Vāyustuti (framed by the Narasiṃha verses); in the Rāghavendra tradition, the Rāghavendra hymn.
alt_method_summary: Rāmānandī and wider north Indian practice: daily recitation of the Hanumān Cālīsā and passages of the Mānas.

name: Holding the mind on the auspicious support (VP 6.7)
method_summary: With breath and senses mastered, fix the mind on Viṣṇu's form as the ground of all powers, simplifying it stage by stage, until dhyāna (a single continuous flow) and samādhi (grasping the object's own nature free of imagination) arise.

name: Sukhāsana (the comfortable seat)
method_summary: A comfortable seated posture: in the Śivasaṃhitā the name is given to svastika (ŚS 3.97); the Gheraṇḍa has sagarbha breath-control done 'seated in sukhāsana' (GS 5.49); the Darśana and Triśikhibrāhmaṇa Upaniṣads list sukha among their postures.

name: Dwelling in an empty house or cave
method_summary: In the stage of conquest he lives in an empty house or cave free from distraction, constantly with the god, senses conquered, studying and meditating.
duration: six months of constant yoga are named for the powers to arise (PS 5.12-13)
signs_of_progress: powers such as distant sight arise gradually

name: Worship of the deity in a pot of liquor (reported)
method_summary: Summary only: opponents report that the Kālāmukhas set up a pot of liquor and worship the deity placed in it.

name: Surat-śabd yoga (the yoga of the sound current)
method_summary: Given only at initiation by a living master: the attention is withdrawn from the body and gathered at the eye centre by simran, held there by dhyān of the master's form, and joined to the inner sound (bhajan), which draws the soul up through the inner regions; practised daily (two and a half hours in the Beas line) with the vows.
prerequisites: initiation (nām-dān)
the four vows
signs_of_progress: attention gathering at the eye centre
inner light (stars, moon, sun) and the radiant form of the master
sounds of the regions (bell and conch first)

warnings.text: Without a living master and initiation the practice is not to be attempted; the lower centres and kuṇḍalinī are not to be worked on.
Inner lights and sounds are not to be sought for their own sake or spoken of; the disciple should not display powers.

equivalents.note: Both are absorption in the inner sound; surat-śabd yoga adds the master's form, the names and the regional cosmology.

name: Sūryabhedana ('piercing the sun')
method_summary: RESTRICTED (extreme retention) — summary only: breath drawn in slowly through the right (sun) channel, held with the locks, and released through the left (HYP 2.48-50; GS 5.59-69). The texts set the limit of the retention at an extreme point, which is not reproduced. The Gheraṇḍa sets the practice in the context of the ten breaths and their seats (GS 5.61-65).
signs_of_progress: cleanses the skull, destroys disorders of wind and of worms (HYP 2.50)
destroys old age and death, awakens kuṇḍalinī, increases the bodily fire (GS 5.68-69)

warnings.text: As a lion, an elephant or a tiger is tamed only slowly, so the breath must be brought under control gradually; otherwise it kills the practitioner.
Proper breath-control destroys all disease; improper practice produces all disease — hiccup, asthma, cough and pains in the head, ears and eyes arise from the disturbed breath.
Draw the breath in slowly and release it slowly; do not hold it excessively nor release it quickly.
Breath-control is to be practised by the path the guru teaches, once posture is firm and the diet wholesome and moderate.

name: Śuṣka-basti (the dry basti)
method_summary: Done on the ground in paścimatāna, moving (the belly) slowly and contracting and expanding the anus with aśvinī mudrā (GS 1.48-49).
signs_of_progress: no bowel disorders; increased digestive fire; destroys āmavāta (GS 1.49)

name: Worship of married women (suvāsinī-pūjā)
method_summary: Married women are honoured as the Goddess, who 'is pleased by the worship of suvāsinīs' (LSN 178).

name: Performing one's own dharma (svadharma)
method_summary: Look to one's own dharma and do not waver: for a kṣatriya, fight a battle that accords with dharma (2.31); perform one's own dharma even if imperfectly rather than another's well (3.35).

warnings.text: Abandoning one's own dharma incurs sin and disgrace (2.33–36); another's dharma brings fear (3.35).

name: Self-study (svādhyāya)
method_summary: Repetition of the praṇava and other purifying formulas, or study of scriptures on liberation (YBh 2.1, 2.32); repetition of mantras preceded by the praṇava (RM 2.1).
signs_of_progress: contact with the chosen deity; gods, sages and siddhas appear (2.44, YBh 2.44)
alt_method_summary: Daily recitation of one's Veda, at least a portion, as the sacrifice to Brahman (ŚB 11.5.6.3; TA 2.10); it brings concentration, independence, sound sleep and delight in the one thing (ŚB 11.5.7.1).
Lineage contribution (Upaniṣadic): every duty is to be joined with study and teaching of the Veda; 'study and teaching alone, for that is austerity' (TU 1.9); 'do not neglect your study' (TU 1.11).

warnings.text: Recitation is suspended on the prescribed non-study occasions (anadhyāya).

name: Performing one's own duty (svakarma)
method_summary: One's own duty is performing the acts enjoined for one's stage of life; with concentration and posture it supports meditation (SS 3.32, 3.35).

name: Support in the knowledge of dream and sleep (1.38)
method_summary: Letting the mind rest on the knowledge of dream or of sleep as its support, taking that form (1.38, YBh 1.38).

name: Svara practice: attending to the flow of breath in the nostrils (svarodaya)
