method_summary: The practice of the Śiva Svarodaya: noting which channel the breath is flowing in — iḍā (left, moon), piṅgalā (right, sun) or suṣumnā (both) — as the flows alternate through the day, and timing actions accordingly: steady and auspicious acts when the moon flows, active and harsh acts when the sun flows, and only meditation and yoga when the suṣumnā flows, since worldly acts then fail. The text treats this knowledge as most secret and also teaches ways of changing the flow (not detailed here).
notes: Verse numbers of the Śiva Svarodaya not recalled; sources cite U28's topic-level teachings.

name: Discerning the elements in the breath (tattva in svara)
method_summary: Within each nostril-flow the five elements (earth, water, fire, air, space) arise in turn; the Śiva Svarodaya teaches how to recognise the element present by the length, direction, colour and taste (and shape) of the breath, and uses this knowledge, with the flows, to foretell outcomes, illness and the approach of death.
notes: Specific lengths and correspondences are not reproduced; recalled only in outline.

name: Svastikāsana (the auspicious-mark seat)
method_summary: Both soles placed between the knees and thighs, sitting with the body straight (HYP 1.19; GS 2.13; ŚS 3.95). The Śivasaṃhitā calls it the comfortable posture (sukhāsana).
signs_of_progress: no disease enters the body and the breath is mastered (ŚS 3.96)

equivalents.note: ŚS 3.97 calls svastika sukhāsana; the Darśana and Triśikhibrāhmaṇa list sukha separately.

notes: Yoga Yājñavalkya ch. 3 is recalled (low confidence) to describe eight postures: svastika, gomukha, padma, vīra, siṃha, bhadra, mukta, mayūra.

name: Dwelling on one's own nature (svasvarūpānusandhāna) as devotion
method_summary: Devotion understood as continuous attention to one's own true nature (VC 31), the chief among the means to liberation.

name: The yoga of the Śvetāśvatara (posture, breath, place)
method_summary: Hold the body steady with chest, neck and head erect; draw the senses with the mind into the heart; restrain the breaths, with movements controlled, and breathe out gently through the nose when the breath is diminished; hold the mind attentively like a chariot yoked to unruly horses; practise in a level, clean place free of pebbles, fire, sand, noise and damp, pleasing to the mind and sheltered from wind.
prerequisites: the invocations of Savitṛ to yoke the mind (ŚU 2.1-7)
signs_of_progress: forms like fog, smoke, sun, wind, fire, fireflies, lightning, crystal and moon precede brahman's manifestation; lightness, health, freedom from craving, clear complexion, pleasant voice and smell, scant excreta (ŚU 2.11-13)

warnings.text: The place must be free of disturbances (pebbles, fire, sand, noise, water-places) and not offend the eye (ŚU 2.10).
The breath is to be let out gently through the nose when diminished (ŚU 2.9).

name: Worship of Śyāmā (Mantriṇī)
method_summary: Worship of Śyāmā/Rājamātaṅgī, Lalitā's minister, with her own cakra and enclosures. Taught in section 6 of the Paraśurāma Kalpasūtra. (Summary; no mantras.)
prerequisites: initiation (dīkṣā) from a qualified guru into the relevant vidyā

name: Singing Śyāmā-saṅgīt
method_summary: Devotional singing of the songs of Rāmprasād, Kamalākānta and their successors to Kālī and Umā, alone or in gatherings, as a way of relating to the Mother.

name: Śyena (a sorcery rite)
method_summary: A rite the Veda states as the means for one who wishes to harm an enemy. Mīmāṃsā records it only to show that the Veda does not enjoin harming: the rite is described as a means, not as a duty.

warnings.text: The Śyena and similar rites (Vajra, Iṣu) are harmful (anartha): their aim is violence, violence is prohibited, and they lead to sin (pratyavāya); they are not dharma.

notes: Summary only (abhicāra rite).

name: Taḍāgī mudrā ('the tank')
method_summary: In paścimatāna, the belly is drawn back and hollowed so that it is shaped like a tank (GS 3.61).
signs_of_progress: destroys old age and death (GS 3.61)

name: Offering all conduct to the Lord (tad-arpitākhilācāratā)
method_summary: Dedicating every action to the Lord (Nārada's own definition of devotion, NBS 19); having so offered all conduct, even desire, anger and pride are to be turned toward him alone (NBS 65); until love is attained, action continues with its fruit given up (NBS 62).

equivalents.note: the Gītā's offering of all acts to the Lord (BhG 9.27)

name: Austerity (tapas)
method_summary: Bearing the pairs of opposites — hunger and thirst, cold and heat, standing and sitting, silence — with vows as suitable (YBh 2.32); it breaks up impurity, without which yoga does not succeed (YBh 2.1). Summary only: the fasting vows the bhāṣya names (kṛcchra, cāndrāyaṇa, sāntapana) are not described here.
signs_of_progress: perfection of body and senses through the destruction of impurity (2.43)

warnings.text: It should be practised so as not to disturb the clarity of the mind (tac ca cittaprasādanam abādhamānam anenāsevyam).
Lopāmudrā's complaint that many autumns of toil wear away the body, and the resolution that tapas and married life together bear fruit, are the Saṃhitā's own counterweight to one-sided austerity.
Rites and austerities performed without knowing the imperishable come to an end (BAU 3.8.10).

notes: Marked restricted because it includes prolonged fasting vows; summary and the text's own warning only.
alt_method_summary: Ascetic exertion that 'heats' the practitioner: by it the ancients reached heaven, the seers were born, the student fills the worlds; the Vrātya stands upright for a year; the unheated cannot attain soma.

Lineage contribution (Upaniṣadic): Bhṛgu seeks brahman by tapas (TU 3.1-6); a year of austerity, celibacy and faith before questioning (PrU 1.2); the self is found by truth and austerity (MuU 3.1.5; ŚU 1.15); austerity as a branch of dharma (ChU 2.23.1).
Enduring pain and harming none (Kuṟaḷ ch. 27).
alt_notes: Extreme austerities are not described in method; none of the Saṃhitā passages gives steps.

name: Wearing Viṣṇu's heated emblems (tapta-mudrā-dhāraṇa)
method_summary: Summary only: the Mādhva tradition marks the body with Viṣṇu's discus and conch emblems, either heated or in clay; heated emblems are received at set times of the year and at the thread ceremony in the presence of the maṭha's head.
notes: Restricted: involves marking the body with heated metal; no procedure recorded. Its legitimacy was contested by Smārta critics and defended by Mādhva authors (a work 'Cakramīmāṃsā' is ascribed to Vijayīndra) — recalled at low confidence.

name: Tāraka-yoga
method_summary: Meditation on the 'crossing' light between the brows through the three targets and the voids, proceeding from tāraka with form to tāraka without form and to the mind-less (amanaska) state.
prerequisites: renouncer endowed with the six qualities (Advayatāraka)

name: Discriminating the principles (Sāṃkhya in the Mokṣadharma)
method_summary: Enumerating the twenty-four principles of prakṛti and knowing the twenty-fifth as other than them, the knower awakens and becomes alone (MBh 12.294); knowing the faults of body, senses and guṇas, the Sāṃkhya follower is freed (12.290).

name: Repeated practice of the principles (tattvābhyāsa)
method_summary: After hearing the principles (manifest, unmanifest, knower) from scripture and teacher and establishing them by reasoning, one contemplates them repeatedly — long, reverently and without interruption — discriminating puruṣa from each principle and renouncing identification with each ('not this, not this'), until the knowledge 'I am not, not mine, not I' arises.
prerequisites: hearing and reasoning about the twenty-five principles; dispassion
duration: long and uninterrupted; Vācaspati speaks of many births of practice
signs_of_progress: the complete, pure, single knowledge 'I am not, not mine, not I' (SK 64); prakṛti seen as by a spectator, having ceased (SK 65–66)

warnings.text: Liberation is not attained by mere hearing, because beginningless latent tendencies are strong.
Dispassion without discrimination leads only to absorption in prakṛti, from which one rises again.

equivalents.note: long uninterrupted contemplation after hearing and reflection, as in Advaita's nididhyāsana; content and goal differ (discrimination vs identity)

name: Temple-building rites from ploughing to installation (karṣaṇādi)
method_summary: Examination and taking possession of the site, ploughing (karṣaṇa), sprouting seeds, laying out the ground-plan (vāstu-maṇḍala), offerings to the site deities, deposit of the foundation (garbhanyāsa), and rites at each stage of construction up to installation; the Kāmika's Pūrvabhāga devotes many chapters to them.
notes: U58 owns Vāstu/Śilpa; here the ritual frame.

name: The three gifts (sopādhi, nirupādhi, sahaja dāna)
method_summary: Giving with a purpose, giving without a purpose, and innate (natural) giving — the last three sub-sthalas of the bhakta-sthala; skill in pure, innate giving marks the passage to māheśvara.

name: Keeping the three supports of life
method_summary: Right use of food, sleep and continence, by which the body is upheld as a house by its pillars.

name: Austerity of body, speech and mind
method_summary: Bodily austerity: worship of gods, the twice-born, teachers and the wise; purity, uprightness, celibacy, non-harm. Verbal: speech that does not agitate, true, pleasant and beneficial, and recitation of scripture. Mental: serenity, gentleness, silence, self-restraint, purity of being — practised with faith and without desire for fruit (17.14–17).

warnings.text: Terrible austerities not enjoined by scripture, done with hypocrisy and egoism, tormenting the elements of the body and the Lord within, are demonic.
Austerity done with foolish obstinacy, by torturing oneself or to harm another, is tāmasic.

name: Pilgrimage (tīrthāṭana)
method_summary: Visiting sacred places: the Goddess's seats listed in the Devī Gītā, and pilgrimage among the Uddhava Gītā's niyamas; the Avadhūta Gītā's apology notes that pilgrimage presupposes a limit to the all-pervading.

name: Pilgrimage to tīrthas
method_summary: Journeying to holy places, bathing, worship, gifts and śrāddha there; seven cities give liberation; the inner meaning is purity of mind and the company of the holy, who themselves make places holy.

warnings.text: The greedy, cruel and hypocritical remain impure though they bathe in every tīrtha.

alt_method_summary: The Āraṇyakaparvan's pilgrimage to the tīrthas; Vidura's inner reading: the self is a river whose fords are sacred, whose water is truth, banks steadfastness and waves self-restraint — bathing in it purifies (MBh 5.40.19).
Vārkarī: pilgrimage is valued, but the saints' company and Viṭṭhala's feet are the true tīrtha (Nāmdev's Tīrthāvaḷī).
notes: U05's contribution; the Āraṇyaka's tīrtha lists are not itemized here.

name: Tirumūlar's eightfold yoga
method_summary: The eight limbs (iyamam, niyamam, ātaṉam, pirāṇāyāmam, pirattiyākāram, tāraṇai, tiyāṉam, camāti — TM 552), commended by the Siddhar poets (Kaṭuveḷi 31).
notes: U22 contribution (lineage) to U18's entry.
alt_method_summary: Tirumūlar's eight limbs — restraints, observances, posture, breath control, withdrawal, holding, meditation, absorption — taught to preserve the body as the vessel of realization and to reach Śiva within; summary only.

warnings.text: Breath retention and advanced practices are to be learned only from a guru (general teaching of the text; specific verses not recorded here).

name: Recitation and contemplation of the tirumantra
method_summary: Lineage contribution (Āḻvārs): Tirumaṅkai, given the eight-syllable mantra by the Lord himself (the tradition's account), sang that he had searched and found the name 'Nārāyaṇa', which gives every good (PTM 1.1).
alt_method_summary: Repetition of 'oṃ namo nārāyaṇāya', received at initiation, with contemplation of its meaning: the soul belongs to the Lord alone, not to itself, and seeks only his service.

name: Singing the Tirumuṟai (paṇṇicai)
method_summary: Singing the Tēvāram and other Tirumuṟai hymns in their melodic modes during temple worship and at home; the ōtuvār's office.

name: Awakening the Lord at dawn (tiruppaḷḷiyeḻucci)
method_summary: At dawn the Lord in the temple is roused with song — the sun has risen, the gods and sages wait at his door — and the singer asks to be made servant of his servants. Toṇṭaraṭippoṭi's ten verses are sung daily at Śrīraṅgam and other Śrīvaiṣṇava temples.
notes: Cf. the Sanskrit suprabhātam (src:venkatesa-suprabhatam, U14) and the Śaiva Tiruppaḷḷiyeḻucci of Māṇikkavācakar (U18).

name: The Mārkaḻi vow of the Tiruppāvai (pāvai nōṉpu)
method_summary: In the month of Mārkaḻi the girls rise before dawn, wake one another, bathe, and go singing the Lord's names to his house; during the vow they take no ghee or milk, wear no kohl or flowers, do nothing forbidden, speak no evil, and give alms; they worship with pure flowers, singing and meditation. In the tradition the Tiruppāvai's thirty verses are sung daily throughout Mārkaḻi, one for each day, in temples and homes.
duration: the month of Mārkaḻi (mid-December to mid-January)

equivalents.note: the Śaiva Mārkaḻi dawn vow of Māṇikkavācakar's Tiruvempāvai

notes: The dietary abstentions are a vow of restraint, not a prolonged fast.

name: Daily home worship of the Lord (tiruvārādhanam)
method_summary: Worship of the Lord's image (arcā) at home each day, with purification, meditation on the teachers, offerings of water, flowers, food, recitation and prostration, done as service and not for any fruit.

name: The Mārkaḻi dawn vow (Tiruvempāvai nōṉpu)
method_summary: In the month of Mārkaḻi, rising before dawn, bathing and singing the Tiruvempāvai and Tiruppaḷḷiyeḻucci.

name: Worship of the Nityā of the lunar day
method_summary: Worship of the Nityā presiding over the current lunar day, the Nityās being the phases of time (Tantrarāja; Bhāvanā Upaniṣad). Summary only.

name: Enduring the sense-contacts (titikṣā)
method_summary: The contacts of the senses give cold and heat, pleasure and pain; they come and go and are impermanent — endure them (2.14). The one they do not disturb is fit for immortality (2.15).
prerequisites: seeing that the sense-contacts are impermanent (2.14)
signs_of_progress: not being disturbed by them; sameness in pleasure and pain (2.15)

name: Tokkaṇam (Siddha therapeutic massage)
method_summary: Therapeutic massage and manipulation, one of the external treatments of Siddha medicine, practised in several named kinds. No techniques recorded.

name: Trāṭaka (the fixed gaze)
method_summary: With steady eyes and concentrated mind, one gazes without blinking at a small target until tears fall (HYP 2.31; GS 1.53). Listed by the texts among the six acts, it is also a practice of concentration: in the Gheraṇḍa it leads to śāmbhavī (GS 1.54).
signs_of_progress: frees from eye diseases and bars sloth (HYP 2.32)
śāmbhavī arises; no eye disease; divine sight (GS 1.54)

warnings.text: To be guarded as carefully as a golden casket.
One with excess fat or phlegm should first practise the six acts; others should not do them, their doṣas being in balance.

notes: The texts name only a 'small target' (sūkṣma-lakṣya); gazing at a candle flame is later usage (recent teachers).

name: Tripuṇḍra (three lines of ash)
method_summary: Ash taken with the five brahma-mantras and applied in three horizontal lines, each line standing for a fire, a letter of Oṃ, a guṇa, a world, a power, a Veda and a deity (Kālāgnirudra); for all four stages of life.

name: Worship with the Triśatī
method_summary: Worship offering vermilion with each of the three hundred names of the Triśatī, which together unfold the fifteen syllables of the mantra.

name: Taking the tuḷsī necklace (Vārkarī initiation)
method_summary: A senior Vārkarī places the tuḷsī-bead necklace (māḷ) on the new member, who vows to keep the vārī, to be vegetarian and abstain from intoxicants, to observe ekādaśī and to remember the name.

name: Service of tulasī
method_summary: Watering, circumambulating and worshipping the tulasī plant, beloved of Kṛṣṇa, and wearing and chanting on tulasī beads.

name: Sleeping without sleeping (Śiva-yoga sleep)
method_summary: Remaining in the unceasing 'sleep of Śiva-yoga', senses withdrawn and awareness awake (Pattirakiriyār 1–2; Kuṭampai 6).

equivalents.note: sleep-like state kept aware; different texts and methods

name: Uccāra: contemplation of the breath (āṇava means)
method_summary: Āṇava contemplation of the vital breath in its five forms as it moves between the heart, the object and the dvādaśānta, recognizing seven successive blisses - one's own, the bliss-less, supreme, Brahman's, great, of consciousness and of the world (TĀ 5.43-52).
signs_of_progress: the seven ānandas; the five signs (ānanda, udbhava, kampa, nidrā, ghūrṇi) of TĀ 5.101-111

name: Udakakarma (water-offerings for the dead)
method_summary: Relatives offer water (with sesame) to the deceased after the cremation and during the days of impurity; not done for infants under two (YS 3.1).

name: Uḍḍīyānabandha (the flying-up lock)
method_summary: Drawing the belly back (paścimatāna) above and below the navel, so that the breath, bound, 'flies up' in the suṣumnā like a great bird (HYP 3.55-59; GS 3.10-11; ŚS 4.48; DYŚ 129-130; GŚ 35 places it above the penis and below the navel). In breath-control it is applied at the end of retention and the beginning of exhalation (HYP 2.45); the Gheraṇḍa applies it at the end of inhalation in sagarbha retention (GS 5.50).
signs_of_progress: the lion to the elephant of death; even the old become young; practised six months it conquers death (HYP 3.57-59; DYŚ 129-130)
the best of locks; when firm, liberation comes naturally (HYP 3.60; GS 3.11)
the navel purified, the belly-fire blazes (ŚS 4.49-50)

warnings.text: It is to be received from the guru and practised in a solitary, settled place.

name: Meditation on the udgītha
method_summary: Venerate the syllable Om as the udgītha, the highest essence, and the udgītha as the breath in the mouth untouched by evil; what is done with knowledge, faith and the upaniṣad is more powerful (ChU 1.1-1.12; BAU 1.3).

name: Ujjāyī ('the victorious')
method_summary: With the mouth closed, the breath is drawn slowly through both nostrils so that it sounds from throat to heart, held, and released through the left nostril (HYP 2.51-53); in the Gheraṇḍa the breath is drawn in through the nostrils and held in the mouth with jālandhara, as far as one is able without strain (GS 5.70-73). It may be done walking or standing (HYP 2.53).
signs_of_progress: removes phlegm in the throat, increases the bodily fire, destroys disorders of the channels, dropsy and the tissues (HYP 2.52-53)
no phlegm disease, indigestion, āmavāta, consumption, cough, fever or spleen disease (GS 5.72-73)

warnings.text: As a lion, an elephant or a tiger is tamed only slowly, so the breath must be brought under control gradually; otherwise it kills the practitioner.
Proper breath-control destroys all disease; improper practice produces all disease — hiccup, asthma, cough and pains in the head, ears and eyes arise from the disturbed breath.
Draw the breath in slowly and release it slowly; do not hold it excessively nor release it quickly.
The breath is held 'as far as one is able, without opposition' (āśakti … avirodhataḥ).

name: Living by gleaning (uñchavṛtti)
method_summary: The ascetic livelihood of gleaning grain left in the fields, praised in the Mokṣadharma and in the mongoose's story, where the gleaner's gift of his last food outweighs a great sacrifice (MBh 14.92–93; 12.184.18; 12.340–353).

name: Entering the mind-less state (unmanī-bhāva)
method_summary: Thinking of no element, no above or below, being like wood, making the mind 'void of void', free of thought and motionless, until the jīva is dissolved and not roused by any sound.
signs_of_progress: insensibility to outer sound; freedom from decay (KJN 14.85–86)

name: Wandering alone like a madman
method_summary: Having closed the doors of the senses with the intellect, he wanders alone as if mad, taking discarded food; people call him mad and foolish. Kauṇḍinya: the madness is a feint to delude worldly examiners.

name: Upakosala's meditation (upakosala-vidyā)
method_summary: Venerate breath, joy (ka) and space (kha) as brahman, the fires as its forms, and the person seen in the eye as the self, the immortal, the fearless, brahman; the knower goes by the path of light and does not return.
notes: Upaniṣadic 'vidyā' (meditation-knowledge); the Brahma Sūtra (3.3) discusses which vidyās are to be combined.

name: Upanayana (initiation into Vedic study)
method_summary: The boy asks to become a student; the teacher takes his hand, invests him with girdle (of muñja grass for a brāhmaṇa), staff, deerskin and (later) sacred thread, and teaches him the Sāvitrī; he is now 'twice-born' with the Sāvitrī as mother and teacher as father. Due at eight, eleven or twelve years for the three classes (ŚB 11.5.4; ĀśGS 1.19–22; MDh 2.36–40; 2.169–171).

name: Ūrdhvapuṇḍra (vertical Vaiṣṇava mark)
method_summary: Vertical marks of gopīcandana clay applied with mantras at twelve places (householder) or fewer (students, forest-dwellers, ascetics; the paramahaṃsa one on the forehead) (Vāsudeva).

name: Wearing the upright mark (tirumaṇ)
method_summary: Daily application of the vertical white clay mark with the central line for Śrī on the forehead and body, a sign of belonging to the Lord.

name: The upright mark in gopīcandana
method_summary: Marking the forehead (and body) with the upright Vaiṣṇava mark in gopīcandana clay, praised as purifying and required for rites to bear fruit.

name: Uṣṭra-niṣadana (sitting like a camel)
method_summary: Named among the examples of posture in Vyāsa's bhāṣya on YS 2.46 ('posture is steady and comfortable'). The bhāṣya gives only the name; its form is explained by the commentators (Vācaspati Miśra, Vijñānabhikṣu and others), whose descriptions are not reproduced here.
notes: Name certain; form per commentators not recalled with confidence.

name: Uṣṭrāsana (the camel)
method_summary: Lying face down, the feet turned up behind and held with the hands, the mouth and belly firmly contracted (GS 2.41).
notes: The Gheraṇḍa's form is prone, unlike the modern kneeling posture of this name.

name: Utkaṭāsana (the squat on the toes)
method_summary: The ground supported by the toes, the heels raised, the anus set upon the heels (GS 2.27). It is the posture taken in water for basti (HYP 2.26; GS 1.46).

name: Yogic departure from the body (utkrānti)
method_summary: The Kubjikāmata's chapter 23 teaches the yogin's voluntary departure from the body at death. Restricted: title only.

name: Yogic departure from the body (utkrānti) — summary only
method_summary: RESTRICTED. The perfected yogin is said to be able to leave the body at will and merge in Brahman (DYŚ 115); the Haṭhatattvakaumudī has a chapter on a breath practice for it. No method is recorded.

name: Forced departure through the skull (utkrānti)
method_summary: A practice for leaving the body by driving the breath upward so that the skull splits and the jīva goes to the spotless; recorded only as the text's claim, without method.

warnings.text: Presented as a 'proof of liberation' for the adept; the texts keep such teachings secret from the untested.

name: Yogic departure at death
method_summary: The yogin, choosing the time of death, withdraws the mind, restrains the breaths and leaves the body through the crown, either for immediate liberation or for the gradual ascent (BhP 2.2.15-31). Summary only.

warnings.text: Addressed to the accomplished yati; the Vāyavīya asks how the practiser who dies before completing yoga avoids becoming a self-killer (ātmahā).

alt_method_summary: Lineage contribution (Upaniṣadic): at death one goes up through the channel to the crown and reaches immortality (KU 2.3.16; ChU 8.6.6); saying 'Om' one rises by the sun's rays (ChU 8.6.5); the person made of mind goes out through the indrayoni (TU 1.6); through the suṣumṇā joined with breath, Om and mind one goes upward (MaiU 6.21). Summary only.

name: Uttānakūrmāsana (the supine tortoise)
method_summary: From the bound kukkuṭa position the neck is clasped with the arms and one lies back like a tortoise on its back (HYP 1.24; GS 2.33).
prerequisites: kukkuṭāsana

name: Uttānamaṇḍūkāsana (the supine frog)
method_summary: From the frog posture, holding the head with the elbows and lying back like a frog (GS 2.35).
prerequisites: maṇḍūkāsana

name: Discussion for truth (vāda)
method_summary: Examining a question with a partner by thesis and counter-thesis, proving and refuting only with the means of knowledge and tarka, within accepted tenets, in the five-membered form, aiming at ascertainment rather than victory.
prerequisites: knowledge of the means of knowledge and of the members
signs_of_progress: ascertainment (nirṇaya)
cutting of doubts

name: Debate for determining the truth (vāda)
method_summary: Debate aimed only at ascertaining the truth, as between teacher and disciple, following the rules of the Kathālakṣaṇa; the maṭhas continue the practice in scholarly disputations.
notes: The maṭha disputations (e.g. during the Cāturmāsya) are recalled, not verified.

name: Cutting the flows (vāhaccheda)
method_summary: Arresting the left and right currents of breath at the heart, as taught by Kṣemarāja, by the silent utterance of vowelless sounds, so that the centre opens (Kṣemarāja's auto-commentary on Pratyabhijñāhṛdaya 18; summary, no method given here).

name: Rule-based devotional practice (vaidhī sādhana)
method_summary: Performing the limbs of devotion — hearing, chanting, worship, fasts, vows — because scripture commands them, under a guru, until spontaneous attraction arises.

name: Initiation of the medical student
method_summary: At an auspicious time the fasting, bathed, ochre-clad student brings the requisites; the teacher kindles the fire, offers to Brahmā, Agni, Dhanvantari, Prajāpati, the Aśvins, Indra and the sages, and before fire, brahmins and physicians instructs him in the vows (celibacy, truth, no meat, no weapons, obedience, service of all beings, never harming the sick); the student assents. Mantras not recorded.
prerequisites: examination of the student's qualities (Vi 8.8)

name: Dispassion (vairāgya)
method_summary: Turning away from objects by seeing the faults of acquiring, guarding, losing, attachment and harm (external dispassion), and seeing even pradhāna as like a dream or magic show (internal dispassion); with practice, a support of meditation.
signs_of_progress: calming of passion; freedom from expectation (like Piṅgalā, SS 4.11)

warnings.text: Through dispassion (alone) comes absorption into prakṛti, not liberation.
External contentment from abstaining from objects, without knowledge of the principles, does not liberate.

alt_method_summary: Cultivating freedom from thirst for objects seen and heard of in scripture, by seeing their faults through reflection (1.15, YBh 1.15); higher dispassion, from discernment of the puruṣa, is freedom from thirst for the guṇas (1.16); dispassion even toward the highest powers yields kaivalya (3.50).
Living without attachment to the world, knowing the body a bubble (Kaṭuveḷi 3), like a lotus leaf on water (Pattirakiriyār 54).

name: Observances for the unseen (Vaiśeṣika)
method_summary: Ablution, fasting, celibacy, residence in the teacher's household, forest-dwelling, sacrifice, giving, sprinkling, and observances regarding directions, lunar mansions, mantras and times — undertaken for the unseen result (adṛṣṭa).

warnings.text: Fasting is listed without further prescription; no durations are given in the sūtra (prolonged fasting is not described here).

name: Yoga: the mind abiding in the self (Vaiśeṣika)
method_summary: Withdrawing the mind from contact with the senses so that it abides in the self, where the embodied one has neither pleasure nor pain; through a particular conjunction of self and mind the yogin perceives the self.
signs_of_progress: absence of pleasure and pain while embodied
perception of the self

name: Vaiṣṇavī mudrā
method_summary: The inner target held while the gaze is outward and unblinking (Śāṇḍilya 1.31); in the Nādabindu, the seal held while listening to the inner sound in the right ear.

name: Meditation on the self common to all men (vaiśvānara-vidyā)
method_summary: Venerate the vaiśvānara self as the whole — sky as head, sun as eye, wind as breath, space as trunk, water as bladder, earth as feet — 'a span in size and beyond measure', not as any one of its parts; the first morsels of food are then offered into it as an agnihotra.

warnings.text: Each partial meditation is incomplete, and the king says each would have come to harm (losing head, sight, breath...) without the whole teaching (ChU 5.12-17).

notes: Upaniṣadic 'vidyā' (meditation-knowledge); the Brahma Sūtra (3.3) discusses which vidyās are to be combined.

name: Vājapeya
method_summary: A soma rite of 'the drink of strength', with a chariot race, granting pre-eminence.

checks.note: VS 9 opens with the vājapeya formulas ('deva savitaḥ prasuva yajñam …'), matching 'VS 9 (as usually located)'.

name: Virilization (vājīkaraṇa)
method_summary: The branch that restores potency and fertility for the continuity of lineage. Summary only: no formulations recorded.

warnings.text: Virilization applied to an unpurified body is fruitless.

prerequisites: purification of the body (AHS Utt 39.4 extends the dirty-cloth warning to it)

name: Vajrāsana (the thunderbolt seat)
method_summary: The thighs made firm like a thunderbolt and the feet placed by the sides of the anus (GS 2.12); it is the seat for khecarī in the Śivasaṃhitā (4.31) and for śakticālana in the Haṭhapradīpikā (3.114-115). HYP 1.37 records vajrāsana as another name for siddhāsana.
signs_of_progress: gives success to yogins (GS 2.12)

name: Making the body adamantine (vajrīkaraṇa)
method_summary: Bhairava's own practice by which he survived dissolution: meditation on the innate centre in the bone-circle and on nested lotuses flooded with milk-white nectar, so that the body stands 'like a thunderbolt'. Summary only.

warnings.text: 'This most secret teaching is to be guarded with effort.'

name: Vajrolī, amarolī and sahajolī
method_summary: RESTRICTED — summary only: practices for the retention and 'drawing back' of bindu (semen, and in women rajas) through upward contraction, which the texts say let even one living as he pleases, outside the yogic rules, succeed; amarolī is ascribed to the Kāpālikas of the Khaṇḍa school and sahajolī involves smearing with ash (HYP 3.83-103; DYŚ 137-145). The Dattātreyayogaśāstra places them in the haṭha of Kapila and his followers (DYŚ 29). No procedure, material or quantity is reproduced. The Gheraṇḍa's 'vajrolī' is a different, posture-like practice (see prc:vajroli-gheranda).

warnings.text: Most secret; not to be given to anyone, only to one as dear as one's own life.
It succeeds only for the meritorious, steadfast, seers of truth and the unenvious — not for the envious.
Death comes from the fall of bindu, life from holding it; semen and mind are to be guarded with effort.
At the start of practice women, fire and travel are to be avoided.
Union with women causes loss of bindu; the yogin should avoid their company.
When women desire the yogin at the beginning stage, union destroys his bindu, shortens life and weakens him — a great obstacle.

alt_method_summary: Named in the Yogatattva among haṭha practices concerned with retaining bindu; recorded by name only.

name: Vajrolī in the Gheraṇḍasaṃhitā (the arm-supported lift)
method_summary: Supporting the ground with both hands, both legs and the head are thrown up into the air; the sages call it vajrolī, for awakening the power and for long life (GS 3.45-48).
signs_of_progress: mastery of bindu; the cause of liberation; success even for one given to enjoyment (GS 3.46-48)
notes: A different practice from the Haṭhapradīpikā's vajrolī sharing only the name and the aim of mastering bindu; not restricted.

name: Vajrolī mudrā
method_summary: U21 contribution: a practice for drawing up and preserving bindu, in the context of which the Haṭhapradīpikā says death comes by the fall of bindu and life by its retention. Summary only.

warnings.text: A restricted practice concerning sexual fluids; only its purpose (retention of bindu) is recorded.

name: Worship of Vālai / Maṉōṉmaṇi at the root and on the Meru
method_summary: The Siddhars' Śākta worship: the goddess Vālai (Bālā), mother Maṉōṉmaṇi, is worshipped at the root centre with her three syllables and on the Meru of forty-three triangles (the Śrīcakra), with the syllables of Tripurā, Bhuvanā and Yāmaḷā, after the five initiations (Rāmatēvar; Caṭṭaimuṉi). Mantras and procedure not recorded.

equivalents.note: the Meru of 43 triangles is the Śrīcakra

prerequisites: initiation (tīṭcai)

warnings.text: Worship done 'by the deluded' becomes waste; the Meru needs initiation, 'a small child cannot touch it'.

name: Vāmakrama bhālabhāti (alternate-nostril form)
method_summary: Breathing in through iḍā and out through piṅgalā, then in through piṅgalā and out through iḍā, without force (GS 1.56-57).
signs_of_progress: removes phlegm disorders (GS 1.57)

warnings.text: One should not do it forcefully.

name: Vamana-dhauti (washing by vomiting)
method_summary: After a meal water is drunk to the throat, the gaze turned upward for a moment, and the water vomited (GS 1.39).
signs_of_progress: removes phlegm and bile (GS 1.39)
notes: Recent teaching calls a comparable practice kuñjala; that name is not in the Gheraṇḍa.

equivalents.note: Both empty the stomach upward; gajakaraṇī does it by raising apāna to the throat, vamana-dhauti after drinking water.

name: Obeisance and adoration (vandana)
method_summary: Bowing, prostrating and adoring the Lord with joined palms. Sixth of the Bhāgavata's nine forms. Tamil toḻutal: 'O my mind, worship his radiant feet and rise' (TVM 1.1.1); the Gītā's 'bow to me' (BhG 9.34).

equivalents.note: Pāśupata prostration as an offering to Rudra

notes: One of the Bhāgavata's nine forms of devotion (prc:navadha-bhakti, U07). Exemplar: Akrūra.

name: Recitation and veneration of the Vāṇī
method_summary: Reading and singing the saint's collected utterances (Dādū Vāṇī; Amritbāṇī of Ravidās) in the panth's seats and gatherings, the book itself being honoured.

name: Day-wise breath (vāra caram)
method_summary: The Tirumantiram's third tantra has sections on the breath flowing through the left or right nostril by weekday (vāra caram, vāra cūlam), read by the Siddhas; summary only.

equivalents.note: svara lore of the nostril breath

notes: Section titles checked in the local TM e-text; contents not summarized.

name: Worship of Vārāhī (Daṇḍinī)
method_summary: Worship of Vārāhī, Lalitā's general, with her own cakra and enclosures. Taught in section 7 of the Paraśurāma Kalpasūtra. (Summary; no mantras.)
prerequisites: initiation (dīkṣā) from a qualified guru into the relevant vidyā

name: The vārī: walking pilgrimage to Paṇḍharpūr
method_summary: Twice a year (above all for Āṣāḍhī ekādaśī, again for Kārtikī) Vārkarīs walk to Paṇḍharpūr in singing companies (diṇḍī) behind the palanquins bearing the sandals of Jñāneśvar from Āḷandī and Tukārām from Dehu, singing abhaṅgas and the name by day, holding kīrtan and bhajan at the halts, keeping the ekādaśī fast, bathing in the Candrabhāgā and taking darśan of Viṭṭhala (or of the temple's pinnacle when the crowds are too great). Those who keep it for life are Vārkarīs.
prerequisites: wearing the tuḷsī necklace (for Vārkarīs proper)
vegetarian diet and abstinence on the road
duration: about three weeks on foot for the Āṣāḍhī vārī from Āḷandī/Dehu; lifelong observance
signs_of_progress: the saints' company experienced as the tīrtha
longing for Paṇḍharpūr as for a mother's home

equivalents.note: a specific, recurring, congregational pilgrimage with its own inner meaning

name: Vārisāra (inner washing with water)
method_summary: Water is drunk slowly until the body is filled to the throat, moved through the belly and expelled downward (GS 1.17-19).
signs_of_progress: cleans the body; one who practises it with effort gains a divine body (GS 1.18-19)

warnings.text: Vārisāra is most secret.

notes: Later (recent) teaching calls a comparable practice śaṅkhaprakṣālana; that name is not in the Gheraṇḍa.

name: Vārkarī kīrtan
method_summary: A kīrtankār takes an abhaṅga as text and expounds it in song and speech, illustrated by the saints' lives, while a chorus with cymbals (ṭāḷ) and drum repeats the refrain and the name ('Jñānobā Tukārām', 'Rāma Kṛṣṇa Hari'); it ends with the name and the Pasāydān. Nāmdev is remembered as its founder.

name: Varṇa: the letters and resonance in the āṇava means
method_summary: Āṇava immersion through the 'letter' (varṇa) - the unstruck resonance and seed-syllables contemplated with the breath (TĀ 5).

name: Placing the letters and forms of Viṣṇu (nyāsa)
method_summary: Placing on one's body the fifty letters as the fifty forms of Viṣṇu (Aja, Ānanda, Indra ...) and the parts of the mantras, as part of worship.

equivalents.note: Dvaita's nyāsa places forms of Viṣṇu, not Śākta or Śaiva deities.

prerequisites: dīkṣā

name: Destruction of latent tendencies (vāsanā-kṣaya)
method_summary: Weakening impure tendencies (attachment, pride, the three vāsanās) by cultivating their opposites and pure tendencies, until even these are let go; practised with knowledge and dissolution of mind.

name: Weakening latent tendencies
method_summary: First replacing dark, object-bound tendencies with pure ones such as friendliness, then giving up all tendencies and even the desire for liberation.

name: Vāci yoga (the Siddhar breath-yoga)
method_summary: Summary only: the Siddhars' mastery of the breath, imaged as binding the 'horse of twelve feet' (TM 722), placing the prāṇa in vāci after initiation (Caṭṭaimuṉi 4), so that the body becomes firm and long-lived and the breath is turned inward towards the root and crown. No counts, ratios or retention times are recorded.

equivalents.note: vāci includes breath-restraint but is framed as body-perfection and inner turning

prerequisites: initiation (tīṭcai) and a guru
signs_of_progress: the texts claim an undecaying body and long life (TM 722)

warnings.text: Kāya-citti and vāci are joined to initiation (tīṭcai) and the guru; 'the Siddhars' worship' requires initiation.
For the true knower who has seen the true thing, kaṟpam and yoga are needless (the means are not the goal).

notes: Restricted as a retention-based practice; the texts' claims are recorded as claims.

name: Vastra-dhauti (washing with a cloth; vāso-dhauti)
method_summary: A moistened strip of fine cloth is slowly swallowed as the guru teaches and then drawn out again (HYP 2.24; GS 1.40). The measurements the texts give are not reproduced.
signs_of_progress: cough, asthma, spleen disorders, skin disease and the twenty diseases of phlegm vanish (HYP 2.25)
gulma, fever, spleen disorders, skin disease, phlegm and bile destroyed; health, strength and nourishment increase (GS 1.41)

warnings.text: One with excess fat or phlegm should first practise the six acts; others should not do them, their doṣas being in balance.
Some teachers hold that all impurities are dried up by breath-control alone and do not approve of the other acts.
The six acts, which purify the body, are to be kept secret.
Dhauti is done 'by the way the guru teaches'.

name: Vātasāra (inner washing with air)
method_summary: With the mouth shaped like a crow's beak (kākī) air is slowly drunk, moved in the belly and released slowly by the lower passage (GS 1.15-16).
signs_of_progress: cleans the body, destroys all diseases, increases the bodily fire (GS 1.16)

warnings.text: Vātasāra is most secret.

name: Vāyavī dhāraṇā (air-concentration)
method_summary: The breath held with the mind in the air-principle, like a heap of collyrium, smoky, with ya and Īśvara (GS 3.77); between the brows, 'whirling' (GŚ 72, 74). Durations are not reproduced.
signs_of_progress: gives the power of moving in the sky; destroys old age and death; one does not die by wind (GS 3.77-78)
notes: One of the five dhāraṇās counted among the Gheraṇḍa's twenty-five mudrās; see prc:element-dharanas.

name: Drinking the breath (vāyu-pāna)
method_summary: A group of practices in the Śivasaṃhitā for removing afflictions: drinking the breath with the tongue at the root of the palate; drinking cool air through the crow's-beak mouth; drinking with the tongue pressed at the cavity of the front teeth while contemplating kuṇḍalinī; drinking with the teeth pressed together and the tongue turned up (ŚS 3.68-83); the Gorakṣaśataka similarly has the yogin press the tongue-tip at the cavity of the front teeth and contemplate the goddess of nectar (GŚ 63-64).
signs_of_progress: destroys fatigue, burning, old age and disease; claims of conquering death, becoming a poet, becoming like Bhairava with the powers (ŚS 3.71-78; GŚ 64)
notes: Where these practices merge into khecarī (the tongue turned up into the cavity) the restrictions of prc:khecari-mudra apply.

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 1: Fullness at the two points where the breath arises
method_summary: The supreme [Goddess], whose nature is emission (visarga), sounds forth as prāṇa above and as jīva (the in-breath) below; by dwelling on and filling the two places where they arise, the state of fullness (bharitā sthiti) comes about.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 24 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering). Commentators identify the two places as the heart and the dvādaśānta (Kaumudī: 'utpattau dvādaśānte dvitīye hṛdi'). First dhāraṇā in Ānandabhaṭṭa's count as well.

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 10: The same method on a void, a wall or a worthy vessel
method_summary: By this very method, contemplation on anything whatever - on a void, on a wall, on an excellent person (pātra) - dissolves of itself and grants the boon.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 33 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 100: Neither attachment nor aversion
method_summary: One should not cultivate aversion anywhere, nor attachment anywhere; in the middle, free of attachment and aversion, Brahman spreads.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 126 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 101: The unknowable and the void as Bhairava
method_summary: What is unknowable, ungraspable, void, what lies in non-being - all that is to be contemplated as Bhairava; at its end, awakening arises.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 127 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 102: The mind in outer space
method_summary: Placing the mind in outer space - eternal, supportless, void, pervasive, free of limitation - one enters the spaceless.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 128 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 103: Letting go of each object the moment the mind goes to it
method_summary: Wherever the mind goes, abandoning that very thing at that very moment, by not letting it settle, one becomes waveless.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 129 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 104: Continuous utterance of the word 'Bhairava'
method_summary: 'He makes all resound through fear (bhayā ... ravayati), he gives all, he pervades the whole' - by continuously uttering the word 'Bhairava' [with this sense], one becomes Śiva.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 130 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 105: At the thought 'I' and 'mine'
method_summary: When notions such as 'I', 'this is mine' arise, the mind goes to the supportless; impelled by meditation on that, one becomes calm.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 131 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 106: Contemplating the words 'eternal', 'all-pervading', 'supportless'
method_summary: Meditating at every moment on the words 'eternal', 'all-pervading', 'supportless', 'pervasive', 'lord of all', according to their meaning, one attains one's aim.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 132 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 107: 'What reality has a magic show?'
method_summary: 'All this, without reality, stands like a magic show; what reality has a magic show?' - by firmness in this, one goes to peace.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 133 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering). Illusion imagery used as a contemplation; relevant to the Advaita/Śaiva dispute on the world.

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 108: The unchanging self: the world as void
method_summary: For the unchanging self, where is knowledge, where is action? External things depend on knowledge; therefore this world is void.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 134 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 109: 'No bondage, no liberation for me'
method_summary: 'For me there is no bondage, no liberation; these are bugbears for the frightened; this [world] is a reflection in the intellect, like the sun in waters.'
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 135 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering). The Kaumudī reads 'bālasyaitā vibhīṣikāḥ' (bugbears for a child).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 11: The mind within the skull, eyes closed
method_summary: Placing the mind within the skull and remaining with eyes closed, gradually, through the mind's steadiness, one discerns the highest object.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 34 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 110: Withdrawing from the senses into the self
method_summary: All contact with pleasure, pain and the like comes through the doors of the senses; so, abandoning the senses, one abides in oneself, established in one's own self.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 136 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 111: Knowledge and the known as one
method_summary: Knowledge reveals everything, and the self is the revealer through everything; because they have a single nature, knowledge and the known are to be contemplated as one.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 137 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 112: Dissolution of mind, awareness, power and self
method_summary: When the four - mind, awareness (cetanā), power (śakti) and self (ātman) - have dissolved, beloved, then there is Bhairava's form.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 138 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering). Kaumudī glosses: mind = manas, cetanā = intellect (buddhi), śakti = the breath-power, ātman = the limited individual.

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 12: The central channel like a lotus fibre
method_summary: The central channel (madhyanāḍī), situated in the middle, [is to be meditated on] in the form of a lotus fibre; by that goddess, meditated as inner space, the God shines forth.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 35 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 13: Closing the sense-doors: the bindu between the brows
method_summary: Blocking the eyes with the 'weapon' of the hands, piercing at the brows and closing the doors [of the senses]: when the point (bindu) is seen and gradually dissolves, in its midst is the supreme state.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 36 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering). Resembles the haṭha ṣaṇmukhī mudrā (see equivalents).

equivalents.note: Closing the sense-openings with the hands; the VBT adds the seen bindu

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 14: The bindu like a subtle spark, at the crest or in the heart
method_summary: For one who meditates on the point (bindu) - shaped like a subtle fiery mark arising from agitation within the light-abode (dhāma) - at the end of the crest (śikhānta) or in the heart, at the end of dissolution there is absorption.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 37 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 15: The unstruck sound (anāhata)
method_summary: One who is immersed in the Sound-Brahman - the unstruck (anāhata), unbroken sound, [heard] in the ear as a vessel, rushing like a river - attains the supreme Brahman.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 38 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering). 'pātrakarṇe' is read differently in the recensions.

equivalents.note: Absorption in the inner unstruck sound

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 16: Uttering Oṃ and resting in the void at its end
method_summary: By uttering the praṇava (Oṃ) and the like, and contemplating the void at the end of its prolonged (pluta) sound, one goes to voidness by the supreme void power, O Bhairavī.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 39 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering). Kaumudī: the sixteenth (ṣoḍaśī) dhāraṇā - agrees with this count.

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 17: The void before and after any sound
method_summary: One should contemplate the beginning and the end of any sound (varṇa) whatever; by the void [power] such a person becomes void, of the form of the void.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 40 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 18: The fading sounds of stringed instruments
method_summary: In the long, successive sounds of stringed and other instruments, one whose mind is on nothing else becomes, at the end of each, of the form of the supreme space.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 41 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 19: A seed-mantra dissolved into its subtle phases and the void
method_summary: Of any compound seed-mantra (piṇḍamantra), by [uttering] its gross letters in order and then, through the half-moon (ardhendu), the point (bindu), the resonance (nāda) and its end, by uttering the void, one becomes Śiva.

method_summary: When the breath, moving inward or outward, does not turn back from the two spaces [at its ends], thus, O Bhairavī, the form of Bhairava is revealed through Bhairavī.

method_summary: Whoever contemplates simultaneously the void 'behind/above' (pṛṣṭha) and the void at the root becomes void-minded through the power independent of the body (44). One should contemplate steadily the void above, the void at the root and the void in the heart; from this simultaneous freedom from thought, the thought-free state arises (45).

method_summary: Gazing at the clear sky with an unbroken gaze, becoming still, O Goddess, one at once attains the form of Bhairava (84). One should contemplate the whole sky as dissolved in the head, as Bhairava; then all of it enters the light-principle in the form of Bhairava (85).

method_summary: Bhairava is present everywhere as being, even in ordinary things; and there is nothing beyond it other than that - this is the non-dual way.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 124 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 99: Equality toward friend and foe
method_summary: Equal toward enemy and friend, equal in honour and dishonour - knowing [this] because Brahman is completely full, one becomes happy.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 125 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering).

name: Vedic study (vedādhyayana / svādhyāya)
method_summary: Learning one's own Vedic recension by recitation from a teacher, as enjoined by 'one's own Veda is to be studied'; in the Mīmāṃsā account it precedes, and makes possible, the inquiry into the meaning of Vedic sentences.
prerequisites: initiation into Vedic study (upanayana), per Dharmaśāstra

name: Vedic recitation (vedapāṭha, svādhyāya of the Saṃhitā)
method_summary: Learning and reciting one's śākhā's Saṃhitā orally from the teacher's mouth, phrase by phrase, with exact accents marked by hand movements, first in the continuous form, then word by word and in the interwoven recitations; daily recitation of the Veda is itself counted a sacrifice (brahmayajña). The Soma book says whoever studies the purifying verses eats purified food (RV 9.67.31).
prerequisites: upanayana (initiation) by a teacher of the śākhā
duration: years of daily study; the complete Saṃhitā with its modified recitations traditionally takes a decade or more (as reported; low confidence)
signs_of_progress: mastery of the Saṃhitā, then pada, krama and the vikṛtis
the six virtues of a reciter (sweetness, distinctness, word-division, accent, composure, tempo)

warnings.text: A mantra wrong in accent or letter does not convey its meaning; as a verbal thunderbolt it harms the sacrificer, as 'Indra-śatru' did through a fault of accent.
One who recites the Veda without understanding its meaning is a post bearing a load; what is repeated without understanding never blazes, like dry fuel without fire.
Studying without the hand-gestures, lacking accent and letters, one is 'burned' by the Ṛg, Yajus and Sāman.

name: Initiation by piercing (vedha-dīkṣā)
method_summary: The rarest initiation, in which the guru's power pierces the disciple's centres; given only to a rare, fit disciple (Kulārṇava 13.79; 14.66). Summary only.

warnings.text: It is not to be given to anyone at all; such a guru and such a disciple are both rare.

name: Breath-control with Oṃ, the utterances and the Gāyatrī
method_summary: Breath-control performed while mentally reciting the Gāyatrī with its 'head', preceded by the utterances and with Oṃ, as part of the twilight worship and as the renouncer's austerity; it burns away the faults of the senses (MDh 6.70–72; YS 1.23; VDh 10.5).
notes: No retention counts or durations are recorded here.

name: The Vedic recitations (pāṭha): continuous, word-by-word, step and the eight modified ones
method_summary: The pupil learns the text orally from the teacher in the continuous form (saṃhitā), word by word (pada), in overlapping pairs (krama) and in the elaborate 'modified' patterns (jaṭā, ghana and others), with exact accent and quantity, pronouncing each sound 'as a tigress carries her cubs' (PŚ 25) and avoiding the six faults of reciters (PŚ 32).

warnings.text: A mantra faulty in accent or sound harms the sacrificer (PŚ 52).
Reciting without understanding is 'dry fuel without fire' (Nirukta 1.18).

name: Not suppressing the natural urges
method_summary: Do not hold back the arisen urges of urine, faeces, semen, flatus, vomiting, sneezing, belching, yawning, hunger, thirst, tears, sleep and breath after exertion; nor force them.

warnings.text: All diseases arise from forcing or suppressing the urges.

name: Night rite in the great cremation ground (literary)
method_summary: Summary only: in Bāṇa's Harṣacarita the Śaiva adept Bhairavācārya performs a mantra-rite at night in the great cremation ground, guarded by the king and disciples.
notes: Named 'vetāla-sādhana' in scholarship; the text's details were not checked in this run.

name: Wearing sacred ash (vibhūti) and tripuṇḍra
method_summary: Applying ash consecrated with 'namaḥ śivāya' as three horizontal lines on the forehead and fifteen places of the body; one of the eight shields.

name: Inquiry (vicāra) as the Yoga Vāsiṣṭha teaches
method_summary: Reflecting, with scripture and the wise, on 'who am I? what is this world?', discriminating the Self from body, senses and mind until the seen is known not to exist apart from consciousness; Cūḍālā's daily self-questioning is the model.

equivalents.note: related to the later practice of self-inquiry (recent teachers); not asserted identical

name: Renunciation of the knower (vidvat-sannyāsa)
method_summary: Renunciation by one who has attained knowledge, as the natural expression and protection of liberation while living (the paramahaṃsa life).

name: Observance of the Vidyāpīṭha adept (vidyāvrata)
method_summary: The Vidyāpīṭha sādhaka, to master a goddess-mantra, lives in Kāpālika style — cremation ground, skull-bowl, offerings to yoginīs — for a fixed period. Recorded as summary only; no procedures.

warnings.text: Lakṣmīdhara (a Samaya critic) condemns the Kāpālika and left-hand tantras as deceiving and far from the Vedic path.

notes: Sexual and impure-substance rites of the Yāmala tantras are not described (restricted).

name: Vidyārambha (beginning of letters)
method_summary: Beginning the learning of the alphabet, a later addition to the lists.

name: Dissolution of thought-constructs (vikalpakṣaya)
method_summary: Letting thought-constructs subside by fixing awareness at the heart and not thinking of anything, one comes to rest in the thought-free centre (Kṣemarāja's auto-commentary on Pratyabhijñāhṛdaya 18; summary).

name: The eight modified recitations (vikṛti)
method_summary: Jaṭā, mālā, śikhā, rekhā, dhvaja, daṇḍa, ratha and ghana: permutations built on the krama that lock the order of every word of the text.
notes: List as traditionally given; the source ascription is low-confidence.

checks.note: List of eight confirmed (jaṭā, mālā, śikhā, rekhā/lekhā, dhvaja, daṇḍa, ratha, ghana — Vikṛtivallī 1.5); ascription to Vyāḍi confirmed.

name: Viparītakaraṇī (the inverting technique)
method_summary: Because the sun at the navel swallows the nectar that drips from the moon at the palate, causing old age, the body is inverted — 'navel above, palate below; sun above, moon below' — the head on the ground (with the hands supporting) and the legs raised (HYP 3.77-79; GS 3.33-35; ŚS 4.45; DYŚ 133-135; GŚ 55-59). It is begun for a moment and lengthened a little day by day (HYP 3.81-82; DYŚ 135). In the Gorakṣaśataka and Vivekamārtaṇḍa it is taught as pratyāhāra, the 'withdrawal' of the nectar from the sun.
signs_of_progress: after six months wrinkles and grey hair are not seen; one who practises for a watch conquers time (HYP 3.82; DYŚ 136)
the digestive fire grows (HYP 3.80)
one does not perish even at the dissolution (GS 3.36; ŚS 4.46)

warnings.text: It increases the digestive fire, so ample food must be provided; if food is scanty the fire burns the body at once.
The same: food must be plentiful, otherwise the fire burns.
Begin with a moment on the first day and increase a little each day.
It is to be learned from the guru's instruction, not from millions of treatises.
To be learned from the guru's mouth.
The practitioner must eat plenty, otherwise the fire quickly consumes the body.

alt_method_summary: Inverting the relation of sun (navel) and moon (palate) — navel above, palate below — so that the nectar is not consumed by the sun.
An inverted posture-seal named in the Yogatattva; the text warns that the practitioner must then eat sufficiently or the fire consumes the body.

name: The Virajā initiation (Śiva Gītā)
method_summary: An initiation with sacred ash and the Virajā mantras, taking the Pāśupata vow, before worship of Śiva.

name: Vīrāsana (the hero's seat)
method_summary: One foot set firmly on the other thigh and the other thigh on the other foot (HYP 1.21); in the Gheraṇḍa one foot on the thigh and the other turned back (GS 2.17).
notes: Listed in the Yoga-bhāṣya on YS 2.46. U10's paraphrase of that list omits vīrāsana; the unit recalls 'padmāsanaṃ vīrāsanaṃ bhadrāsanaṃ svastikaṃ …' — check the bhāṣya. Yoga Yājñavalkya ch. 3 is recalled (low confidence) to describe eight postures: svastika, gomukha, padma, vīra, siṃha, bhadra, mukta, mayūra.

name: Hospitality (viruntōmpal)
method_summary: Receiving and feeding guests as the purpose of the householder's life.

name: Concentration giving rise to subtle sense-perception (1.35)
method_summary: Concentrating on the tip of the nose, tip, middle and root of the tongue, or the palate, until divine smell, taste, touch, sound or form is perceived; such experiences bind the mind to steadiness and confirm what scripture and the teacher say (YBh 1.35).
signs_of_progress: awareness of divine smell, taste, form, touch or sound (YBh 1.35)

name: Viśeṣa-dīkṣā
method_summary: The 'special' initiation that qualifies the initiate for the regular worship of Śiva (content varies among manuals).

name: Worship of Viṣṇu according to the Tantrasārasaṅgraha and Yogadīpikā
method_summary: Daily and occasional worship of Viṣṇu (and his forms, especially Kṛṣṇa, Narasiṃha and Rāma) with mantras derived from the praṇava, placing of letters and forms on the body, purifications, invocation into the image and offerings, remembering that Hari in the worshipper and Hari in the image is the one Lord who accepts the worship.
prerequisites: dīkṣā

name: Recitation of the thousand names of Viṣṇu
method_summary: Reciting the thousand names of Viṣṇu taught by Bhīṣma, which frees from the bondage of saṃsāra and from fear (MBh 13.135).

name: Prenatal offering to Viṣṇu (viṣṇubali)
method_summary: A saṃskāra performed during pregnancy (the eighth month) dedicating the unborn child to Viṣṇu, on which the Vaikhānasa claim to be Vaiṣṇavas from the womb rests.

name: The sorrowless, luminous activity (1.36)
method_summary: Concentrating on the lotus of the heart until the luminous buddhi appears like the light of sun, moon, planets and gems; or absorbing the mind in I-am-ness until it is calm and endless like a waveless ocean (YBh 1.36).
signs_of_progress: luminous appearances; 'I am' alone (YBh 1.36)

name: Viśvajit (the rite of giving away all)
method_summary: A rite in which the sacrificer gives away all he owns; no fruit is stated, so heaven is understood (MS 4.3.15); what one is master of is given, but not the land, which is common to all (MS 6.7.1–3).

name: Mind on one free of passion (1.37)
method_summary: Letting the mind take as its support the mind of one free of passion (1.37, YBh 1.37).

name: Vivāha (marriage)
method_summary: The householder's sacrament, following regional and village custom (ĀśGS 1.7.1): the taking of the bride's hand, circling the fire, stepping on the stone, the seven steps, and establishing the domestic fire; eight forms of marriage are recognized (MDh 3.21).

name: Cultivating discriminative discernment (viveka-khyāti)
method_summary: Cultivating the cognition of the difference between sattva and puruṣa until it is unwavering, false knowledge burnt like a seed (2.26, YBh 2.26); the practice of the limbs makes knowledge shine up to it (2.28).
signs_of_progress: the sevenfold final insight (2.27); the mind bends toward kaivalya (4.26)

warnings.text: In its gaps other cognitions ('I am', 'mine') arise from impressions; they are removed like the afflictions.

name: Renunciation of the seeker (vividiṣā-sannyāsa)
method_summary: Formal renunciation of rites and possessions by one who desires knowledge, to devote oneself wholly to hearing and the rest.
prerequisites: dispassion

name: Resorting to solitude (vivikta-sthāna-sevana)
method_summary: Among the marks of the one who crosses māyā: resorting to a solitary place, uprooting worldly bonds, giving up acquiring and keeping (NBS 47); with giving up sense-objects and attachment, a means to devotion (NBS 35).

name: Circumambulation of Vraja (vraja-parikramā)
method_summary: Pilgrimage around the sites of Kṛṣṇa's play in Braj (Govardhana, Rādhākuṇḍa, the forests), done by Gauḍīyas and the Puṣṭimārga (whose ban-yātrā follows Vallabha's seats); residence in Vraja is one of the five potent limbs.

name: Vows (vrata)
method_summary: Observances for a lunar day or a period - fasting, vigil, worship, recitation and gifts - dedicated to a deity, with a story and a promised fruit.
notes: Prolonged fasts (e.g. month-long regimens) are restricted content and are not detailed here.

name: Vrātyastoma (rites for admitting Vrātyas)
method_summary: Soma rites by which groups living outside the sacrificial order are made fit to sacrifice (PB 17.1–4).

name: Vṛkṣāsana (the tree)
method_summary: Standing on the left leg with the right foot set at the root of the left thigh, like a tree (GS 2.36).

name: Vṛṣāsana (the bull seat)
method_summary: The anus set on the right ankle and the other foot, turned the other way, on the left side touching the ground (GS 2.38).

name: Release of a bull (vṛṣotsarga)
method_summary: On the eleventh day a consecrated bull is set free for the dead; without it the preta state becomes fixed.

name: Meditation on the vyāhṛtis
method_summary: Meditate on bhūḥ, bhuvaḥ, suvaḥ and mahaḥ as the worlds, lights, Vedas and breaths, mahaḥ being brahman, the self (TU 1.5-6).

name: Exercise (vyāyāma)
method_summary: Bodily exertion for steadiness and strength, done in measure — to half one's strength by the strong in the cold season and spring, less at other times — followed by gentle massage.

warnings.text: Excess causes fatigue, wasting, thirst, bleeding disorders, cough, fever and vomiting; one who overdoes exercise, talk, travel, sex or waking perishes like a lion dragging an elephant.
To be avoided by the vāta- and pitta-afflicted, children, the old and those with indigestion.

signs_of_progress: lightness, capacity for work, kindled fire, reduced fat, firm well-divided limbs

name: Vyutkrama bhālabhāti (water through the nose)
method_summary: Water is drawn in through the nostrils and expelled through the mouth, again and again (GS 1.58).
signs_of_progress: removes disorders of phlegm (GS 1.58)

name: Sacrifice and eating its remains (yajña, yajña-śiṣṭa)
method_summary: Summary as the text states it (no procedure is given): action done for the sake of sacrifice does not bind, so act for it free of attachment (3.9); by sacrifice nourish the gods, who nourish you in turn (3.10–11); offer to the gods what they give before enjoying it (3.12); eat the remains of sacrifice (3.13); keep the wheel of food, rain, sacrifice and action turning (3.14–16).
signs_of_progress: release from all faults (3.13)
the highest good through mutual nourishment (3.11)

warnings.text: One who enjoys what the gods give without offering to them is a thief.
Those who cook only for their own sake eat sin.
One who does not keep the wheel turning, delighting in the senses, lives in vain.
Sacrifice contrary to injunction, without distribution of food, mantras, priests' fees and faith is tāmasic.

alt_method_summary: Perform sacrifice according to injunction, without desire for fruit, with the resolve 'it ought to be done' (17.11), for the sake of which action does not bind (3.9); in the widened sense, the sacrifices of austerity, yoga, study, sense-restraint, breath and knowledge (4.25–33).
The principal enjoined act: offering a substance with reference to a deity named in the injunction or mantra, with its subsidiaries in fixed sequence; it produces the apūrva that yields the fruit.
notes: U05's contribution; Vedic ritual is covered by U01–U02.

name: Eating the remainder of the sacrifice
method_summary: The good eat what remains of the sacrifice and are freed from all faults, whereas those who cook for their own sake eat sin (3.13).

warnings.text: Those who cook only for their own sake eat sin (3.13).

name: The restraints (yama)
method_summary: Keeping non-harming, truthfulness, non-stealing, celibacy and non-possessiveness (2.30), without limitation of class, place, time or occasion — the great vow (2.31); non-harming is the root of all (YBh 2.30).
signs_of_progress: the fruits of 2.35–39

name: Meditation on whatever is agreeable (1.39)
method_summary: Meditating on whatever object one finds agreeable; the mind stable there becomes stable elsewhere too (1.39, YBh 1.39).
signs_of_progress: mastery from the smallest to the greatest (1.40)

name: Yathāsukha (as is comfortable)
method_summary: Named among the examples of posture in Vyāsa's bhāṣya on YS 2.46 ('posture is steady and comfortable'). The bhāṣya gives only the name; its form is explained by the commentators (Vācaspati Miśra, Vijñānabhikṣu and others), whose descriptions are not reproduced here.
notes: Name certain; form per commentators not recalled with confidence.

name: The practice-hut (maṭha, kuṭīra) and the place of practice
method_summary: The haṭha yogin lives and practises alone in a small hut with a small door and no windows or holes, neither too high nor too low, smeared with cow-dung, clean and free of creatures, walled, with water nearby, in a righteous, well-governed and prosperous land free of trouble (HYP 1.12-14; GS 5.5-7; DYŚ 49-54; ŚS 3.20, 3.35). Practice is not to be begun in a far country, a forest, a capital or a crowd (GS 5.3-4).

warnings.text: In a far country there is no trust, in a forest no food, in a crowd one is exposed — so begin yoga in none of them.

name: Yogāsana (the yoga seat)
method_summary: The feet, turned up, placed on the knees and the hands, turned up, on the seat, drawing in the breath and gazing at the nose-tip — a posture for yoga-practice (GS 2.44-45); also listed in the Triśikhibrāhmaṇa.

name: Worship of the circle of yoginīs (Kaula cakra rite)
method_summary: Kaula worship of the sixty-four yoginīs and the eight-by-eight circles in a secluded place with food, fish, meat and wine, with a Śakti partner; recorded only in summary.

warnings.text: To be given only to a devoted disciple tested (even for a year); kept secret from the deceitful, cruel and undevoted.
One fallen from the pledge (samaya) is a paśu; dualistic attitude in the rite is condemned.

name: Propitiation of yoginīs (yoginī-sādhana)
method_summary: Rites to win the favour of yoginīs for powers, set out in the Kaula and eastern digests (Tantrasāra, third pariccheda). Restricted: named only.

name: Yoni mudrā as a hand-gesture in Śākta worship
method_summary: A gesture of the hands forming the yoni, shown to the goddess after meditation in Śākta worship (named repeatedly in the Śāradātilaka's rites, e.g. with the śaṅkha, cakra and mahāmudrā); distinct from the haṭha yoni mudrā.
notes: The form of the gesture is not described here; its details were not verified.

name: Yoni mudrā (the womb seal)
method_summary: In the Gheraṇḍa: seated in siddhāsana, the ears, eyes, nostrils and mouth are closed with the fingers, prāṇa is drawn in by kākī and joined with apāna, the six centres are contemplated in order with the mantra 'huṃ haṃsa', the sleeping serpent-goddess is roused and led with the jīva to the supreme lotus, and one contemplates union with Śiva — 'I am Brahman' (GS 3.37-42); it is the means to laya-samādhi (GS 7.12-13). In the Śivasaṃhitā it is the contraction of the yoni between anus and genitals with meditation on the flame rising from the brahma-yoni (ŚS 4.1-11), perfected by mūlabandha (ŚS 4.42). The Haṭhapradīpikā mentions it as holding bindu (HYP 3.43).
signs_of_progress: one established in it even once is in samādhi (GS 3.42)
makes defective mantras effective (ŚS 4.6)

warnings.text: Yoni mudrā does not succeed without first practising śakticālana.
It is most secret; it is not to be given to anyone, not even with one's life in one's throat.

equivalents.note: The Gheraṇḍa's yoni mudrā includes the closing of the six openings that is elsewhere the whole of ṣaṇmukhī; the Śivasaṃhitā's yoni mudrā is a perineal contraction.

notes: The texts' claims that it removes even the great sins are arthavāda in their own manner.

name: Worship of the divine couple (yugala-upāsanā)
method_summary: Worship and meditation on Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa together — Rādhā on Kṛṣṇa's left, served by the sakhīs — in the Nimbārka school, with Braj songs of the couple's play (Yugalaśataka, Mahāvāṇī).
alt_method_summary: In the Rādhāvallabha and Haridāsī traditions the pair are worshipped together as inseparable, Rādhā supreme (Rādhāvallabha) or the natural pair in the grove (Haridāsī).
